title: Construction begins on Blue Point project
content:
Construction begins on Blue Point project
Project partners CF Industries, JERA, and Mitsui & Co. have broken ground on construction of Blue Point: a 1.4 million tons per year ammonia production facility fed with CCS-based hydrogen feedstock. The plant is located in Modeste, Louisiana, and is expected to begin low-carbon ammonia production in 2029.
Last June, Linde announced it would invest more than $400 million in a new on-site air-separation unit to supply oxygen and nitrogen to the plant. Topsoe’s SynCOR™ Ammonia production technology will be deployed at Blue Point. An autothermal reforming (ATR) ammonia production facility coupled with an onsite CO2 dehydration and compression unit, preparing emissions for transportation and eventual sequestration. CCS specialists 1PointFive and Enbridge will transport and sequester approximately 2.3 million tons of CO2 from Blue Point annually (~98% of the CO2 emissions generated in ammonia production) at its onshore Pelican Sequestration Hub in Louisiana. 1PointFive has already taken FID on the Pelican Hub, and the Class VI site is moving through the state-based approvals process. Electricity utility Entergy Louisiana will provide power for the site. CF Industries is investing an additional $550 million in scalable infrastructure (including product storage and loading) at the site, and will also be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the ammonia production facility. The site also includes room for future ammonia production expansion.
$3.7 billion has been invested by the Blue Point One joint venture members, with contributions allocated according to ownership levels. CF Industries holds 40% ownership, JERA 35% ownership, and Mitsui 25% ownership.
We are proud to break ground on the Blue Point One joint venture, a transformative project that brings together American energy resources, world-class engineering and partnerships, and trusted global allies. Most importantly, this facility will serve people, growing access to the reliable, domestic nitrogen supply American farmers need to feed the world, expanding our nation’s export capacity through shipping American-made energy to global markets and creating jobs in Louisiana.
CF Industries President and Chief Executive Officer Chris Bohn, in his organisation’s official press release, 26 Aug 2026
Today’s groundbreaking marks an important milestone for Blue Point One and brings us one step closer to establishing a reliable low-carbon ammonia value chain. At JERA, we believe that energy transition must be supported by practical projects and strong partnerships across the value chain. Blue Point One reflects this belief, bringing together partners with a shared commitment to build the foundation needed to scale lower-carbon ammonia for the future.
JERA Global Energy Solutions Chief Executive Officer, JERA Senior Managing Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer of Low Carbon Fuels Business Irtiza Sayyed, in CF Industries’ official press release, 26 Aug 2026
We are delighted to celebrate the groundbreaking of Blue Point One and sincerely thank our partners, the State of Louisiana, the local community, and all stakeholders whose support has made this milestone possible. Building on Mitsui’s long-term commitment to Louisiana, this project further strengthens the enduring partnership between the United States and Japan and advances a low-carbon ammonia value chain that contributes to supply chain resilience in the U.S., Japan, and beyond. We look forward to working closely with our partners to deliver this project safely and successfully, while contributing to the long-term prosperity of the region and its communities.
Mitsui & Co., Ltd President and Chief Executive Officer Kenichi Hori, in CF Industries’ official press release, 26 Aug 2026

title: Mitsui E&S commercializes marine ammonia engine
content:
Mitsui E&S commercializes marine ammonia engine
Two-stroke, dual-fuel engines and fuel supply systems now available to customers
Japan-based Mitsui E&S has completed the commercialization phase of its two-stroke, ammonia-fueled marine engines and ammonia fuel supply systems (AFSS), now able to serve customers with both products from its Tamano manufacturing base. Having now established a full “supply framework for marine propulsion systems”, Mitsui E&S is focused on the “practical implementation” of ammonia-fueled vessels.
Mitsui E&S has been pursuing a Japan-based engine manufacturing setup based on the Everllence B&W ME-LGIA model, with the technology licensed to Mitsui E&S by Denmark-based Everllence (formerly MAN ES). The initial prototypes of the “MITSUI-Everellence B&W 7S60ME-C10.5-LGIA-HPSCR” engine went through technical testing in Tamano in early 2025. This February, Mitsui E&S conducted tests of the integrated operation of the engine and the AFSS, witnessed by class society ClassNK. This recently-completed onshore testing has confirmed compliance of the integrated engine-AFSS setup with International Maritime Organization (IMO) NOX emissions limits: a key regulatory and environmental threshold for ammonia-fueled marine engines. Mitsui E&S plans to expand its capabilities to produce AFSS integrated systems compatible with WinGD’s ammonia-fueled X-DF-A engine, and Tamano may potentially be a future manufacturing site for a WinGD-licensed engine model.
On the vessel front, Mitsui E&S is part of two long-standing partnerships to deploy marine ammonia engines:
- Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Namura Shipbuilding and Mitsubishi Shipbuilding’s large-size ammonia-powered ammonia carrier (under development since 2021), will use an Everllence two-stroke engine built by Mitsui E&S.
- And (from Singapore Maritime Week 2024) K Line, ITOCHU, Nihon Shipyard, MAN Energy Solutions (MAN ES), and Mitsui E&S agreed to develop and build 200,000 dwt Newcastlemax-size bulk carriers at Nihon Shipyard, equipped with ammonia-fueled engines built by Mitsui E&S in Japan.
The development of the AFSS utilized funds from the “Integrated Project for the Development and Social Implementation of Ammonia-Fueled Ships” scheme administered by Japan’s New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO). Expansion of the AFSS for onshore testing will be in part funded by the “Project to Promote the Construction of Zero-Emission Ships,” a joint initiative of the Ministry of the Environment and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism.

title: 7 North American Battery Recycling Companies Scaling in 2026
content:
Battery Recycling
Battery News
These recyclers are adding capacity as new federal rules push end-of-life battery material toward domestic refining.
August 31, 2026
7 Slides
Start slideshow
Inside Redwood Materials' South Carolina facility
Redwood Materials
For most of the lithium-ion era, North America had very limited battery refining capacity. While facilities with shredders and sorting lines could turn used packs into black mass, almost all of that powder had to be sent to refiners in Asia. Because refining capacity lived overseas, recycling economics rose and fell with freight rates and cobalt prices instead of with battery demand at home.
Today, gigafactories in the US Battery Belt continuously generate manufacturing scrap, and the first large wave of EV packs sold in the late 2010s is starting to reach retirement. Together, those streams give recyclers a feedstock volume that finally justifies building hydrometallurgical refineries on this continent. Cell makers also need recycled nickel, cobalt, and lithium with documented domestic origin to qualify for federal incentives, which gives refined output a buyer before it leaves the plant.
Related:
DOE Announces Lithium-Ion Recycling Prize Winners
In 2026, policy has begun to shape around this trend. For example,
a presidential determination
gave the Commerce Department authority to restrict exports of black mass and other critical minerals, with the stated goal of keeping end-of-life battery material inside US borders. Weeks later, t
he Department of Energy named recycling and refining projects
in a $500 million grant round.
As the US embraced domestic refining, we've put together a list of seven battery recycling companies scaling up operations in North America. Read on to learn about their facilities, capacities, and the technologies behind them.

title: NeoVolta, SK On Sign $1B Battery Deal for U.S. Energy Storage
content:
Stationary Batteries
Battery News
Battery Manufacturing
Five-year, $1 billion-plus collaboration establishes end-to-end US supply chain for utility and commercial energy storage systems.
August 31, 2026
5 Min Read
SK Battery America's facility in Commerce, GA.
SK Battery America
At a Glance
$1.09 billion deal supplies 18 GWh of U.S.-made LFP cells from SK On's Georgia factory through 2031
NeoVolta Power targets 8 GWh annual BESS production capacity by 2028 for utility, commercial, and data center markets
All-domestic supply chain positions partnership to meet evolving OBBBA domestic content requirements
NeoVolta Inc. and South Korean battery giant SK On have announced a five-year strategic collaboration valued at approximately $1.09 billion that will supply 18 gigawatt-hours of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells for energy storage systems manufactured in Georgia, marking one of the largest domestic battery supply agreements since the passage of the “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” (OBBBA).
The deal, announced August 31 by both companies, establishes a two-phase partnership: an initial signed agreement for SK On to supply 9 GWh of U.S.-manufactured LFP cells to NeoVolta Power from 2027 through 2031, plus a framework for an additional 9 GWh arrangement under which NeoVolta Power will manufacture battery packs for purchase by SK On over the same period.
"This collaboration represents an important milestone in NeoVolta's expansion into large-scale energy storage and the continued buildout of our U.S. manufacturing platform," stated Ardes Johnson, Chief Executive Officer of NeoVolta, in the company's announcement.
Related:
Cummins Wins Its Largest BESS Contract for US Data Center Project
Ardes Johnson, CEO of NeoVolta. Credit: NeoVolta
Strategic timing: From residential roots to utility scale
The announcement represents a dramatic acceleration of a strategy Johnson outlined to Battery Technology just three months ago. In a
May 2026 interview
Battery Technology
, the CEO emphasized that NeoVolta's domestic manufacturing roadmap "predates the OBBBA," explaining that the company had "long planned to establish US-based manufacturing across the full storage spectrum — from residential systems through the often underserved commercial and industrial 'middle market,' and into utility-scale storage."
That vision is now materializing at commercial scale. The SK On partnership will supply pouch-type LFP cells produced at SK On's Georgia factory to NeoVolta Power's Pendergrass, Georgia facility, which manufactures battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and utility-scale applications. According to the company's announcement, the collaboration is expected to accelerate NeoVolta Power's expansion to a two-line manufacturing platform targeting up to 8 GWh of annual BESS production capacity by 2028.
NeoVolta’s NV Wave modular click-in residential ESS. Credit: NeoVolta
The deal validates Johnson's earlier assertion about building ecosystems, not just products. "What truly shortens deployment timelines is building the ecosystem around it," he told Battery Technology in May. "That means working with developers, community choice aggregators, utilities, and program operators that need reliable technology partners and a consistent supply of systems to scale their programs."
Related:
7 Residential Battery Storage Systems Worth Buying in 2026
SK On and ESS as EV hedge
For SK On, the NeoVolta partnership represents a strategic hedge against weakening electric vehicle demand. According to
, "the agreement comes as SK On expands into the energy storage system business to offset weaker demand for electric vehicles."
"This partnership strengthens SK On's position in the US BESS market and brings together SK On's U.S.-made LFP battery technology with NeoVolta Power's growing energy storage manufacturing capabilities," stated Daejin Choi, Head of ESS Business at SK On, in the joint announcement.
SK On had set a target of securing more than 20 GWh of global energy storage system orders this year and is in talks with several U.S. customers over additional supply contracts totaling more than 10 GWh, according to
. Competitors including LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI are also repurposing EV battery production lines for energy storage as U.S. EV subsidies phase out.
LFP chemistry as insulation from commodity volatility
NeoVolta's commitment to lithium iron phosphate chemistry—rather than nickel-manganese-cobalt formulations—provides strategic insulation from raw material price volatility, a consideration Johnson emphasized in our
May interview
Related:
Understanding Base Power’s role in energy storage solutions
"Our use of lithium iron phosphate chemistry helps avoid exposure to nickel and cobalt volatility, while our US assembly platform improves logistics, quality control, and alignment with domestic content incentives," Johnson explained. He added that the company is "preparing for where policy and market requirements are headed," noting that "as domestic content thresholds and FEOC [Foreign Entity of Concern] requirements increase over time, we anticipate the industry moving further upstream."
The all-domestic supply chain—SK On's Georgia-manufactured cells paired with NeoVolta Power's Georgia-based pack assembly—positions the collaboration to meet evolving domestic content requirements under OBBBA. As the release notes, "by pairing US-manufactured LFP cells with US-based BESS manufacturing, [NeoVolta] believes its platform is positioned to serve customers seeking reliable and domestic content BESS solutions."
The deal arrives as the energy storage industry undergoes fundamental repositioning. As Johnson told Battery Technology in May, "the industry conversation is shifting from simply pairing solar with storage to recognizing that storage itself is the primary grid asset, with solar as an optional generation source layered on top."
This philosophical shift—from viewing batteries as backup devices to treating them as dispatchable, revenue-generating grid infrastructure—underpins the commercial logic of multi-gigawatt-hour supply agreements. The target markets reflect this evolution: according to the press release, the partnership targets "utility, commercial, industrial, AI data-center markets." The inclusion of AI data centers is particularly notable, reflecting explosive growth in power-intensive computing infrastructure.
Production timeline and industry implications
NeoVolta Power's initial Pendergrass production line "remains on track to advance through commissioning and production-ramp activities," with cell deliveries and pack production scheduled to begin in 2027 and continue through 2031.
The NeoVolta-SK On collaboration represents one of the clearest examples to date of how OBBBA and related domestic content incentives are reshaping battery supply chains. Rather than importing finished products from Asia, the partnership establishes an end-to-end domestic value chain: Korean battery technology transferred to U.S. manufacturing, paired with U.S.-based system integration.
This model—foreign technology expertise combined with domestic production—may become a template for other international battery manufacturers seeking to serve the U.S. market while meeting increasingly stringent domestic content requirements.
For NeoVolta, the deal validates the strategic bet Johnson described in May: that focusing on "efficient product design with a growing domestic manufacturing footprint" would position the company as policy shifts toward domestic sourcing.
"We're not only planning for what the supply chain needs today," Johnson told
Battery Technology
. "We're preparing for where policy and market requirements are headed."
With 18 GWh of committed collaboration and a manufacturing platform designed to scale to 8 GWh of annual capacity, NeoVolta and SK On are now positioned to help define what that future looks like.

title: Nvidia Opens NVLink to Custom XPUs as AI Goes Heterogeneous
content:
Nvidia is opening its rack-scale AI infrastructure to custom accelerators from hyperscalers and other AI developers, expanding NVLink technology beyond Nvidia’s own processors. Through an expanded partnership with MediaTek, customers can design their own AI accelerators (XPUs) on a pre-validated NVLink Fusion platform and integrate them into Nvidia-connected AI factory infrastructure built around the Modular GPU Accelerated (MGX) ecosystem.
Nvidia also invested $3.5 billion in convertible bonds issued by MediaTek.
“Ultimately, this gives customers more freedom to innovate without having to rebuild the entire AI factory around custom silicon,” said Dion Harris, senior director of HPC and AI hyperscale infrastructure solutions at Nvidia, during a media Q&A on Monday.
Customer Chips and AI Factories
The announcement comes as hyperscalers develop their own processors for AI workloads. AWS has Trainium and Inferentia, Google has TPUs, and Microsoft has developed Maia accelerators. Nvidia’s strategy is to make that custom silicon interoperable with its rack-scale stack.
Related:
Data Center Hardware Highlights: August 2026
Nvidia says NVLink Fusion provides a pre-validated foundation for bringing custom XPUs into Nvidia-connected AI factories. The platform combines NVLink Fusion connectivity with NVLink-C2C, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), and chiplet technologies. Customers can use Nvidia intellectual property for elements of their systems while retaining control over their custom accelerator designs.
“Customers can focus on differentiated compute,” Harris said.
MGX, Nvidia’s modular server and rack reference architecture, underpins the rack-scale infrastructure around these processors. “We’ve built out this incredible ecosystem, which is what we call MGX, that now all these customers can tap into, and they don’t have to go and reinvent the wheel,” Harris said.
MediaTek’s Role
MediaTek will provide system-on-chip (SoC) design and packaging capabilities for custom XPU customers, while Nvidia provides connectivity and rack-scale infrastructure technologies.
“Production AI factories require packaging, HBM, I/O, and networking,” Harris said. Customers also have to qualify and certify rack-scale systems at data center scale.
The companies did not identify customers developing XPUs through their relationship with MediaTek or announce any specific data center deployments.
Heterogeneous AI
As AI infrastructure diversifies, analysts expect a broader mix of processors, especially as inference workloads grow.
“Heterogeneity is the future of AI,” said Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. That includes custom silicon from hyperscalers such as AWS and Google, as well as specialized accelerators from other vendors.
Related:
Data Center Hardware Highlights: July 2026
Those processors need high-speed,
scale-up connections
to communicate within large systems. “There are effectively three options,” Kimball said. “Scale-up Ethernet, NVLink Fusion, and UALink.” Ethernet is the established approach for data center networking; NVLink Fusion is Nvidia’s proprietary scale-up technology; UALink is an open standard being developed by a group of chip and infrastructure companies with AMD among its supporters.
“These fabrics are to make scale-up easier and more performant,” Kimball said. “[All] require broad ecosystem support to be meaningful.”
Building the NVLink Ecosystem
Nvidia announced NVLink Fusion in May 2025 and has since expanded the number of companies supporting the technology. According to Kimball, MediaTek joins companies such as Astera Labs, Marvell, Samsung, and AIchip in supporting
NVLink Fusion
for custom silicon, with Arm, Intel, Qualcomm, and SiFive having announced support on the CPU side.
Harris said Nvidia’s goal is to make the technology available to a broad range of customers: “This will be available to all of MediaTek’s custom XPU partners.”
Related:
Data Center Hardware Highlights: June 2026
Harris added that AWS plans to use a mix of its own processors and Nvidia infrastructure, including NVLink-C2C and NVLink switch technology.
The licensing model for NVLink Fusion has not been disclosed. “There will be some licensing elements in place,” Harris noted.
UALink Challenges NVLink
UALink provides an open-standard alternative to Nvidia’s proprietary interconnect technology. AMD is among the companies championing UALink and is incorporating it into its
Helios rack-scale AI platform
. Helios combines 72 AMD MI455X accelerators with Epyc processors and Pensando networking. In this model, UALink is used for scale-up connectivity, while Ethernet-based networking handles scale-out.
The competing approaches reflect a broader effort to connect increasing numbers of accelerators within AI systems.
Nvidia’s strategy is to make NVLink available beyond Nvidia GPUs. “Nvidia is an AI infrastructure company,” Harris said. “Customers need different architectures for different workloads.”
Beyond the Accelerator
Nvidia is expanding NVLink beyond GPU-to-GPU connectivity. Harris said NVLink-C2C can connect CPUs and GPUs at the chip level, while NVLink switch technology provides scale-up connectivity among processors. For scale-out networking, Nvidia employs Spectrum-X Ethernet and InfiniBand, positioning those as complementary parts of its networking stack.
When asked whether Nvidia’s longer-term objective is to control AI infrastructure architecture regardless of which accelerator is inside the rack, Harris said it’s not about ownership. “It’s really about being able to take all the technologies that we've built over the last several decades, and offering that to the ecosystem,” he said.
The MediaTek partnership also extends beyond data center infrastructure. The companies are continuing work on local AI computing, including future RTX Spark and DGX PC platforms, as well as automotive systems using MediaTek technology with Nvidia AI and graphics.
For data centers, the immediate expansion centers on NVLink Fusion and its support for custom accelerators from MediaTek’s customers.

title: Solid-State Transformers Power Next-Gen AI Data Centers
content:
The distribution outside most data centers still runs on alternating current (AC). Inside the newest GPU-heavy designs, however, high-voltage direct current (HVDC) is gaining ground. Moving key conversion stages
can shrink equipment footprints and weight, improve efficiency and control, and simplify the integration of solar and battery storage. That’s why solid-state transformers (SSTs) are emerging as a cornerstone of proposed HVDC architectures for
high-density AI facilities
“The move from AC to DC can be hastened by the introduction of solid-state transformers that act as a higher-voltage foundation,” said Shen Wang, partner at Fortune Virtue Capital and former practice lead for global data center infrastructure research at Omdia.
What Is a Solid-State Transformer?
An SST is a power electronics-based system that conditions and converts grid AC to DC. Unlike traditional low-frequency iron-core transformers, SSTs use high-frequency magnetics (with much smaller cores) combined with semiconductor switching stages. They can feed DC directly into a data center or convert back to AC if the site remains AC-native. Beyond being smaller and lighter, SSTs enable bidirectional power flow, easing the addition of onsite solar and battery energy storage. They can also clean and condition incoming power – filtering electrical noise and mitigating voltage and current oscillations – while tailoring voltage to different loads. Most designs maintain galvanic isolation through their high-frequency transformer stage and integrate sophisticated protection and control.
Related:
SLB’s $4.1B Kelvion Deal Expands AI Data Center Push
Why Silicon Carbide (SiC) Matters
Silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductors tolerate higher voltages and temperatures and switch faster than silicon devices, reducing losses at high power levels. In SST applications, this can translate into higher efficiency, compact form factors, and potentially shorter lead times compared with conventional large transformers, which can take multiple years to deliver.
Direct MV-to-800 V DC for AI Loads
SSTs typically connect to medium-voltage (MV) AC distribution (for example, 15 kV or 35 kV) and convert to an
800 V DC bus for
facility distribution. Many platforms are bidirectional, allowing import/export to support the grid. With
voltage transients
a growing concern in AI data centers, bidirectional functionality and fast dynamic response are increasingly design requirements. In many deployments, the 800 V DC bus is then
converted at the rack or sled level to 48 V
for server power rails, aligning with modern AI chassis power architectures.
Related:
Trump Targets Foreign Grid Equipment as Data Centers Expand
“Power delivery has become a performance bottleneck … fueling conversion to 800 V DC distribution, along with the chips (SiC) and control software finally catching up enough to make this kind of MV-to-DC conversion practical at scale and at the needed reliability,” said Waqas Arshad, vice president of product and technology, microgrid solutions, at Delta, a maker of SSTs and other power and thermal management systems.
According to Delta,
its SST platform
converts MV AC (6.6-35 kV) directly to 800 V DC at up to 98.5% efficiency. The platform was developed alongside the Open Compute Project (OCP) efforts and Nvidia’s 800 V DC specification and was
demoed at the OCP Summit 2025
. Delta reports dozens of units in Asia, with customer pilots underway in the US.
Who Should Adopt SSTs?
While SSTs remain in early deployment, many in the industry see them as essential to advancing AI – from raising rack power density to improving energy management and resilience.
Rick Sander, CEO of electrical infrastructure and SST supplier Alderbuck Energy, recommends SSTs for greenfield builds and AI retrofits. The company’s Nexus Power Unit is positioned as a software-defined platform that replaces multiple pieces of conventional gear – transformers, rectifiers, inverters – with direct MV-to-HVDC conversion, reducing footprint, installation time, and energy losses. Its PowerVectorAI software manages energy flows among utilities, batteries, renewables, and loads in real time, using AI to optimize performance and flag issues before failures. Alderbuck is
piloting its technology
at the San Diego Supercomputer Center at UC San Diego.
Related:
DOE Retreat on Transmission Corridors Tests the Case for Building Ahead
Sander noted, however, that if no GPU upgrades are planned, SSTs may not be necessary. He expects most new installations to use SSTs by 2028 and forecasts that by 2035, most data centers will rely exclusively on SSTs.
Alderbuck’s Nexus Power Unit. (Image: Alderbuck)
Risks, Tradeoffs, and Alternatives
Not everyone agrees on deploying a solid-state MV-to-DC backbone today. Clayton Gibbons, head of power systems at power-conversion system manufacturer SPOC Energy, argues that SST technology still lacks the maturity and supply-chain depth needed for a broad rollout. As an alternative path to 800 V DC, he advocates transformer-plus-rectifier approaches that he says can reach about 97.3% grid-to-rack efficiency while leveraging the existing MV transformer supply chain and providing intelligent, fast-response power electronics. This approach aims to provide operators with
the benefits of DC
today without committing to a wholly new electronics platform.
Hitachi Energy urges caution, as well. Operating at 34.5 kV while keeping designs compact introduces significant design and manufacturing challenges, said Vishak Gopinath, a Hitachi Energy spokesperson. Compact SSTs demand stringent insulation systems and high manufacturing quality to ensure a 20-year service life. Hitachi Energy continues to invest across SST building blocks – MV converters, transformer design and manufacturing, MV SiC semiconductors, and low-voltage converter products – for SST applications. In short, the technology is advancing but is not fully mature for every use case.
A Phased Path to 800 V DC Adoption
Traditional AC systems are not disappearing overnight. Wang expects phased steps – from AC-native designs to 400 V DC and then 800 V DC configurations – over the next year or two, with hyperscalers leading. In the near term, expect more HVDC prototypes and a handful of initial deployments to be announced and tested.
“Scaled SST deployments should become more common in 2027, particularly among
hyperscalers and cloud service providers,” Wang said.

title: Grenergy plans 516.9 MWp solar plant with 3.01 GWh BESS in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Solar Antofagasta has submitted the environmental impact declaration for the Parque Fotovoltaico Antofagasta 1 project to Chile’s Environmental Impact Assessment System (SEIA). The project, whose parent group is identified in the documentation as Grenergy Renovables, comprises a 516.92 MWp solar plant and a 430 MW/approximately 3,010 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS), equivalent to seven hours of storage. The project will be located in the María Elena municipality, Tocopilla province, in the Antofagasta region, covering a total area of 834.58 hectares. Permanent and temporary works will occupy 402.37 hectares, with the remainder left free of installations. The solar plant will comprise 820,512 modules rated at 630 W each. Electricity generated by the plant can be stored in the BESS for subsequent injection into Chile’s National Electricity System (SEN), shifting energy delivery toward periods of higher demand. For grid connection, the project includes the new Salitre step-up substation, rated at 33/220 kV, and a 20.7 km high-voltage transmission line. The line will comprise 59 structures – two line gantries and 57 lattice towers – and connect to the existing 220 kV Kimal substation, which is owned by a third party. The environmental impact declaration estimates investment of approximately $250 million for the solar plant, including the transmission line and substation, and a further $270 million for the BESS. This brings the investment described in the executive summary to about $520 million. The figure differs from the $593 million attributed to the project in reports published after its submission to SEIA; the attached document explicitly breaks down the two lower amounts. Construction is expected to take 20 months and require up to 400 workers, with an average workforce of 200. The documents schedule construction to begin in May 2028, subject to a favorable Environmental Qualification Resolution (RCA) and the required sectoral permits. Grid connection and commercial operation are scheduled for February 2030. The plant is expected to operate for 40 years, through February 2070, while decommissioning will take 18 months. Average staffing during operations is expected to be five people, rising to a maximum of nine during maintenance activities. The voluntary environmental commitments included in the filing include a coordination plan with the Tocopilla provincial fire department covering procedures for potential battery fires or explosions. The document also outlines specific measures for BESS fires, chemical explosions involving battery racks, and potential incidents during the transportation, installation, or storage of lithium batteries. title: Investments in co-located solar-plus-storage reach $25 billion in H1, says BloombergNEF - Energy Storage
content: Global investment in renewable energy reached $327.5 billion (€281 billion) in the first half of 2026, virtually unchanged from the previous six months but 21% below the record set in the second half of 2024. Data from BloombergNEF (BNEF) show that renewable energy deployment remains on track despite regulatory changes in key markets, including the United States and China. Investment, however, is increasingly shifting toward assets that offer greater flexibility in managing revenues. Storage drives hybrid projects Financing for standalone utility-scale solar fell more sharply than investment in onshore wind. Investment in standalone solar PV declined 20% year on year to $75.4 billion (€64.7 billion), its lowest level since the solar investment boom began in 2021. Growing revenue uncertainty, driven by solar price cannibalization, curtailment and grid congestion, is pushing investors and developers toward more flexible project configurations. Against this backdrop, co-located solar-plus-storage projects attracted a record $25 billion (€21.5 billion) in investment in the first half of 2026. The figure was nearly double the total recorded in the second half of 2025 and three times the amount invested in the first half of that year. The United States and Australia led investment in the segment. US accelerates ahead of incentive expiration The United States was the second-largest market for renewable energy investment, behind China but ahead of the European Union, recording 54% year-on-year growth. Developers accelerated project financing to meet tax credit deadlines and respond to surging electricity demand, driven in part by data centers. Solar investment rose 41% to a record $45.8 billion (€39.3 billion), while wind investment reached $13.8 billion, more than double the previous year’s figure. Projects that remain eligible for tax credits could sustain construction activity in the short term, with the final installations scheduled through 2030. BloombergNEF expects new renewable energy installations in 2026 to fall below 2025 levels, marking the first year-on-year decline in more than a decade. It expects growth to resume in 2027. title: EPA estimates vs. real-world data: EV drivers share some surprising experiences
content:
ev range
range anxiety
Jo Borrás
| Aug 31 2026 - 6:25 am PT
Electric cars are often marketed as having “x” miles of EPA-estimated range, but that doesn’t mean that’s how many miles you’ll be able to get out of yours. That’s the reality facing a growing number of Redditors who are sharing their EV commuting experiences online — and their real-world results might surprise you!
In a recent post to
r/electricvehicles
, a Redditor going by TallWall6378 shared that they weren’t seeing anything like their Ford E-Transit’s EPA-rated 116 miles of range per charge –
they were getting a lot more
“All summer I get 140 miles range in my 116 mile rated Ford E-transit due to my typical 40 mph windy road drive into town, with very little use of friction brakes,”
writes TallWall6378
. “And that’s with 1,800 pounds payload as my baseline (verified today on scales). So about 20% better than rated, but kind of an unusual vehicle.”
Van-tastic range
2024 E-Transit electric van; by Ford.
TallWall6378’s real-world range results are impressive – but they were quickly one-upped by another E-Transit owner going by
FlatDiscussion4649
. “I’m doing slightly better with the same vehicle @ 150 miles in summer (2.2 miles per Kw),” they wrote. “I always keep it in ‘eco’ mode and I try not to use more than 30% of the power available when accelerating. I drive about 60 miles per trip and at least 20 miles of that is at 60 mph, Probably another 20 miles at around 50 mph and the rest @ 30-40 mph.”
Other Redditors quickly piled on, sharing not only their anecdotal experiences but photos of their in-dash range guess-o-meters (GoMs) for additional back up and validation.
Range guess-o-meters
IndieMrToasty
That last GoM works out to about 5 miles of driving per kWh of battery capacity, and jifff’s description of their commute might sound pretty familiar to suburban parents. “Over 8km/kwh (5mi/kwh?),”
they write
, “my commute/suburb is mostly 30kmh zones with speed bumps and schools everywhere 😝”
Others piled on. “The EPA says my Kia does 240 miles on a charge,”
writes Traditional-Forum
. “In good weather I get 100 extra miles on a regular basis! Certainly some of it is driving style,
but it is widely reported that these early Kia EV’s are hyper efficient
My favorite personal EV range story, though, is the one shared by a user going by pimpbot666, who wrote about one of my personal favorites, the Volkswagen eGolf.
When my wife drives the ’19 eGolf to work, she comes back with some crazy numbers.
eGolf has 125 miles EPA rated range. We usually show around 135 miles on the guess-o-meter in moderate weather on a full charge after some average around town and a little freeway driving.
Her commute is 52 miles round trip, over a ridge that peaks 900 feet above sea level. The house is at 180 feet above sea level. This has a lot of stop and go traffic.
She leaves with 135 miles and comes home with …
110 miles on the guess-o-meter
. Average consumption shows up to 5.5mi/kWh when she commutes. Normally, we see around 4 to 4.5 miles/kWh.
The next day when we charge it back up to 100%, the guess-o-meter will show up to 155 miles, but drops fast in average driving.
PIMPBOT666
Taken altogether, these real-world snapshots prove that whether it’s an affordable VW eGolf or a late-model Lucid Air, EV drivers out in the real world are seeing range that’s meaningfully and measurably better than the EPA range estimates might suggest, underscoring the fact that those range estimates aren’t “ideal scenarios,” as many EV critics suggest, but rather exactly what it says on the tin:
estimates
What’s more, by the EPA’s own admission,
their range estimates are a bit conservative
. “The city and highway driving ranges determined from this testing are adjusted to account for real-world factors that are not represented on the laboratory test procedures,”
reads the EPA’s official explainer site
. “These factors include such things the impact of air conditioning, of cold temperatures, and of high speed and aggressive driving behavior. Although the regulations allow some optional approaches, the most common approach is to use a factor of
to adjust all the test parameters,
including range
. For example: An EV achieves 200 miles on the highway laboratory test.
Real-world highway driving range → 200 x 0.7 = 140 miles
to account for aggressive driving and HVAC use.”
What they’re getting at there is that (as ever) when it comes to efficiency,
it is often more important
you drive than
you drive
– and beating the EPA estimated range estimate isn’t just theoretically possible …
a lot of people are already doing it
How about you guys? Are your real-world range results better or worse than what the EPA thinks you’ll get, or are you making them look like chumps? Head on down to the comments and let us know.

title: I traded my electric motorcycle for a gasoline bike on vacation. It was pretty shocking
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Aug 31 2026 - 7:23 am PT
For the last few weeks, my wife and I have been hopping between islands in the Philippines, and like so many travelers (and locals), we’ve been getting around on small gasoline-powered motorbikes.
It’s a big change from our normal electric steeds back home, and an eye-opening reminder of just how stark the everyday differences truly are.
First of all, no matter what is powering it, a motorcycle or scooter is a fantastic way to travel, whether at home or especially abroad. In this case, these were a great way to travel through a new country.
You can explore tiny villages, pull over at hidden beaches, climb mountain roads, and stop wherever something catches your eye. You can park anywhere, squeeze past stopped traffic, and often take roads or routes that would disallow four-wheeled vehicles.
For many places around the world, motorcycles are simply the standard, normal transportation choice.
[Safety note: I always try to gear up for rides, but my wife caught me here while I was just moving the bike a short distance to the hostel parking area.]
But as much fun as I had on the trip, the experience also reminded me just how different small electric motorcycles can be compared to their fuel-burning cousins.
First of all, I’ll still give gasoline bikes one major win: fueling.
Need gas? It’s everywhere. Sure, there are regular gas stations, but what is even more convenient is how in these types of countries, there are so many little roadside convenience shops that seem to always have recycled liquor bottles filled with gasoline sitting out front. Running low wasn’t something I ever worried about. A couple of dollars later, you’re back on the road. I’ve seen this often in my travels around Asia, and I can’t deny how convenient it is.
That’s still an advantage electric motorcycles don’t universally have, especially in developing regions where charging infrastructure is limited. Sure, we can charge our electric motorbikes just about anywhere there’s an electrical outlet, which is theoretically a big win (there are way more electrical outlets than gas stations), but there aren’t necessarily electrical outlets
available
everywhere. So for a few more years, the distributed gasoline station and/or liquor bottles of gasoline infrastructure still has some advantages.
This nice fellow filled me up with 1.5 liters of Coca-Cola’s finest gasoline
After that, though, I found myself missing almost everything about riding electric.
The first thing I noticed was the vibration.
You don’t really appreciate how much a little single-cylinder engine buzzes until you’ve spent several hours on one. By the end of longer rides, I could still feel the tingling in my hands, arms, and bottom for several minutes after I stopped. The handlebars, the seat, even the foot pegs are constantly humming away beneath you. It’s not unbearable, but after spending years riding smooth electric motorcycles and scooters, it felt strangely primitive.
Then there’s the heat.
Small displacement motorcycles don’t produce huge amounts of power, but they certainly produce plenty of waste heat. Every time I pulled a bottle of water from the storage compartment under the seat, it was practically warm tea. That compartment shares a wall with the engine, turning it into a convenient little warming drawer. There might be an advantage there somewhere in the winter, but I didn’t find it.
This little Yamaha did me right, even if it can’t compete with my Gogoro
I also found myself constantly reminding my wife not to let her ankle drift too close to the exhaust pipe when getting on or off the back of the bike – not a concern I’ve ever had on my electrics.
The noise is another thing many people may gradually stop noticing – until you ride electric again.
These little engines spend much of their lives revving near the top of their RPM range, especially climbing hills or accelerating away from traffic lights. It’s not deafening, but it creates a constant soundtrack that becomes mentally fatiguing over the course of a full day in the saddle. With an electric motorcycle, the ride becomes quieter, making it easier to hear the environment around you, carry on conversations during brief stops, or simply enjoy the scenery.
At one point, I rode through a beautiful forest, but the engine noise certainly overwhelmed the natural wind and bird noises I’m used to hearing when riding on my electrics.
Then there are the little annoyances.
Waiting a few moments for the engine to warm up before setting off. The occasional whiff of gasoline when filling up. Hunting for neutral on the motorbikes and the slight jerkiness of low-speed clutch work in heavy traffic (not a concern on the scooters). Having to remember oil changes, air filters, spark plugs, and all the other routine maintenance that internal combustion engines quietly demand. Fortunately, I didn’t have to deal with any of those maintenance concerns since I was on rental bikes the entire time, but there’s nothing like a hundred moving parts underneath you to remind you that it’s
someone’s
headache, even if not yours.
None of these is a major problem individually. They’re all manageable and overcomable. But together, they remind you how much mechanical baggage we’ve simply accepted for over a century.
Electric motorcycles strip away nearly all of it. Twist the throttle and go. No vibrations, almost no noise, no scorching exhaust, no hot engine between your knees, and dramatically less maintenance. I’ll never forget the first time I showed my brother-in-law the controls on
my LiveWire S2 Del Mar motorcycle
(an 80 hp beast that does 0-60 MPH in 3.1 seconds), to which he remarked, “So it’s basically just a big e-bike?”
“Yeah,” I shrugged. “Basically.”
That’s really all there is to electric two-wheelers. Twist and go – no headaches. Compared to gasoline-powered bikes, e-motorcycles are easy like Sunday morning.
If everyone were going electric, we wouldn’t need those masks
Ironically, the Philippines may actually be one of the places that stands to benefit most from electric two-wheelers. The country already relies heavily on motorcycles for daily transportation. Trips are often relatively short. Air quality in many cities would improve (it was bad enough in Cebu City that my wife and I stopped at a local pharmacy to buy masks, though the smaller islands were much better). And while charging infrastructure still has a long way to go, electricity is ultimately easier to distribute than liquid fuel once the investment is made.
I’m not going to sit here and tell you that my vacation was ruined by riding gasoline motorcycles. Quite the opposite – I loved every minute of exploring the islands on two wheels. It was still a lot of fun, and it’s never a bad idea to practice shifting again to keep skills fresh in case you ever need them.
But every day I climbed back onto another buzzing, vibrating little engine, I found myself thinking the same thing: This is exactly the kind of riding that electric motorcycles were made for.

title: Kia confirms PV7 debut and previews the larger electric van for the first time [Video]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 31 2026 - 7:05 am PT
Kia is preparing to launch its second fully electric van following the PV5’s success. With its debut less than a month away,
offered a first look at the larger PV7.
When will the Kia PV7 make its debut?
The PV5 is already the
best-selling small electric van
in Europe, accounting for 37% of the market through the first half of the year.
In five countries, it accounts for more than 50% of C-segment EV van sales. Through August, Kia sold 39,000 PV5s globally. While Kia continues introducing new PV5 variants, it’s preparing to launch the second model from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) lineup.
We knew the PV7 would go on sale sometime in 2027, but Kia finally confirmed its official debut date.
Kia will unveil the electric van in full at IAA Transportation 2026 in Hanover, Germany, which runs from September 14 (press day) through September 20.
Ahead of its upcoming debut, Kia previewed the PV7 for the first time in a series of images and videos. While it’s still just a brief look, it’s pretty clear that the PV7 is noticeably longer than the PV5.
Kia PV7 preview (Source: Hyundai Motor Group)
Kia has yet to announce specific details, but we do know the PV7 will be based on the same modular E-GMP.S platform as the PV5.
The PV7 concept from CES 2024 measured 5,270 mm in length, 2,065 mm in width, and 2,120 mm in height, with a 3,390 mm wheelbase. That’s considerably bigger than the PV5 Passenger, measuring 4,695 mm in length, 1,895 mm in width, and 1,915 mm in height, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
The official teasers confirm previous prototype sightings. Leading up to its debut, the PV7 has been
spotted several times
testing in public.
A few weeks ago, it was captured on a car carrier in Korea. In the video from
HealerTV
(watch below), the PV7’s wheelbase is nearly the same size as the truck it’s sitting on.
Like the PV5, the PV7 is expected to feature Hyundai’s new Pleos Connect infotainment system and fleet management software.
Kia said the PV7 will deliver “a new mobility experience that caters to diverse customer needs, ranging from professional work environments to daily travel and leisure activities, by offering a spacious and flexible space.”

title: Rivian (RIVN) CFO steps down for GE Vernova amid critical R2 ramp
content:
Rivian R2
Fred Lambert
| Aug 31 2026 - 8:23 am PT
Rivian CFO Claire McDonough is stepping down effective October 30, leaving after nearly six years to become chief financial officer of energy giant GE Vernova.
The departure lands at the most important moment in Rivian’s history — the ramp of the R2, the $45,000-to-$58,000 SUV the entire company is betting on.
McDonough joined Rivian in January 2021 and steered the company through its $13.7 billion IPO in November 2021, still one of the largest US public offerings of the decade. She is relocating to the East Coast to be closer to family, and Rivian says the exit is “not the result of any disagreement.”
Derek Mulvey, Rivian’s VP of Finance, will take over as interim CFO on October 30. Mulvey joined Rivian in 2021 and previously worked at J.P. Morgan. The company says it is running a “comprehensive search” for a permanent CFO, evaluating both internal and external candidates, while McDonough stays on for a two-month transition.
McDonough’s tenure covers Rivian’s entire life as a public company. Beyond the IPO, she helped structure the $5.8 billion
Volkswagen Group joint venture
finalized in November 2024 — the deal that gave Rivian both a cash lifeline and a software-platform customer.
GE Vernova, the power-equipment spinoff, has become one of Wall Street’s favorite AI-and-grid plays, riding surging electricity demand from data centers. For a CFO, it’s a jump from a cash-burning EV startup to a profitable energy incumbent at the center of the AI boom.
Rivian’s stock tells the other side of the story. RIVN debuted at $78 in November 2021 and now trades near $17 — down more than 75% from its IPO price. Shares slipped on the CFO news.
Timing collides with the R2 ramp
The exit comes just as Rivian starts delivering the vehicle that has to work. R2
customer deliveries began in June
, and the company is now scaling production at its Normal, Illinois plant.
Rivian has spent 2026 shoring up its finances for exactly this moment. In July, it
launched a 75-million-share offering to raise roughly $1.5 billion
to fund the R2 push, and its
Q2 2026 earnings
showed revenue up 27% with gross margins improving — early signs the cost structure McDonough helped build is starting to pay off.
The R2 itself,
priced from $57,990 with a $45,000 RWD version coming later
, is aimed squarely at the Tesla Model Y — the best-selling SUV in the world and the vehicle Rivian must take volume from to reach profitability.
Electrek’s Take
Losing your CFO in the middle of a make-or-break product ramp is never ideal, but this reads more like a personal move than a red flag. For comparison, Tesla went through several CEO in a similar period.
McDonough guided Rivian through its IPO, the Volkswagen deal, and a genuinely brutal cash-burn period, and she’s leaving with the R2 finally shipping and margins finally turning the right direction. If you’re going to hand off, this is a defensible moment to do it.

title: Tesla confirms Autopilot/FSD was active in strange fatal crash
content:
Tesla told federal regulators that its driver-assist system was “verified engaged” when a Model 3 crashed at 104 mph and killed its driver in Clute, Texas — a detail that never appeared in any police statement or news report about the crash, which happened in May 2026.
The gap between Tesla’s own data and the public account of the crash is the latest example of how little the public learns about crashes involving the company’s Autopilot and “Full Self-Driving” systems.
What Tesla reported to NHTSA
The crash appears in Tesla’s own filings to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration under the Standing General Order (SGO), which requires automakers to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed, injured, or the vehicle was towed.
We found it while analyzing the full SGO dataset, which now contains nearly 4,000 Tesla driver-assist crashes.
In the report, Tesla lists the vehicle as a 2025 Model 3 driven by a consumer, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s a step beyond the “unknown” or “reported” labels that appear on many records — it means Tesla confirmed, through its own telematics, that Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was active. The report also shows Tesla had telematics data available for the crash.
Tesla logged the vehicle’s pre-crash speed at 104 mph, on a road it categorized as a “Street,” and recorded the outcome as a fatality.
Then it redacted almost everything that would explain how those facts fit together. The crash narrative, the specific software version, and even the field indicating whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area are all blacked out as “confidential business information” — the same redactions Tesla applies to 99.9% of its crash reports. Because the software-version field is hidden, the public file cannot even confirm whether the system engaged was Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving.”
What police and the media said
The public account of the same crash contains none of that.
The driver was Steven Alvarez, 23, an IT technician at Lake Jackson Intermediate School and a Brazoswood High School graduate, according to Brazosport ISD, which mourned him publicly. Local outlets reported that on the afternoon of May 20, 2026, his car left Brazoswood Drive, crashed through a fence at Clute Municipal Park, and hit the complex of a decommissioned, empty pool, where it caught fire.
Clute police said their preliminary belief was that Alvarez had suffered a medical episode. No outlet mentioned Autopilot, “Full Self-Driving,” or any Tesla driver-assist system. And crucially, no police statement or news report cited a speed — the only public hint that speed was a factor was a single description of a “speeding Tesla” on social media. The 104 mph figure exists only in Tesla’s telematics.
What could have happened — and why we can’t tell
Tesla’s data confirms one thing: the driver-assist system was on. It does not, on its own, tell us what role the system played. Several possibilities are consistent with the redacted record.
The system could have been actively driving in a way that contributed to the crash. But Autopilot and “Full Self-Driving” do not normally take a car to 104 mph on a residential street on their own, which points toward driver input.
Tesla’s speed figure could be wrong. SGO speed fields are self-reported and occasionally inconsistent, and 104 mph is extreme for the setting. It deserves independent verification against the police crash report and any physical evidence.
Or the police theory and Tesla’s data could both be right at once: Alvarez may have suffered a medical emergency and involuntarily pressed the accelerator while the system was engaged, pushing the car past any speed the software would command. That is close to what Tesla says happened in the fatal Katy, Texas crash, where it admits “Full Self-Driving” was on but blames the driver for flooring the accelerator to 73 mph.
The point is that the public cannot distinguish between these scenarios — and neither can investigators working only from the public file — because Tesla sealed the narrative, the software version, and the operating-area field.
Electrek’s Take
I want to be careful here, because a young man died and his family deserves accuracy, not a narrative. We do not know that Tesla’s driver-assist caused this crash. It’s entirely possible a medical emergency did, with the system a bystander.
Top comment by Rick Bungiro
It makes sense given Tesla’s overall “pay no attention to the man behind the curtain” strategy. One would think that if the software was running but played no significant role in the crash, Tesla would want to put all the data out there to prove it. But if they did, that naturally leads to the reasonable question of why they’re still hiding the details of other crashes.
Bottom line: Beware the person who claims to have invented a better mousetrap, but then makes it hard to figure out why it just killed the cat.
But that’s exactly the problem. Tesla holds the data that would answer the question, verified engagement, the telematics behind that 104 mph, the software version, the video, the driver-monitoring state, and it has chosen to black all of it out. The public was told this was likely a medical episode. Tesla’s own records say its automation was verified engaged in the crash. Both can’t be the whole story, and only Tesla can reconcile them.
This is the strongest argument for why the redactions have to end. When Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” is verified engaged in a fatal crash, “confidential business information” should not be allowed to bury what the car was doing. Tesla is already under NHTSA investigation over how it reports these crashes, and its own AI trainers have told Reuters they don’t trust its safety stats. A family in Clute is left with a police theory, while the company that sold the software sits on the data. That shouldn’t be Tesla’s call to make.
I strongly advocate that Tesla stop redacting crash data from NHTSA. We need to understand exactly how these automated systems are involved in crashes happening on public roads, especially as Tesla claims that it won’t require supervision soon.

title: AFRY wins Uniper FEED for NorthStarH2 e-methanol plant
content:
NorthStarH2 is planned to produce around 115,000 tonnes of e-methanol per year. The plant will combine green hydrogen produced through electrolysis, powered by 175 MW of renewable electricity, with biogenic CO₂ captured from Jämtkraft’s biomass-fired heat and power plant in Lugnvik, Sweden.
AFRY’s front-end engineering design (FEED) scope covers process design, plant engineering, operating philosophy, technical specifications, health, safety, and environment in design, and coordination with original equipment manufacturers supplying electrolysis, carbon capture, and methanol synthesis technologies. The FEED work is intended to advance NorthStarH2 from early project development toward a final investment decision.
The assignment started in late August 2026 and is expected to run until summer 2027. Uniper plans to make its final investment decision for NorthStarH2 in 2028, with commissioning currently scheduled for 2031. Uniper is developing NorthStarH2 through Sydkraft Hydrogen AB, in cooperation with Jämtkraft.
“E-methanol will play an increasingly important role in decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors such as transport and chemicals. AFRY is honored to support Uniper in transforming this vision into a technically robust and investment-ready project,” said Guy Skantze, Head of Chemicals and Biorefining at AFRY.
Broghan Helgeson, NorthStarH2’s project manager at Uniper, said: “NorthStarH2 is an important project in Uniper’s energy transition portfolio, and we are pleased that the FEED contract with AFRY is now in place. We look forward to continuing our successful collaboration and completing the FEED phase together.”

title: Ballard acquires GeoPura in £275m hydrogen deal | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
Founded in 2019, GeoPura designs, manufactures, and operates its Hydrogen Power Unit (HPU) systems, which use Ballard fuel cell modules to convert hydrogen into clean electricity for off-grid applications. The company also produces green hydrogen via electrolysis at dedicated production facilities and operates what it describes as the UK’s largest compressed hydrogen distribution fleet.
The combined business brings together GeoPura’s HPU platform, hydrogen fuel production, and logistics with Ballard’s fuel cell technology to create a turnkey Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS) offering. Ballard said the end-to-end capability strengthens its market presence across Europe and opens commercial opportunities in North America.
The transaction includes total upfront consideration of £275.0 million, comprising £82.5 million in cash, 49,584,212 newly issued Ballard common shares, and restricted share units to be settled in 12 months for an additional 1,084,540 common shares. Former GeoPura shareholders hold approximately 14.1% of Ballard’s outstanding common shares on a pro-forma basis. Ballard may pay up to £27.5 million in additional contingent consideration subject to specified post-closing financial milestones.
“Today marks a pivotal milestone in Ballard’s evolution as we officially welcome GeoPura to our organization,” said Marty Neese, Chief Executive Officer of Ballard. “By bringing GeoPura’s clean power generation platform together with Ballard’s fuel cell stack engineering under one roof, we provide our customers with a single, integrated source for reliable zero-emission power.”
Andrew Cunningham, who has assumed the role of President of Ballard, added: “Uniting with Ballard creates a stronger, more resilient partner for customers facing increasingly complex energy challenges. Together, we combine world-leading fuel cell technology with proven hydrogen power production and infrastructure expertise to deliver reliable, zero-emission energy where and when it’s needed.”

title: What The World's EV Capital Can Teach Us About Fast Charging
content:
Almost half the cars in Oslo are electric, and it keeps them charged with thousands of AC plugs placed where drivers already park.
Photo by:
Out of Spec Roaming (YouTube)
7:13am ET
Nearly half of Oslo’s passenger cars are electric, making it one of the world’s most electrified cities.
Around 78% of Oslo’s 4,519 public plugs are slower AC units installed where drivers already park.
Since 2020, many Oslo apartment residents have had the legal right to install a plug at their parking space and it shows.
Nearly half of all passenger vehicles on the road in Oslo, Norway’s capital, are electric. The city predictably has plenty of public fast chargers, but they aren't what keeps most of its EVs running. The city keeps them charged with thousands of simple AC plugs placed where drivers already park, and they make up the majority of its charging infrastructure.
Official data from
Statistics Norway
says Oslo had 4,519 public charging points at the end of 2025. Of those, around 78% (3,532) were chargers rated between 3.6 and 43 kW. Another 611 delivered 50 to 250 kW, and the remaining 376 were rated above 300 kW.
That means it has nearly 1,000 public plugs that can deliver at least 50 kW, providing essential coverage for taxis, commercial vehicles, road trips, and drivers who need a quick emergency top-up. But fast chargers aren’t doing all the heavy lifting, and this video from Out of Spec Roaming shows how Oslo’s slower, widespread network of AC chargers became the backbone of its EV transition.
The high number of AC chargers can be explained by how Oslo dealt with one of the hardest parts of owning an EV: apartment charging. Since 2020, many residents have had the right to install a plug at their parking space. The city also drops its public-charger parking fees at night, making overnight AC charging more attractive.
This turns charging into something drivers don’t really have to think about. The video shows that even a modest 6-kW plug can add 36 kWh during a six-hour stay, which is 100 miles or more of range in many EVs, while the owner is working, sleeping, or running errands. Drivers typically bring their own Type 2 cables, and untethered posts reduce cable theft and maintenance needs.
Basically, Oslo has made dedicated charging stops largely unnecessary. People drive to where they need to go, knowing they can likely plug in wherever they go, and carry on with their day.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Statistics Norway
counted 120,469 electric cars in Oslo at the end of 2025, out of 246,809 passenger cars overall. That works out to 48.8%, making Oslo unlike any other large city, and the share
will keep
since the vast majority of all new cars sold in Norway are now electric. Interestingly, it doesn't have Norway's highest EV share, as that goes to Bergen, where it's 49.7%.
Just under 96% of all new cars sold in Norway last year
were pure EVs
. The share rose to 97.6% in the first half of 2026. That transition to electric now extends far beyond private cars: the video shows electric taxis, work vans, box trucks and even a battery-powered semi using the same charging ecosystem.
The video notes that Oslo residents never stopped being car people. Many still rely on personal vehicles not just for local errands, but also for longer trips to countryside cabins and remote parts of Norway that public transit can't easily reach. They weren’t forced to give up their cars or radically change how they lived; Oslo simply made the electric alternative fit into their lives.

title: 博通推出 VMware AI 工厂，简化企业私有云 AI 部署
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，博通公司今天宣布推出 VMware AI 工厂。新产品是 VMware AI 私有云的软件定义基础，通过一系列自动化创新功能为 AI 基础设施部署提供支持，进而为客户提供更加简单的 AI 生产力部署路径。
据介绍，VMware AI 工厂可将 AI 应用直接部署到企业私有云环境。其 VCF（IT之家注：VMware Cloud Foundation）具备独特的基础设施自动化能力，可将服务器部署到 AI 模型开始服务，从数周缩短至数小时。
VCF 可在整个企业内部汇集 GPU 资源，使不同团队在共享硬件上运行多个模型，不必为每个 AI 单独配置服务器。统一模型库可为数据科学团队提供单一界面，在虚拟机、容器和 GPU 资源之间部署及管理模型推理和 RAG 工作流。
该平台还内置了可观测性功能，用于监控 Token 吞吐量、延迟，以及计算和内存利用率，帮助企业将 Token 利用率最大化。
VMware AI 工厂将支持思科、戴尔、联想、超微等厂商的 VCF AI ReadyNodes 认证产品，同时支持客户偏好的 AI 软件和加速器架构，兼容 Gemma 4、cotomi、Qwen 3.7-Max、GLM 5.2 等 AI 大模型。

title: 微信 2026 年 8 月朋友圈热度谣言公布，含“青岛大学新校徽像旭日旗”“新疆阿勒泰八月就能滑雪”等
content:
感谢IT之家网友
Autumn_Dream
8 月 31 日消息，“微信安全中心”公众号今日公布 2026 年 8 月朋友圈热度谣言，主要涉及台风期间各类涉灾谣言、虚假骑手补贴等内容。
IT之家附本月朋友圈热度谣言合集如下：
1、浙江台州餐饮停业、骑手补贴 200 元？
近期，网络流传“受台风‘白海豚’影响，8 月 8 日 18 时至 8 月 9 日 18 时，台州全市餐饮停业一天、外卖骑手统一休息并发放 200 元补贴，如有未发放，请拨打 12345 举报，举报属实可奖励 500–1000 元”等信息，引发部分市民关注。
经浙江省台州市有关部门核实，上述内容纯属谣言，台州市从未发布此类通知或安排。所谓“拨打 12345 举报奖励 500–1000 元”亦不属实，12345 为政务咨询投诉热线，未设置相关举报现金奖励。请广大市民不信谣、不传谣，共同维护清朗网络空间。（“台州网警”微博账号）
2、国家博物馆授权馆外扫码入群、采集个人信息？
近期，观众反映有社会人员以“国家博物馆工作人员”的名义从事引导公众扫码，收集获取手机号码、身份证号码等个人信息的活动。
对此，中国国家博物馆发布严正声明，国家博物馆从未授权任何机构、个人在馆外公共场所开展扫码入群、信息采集等活动，凡是以该馆名义进行的此类活动，均与该馆无任何关联。上述行为严重侵犯了该馆的合法权益，该馆将依法保留追究相关组织及个人法律责任的权利。
国家博物馆特别提醒公众，妥善保管个人信息，切勿轻易扫描来源不明的二维码。如发现有组织或个人以该馆名义进行非法活动，请及时向相关执法部门举报。（“国博君”微信公众号）
3、安徽蚌埠普通高中后补录取 65 名学生？
近期，一份题为《安徽省教育厅关于公布蚌埠市普通高中录取后补名单公示的通知》（皖中招 [2026]61 号）的纸质复印件在网上流传，“通知”声称有 65 名学生通过后补方式获得普通高中录取资格，引发关注。
经核实，安徽省教育厅从未印发“皖中招 [2026]61 号”文件，文件印章、文号、发文内容均为仿造，蚌埠市也未收到该份所谓“后补录取通知”。蚌埠普通高中录取、征集志愿严格按照省市中招招生政策执行。（安徽网络辟谣平台）
4、上海浦东一女子在台风中坠楼？
近期，网上流传“浦东一女子在台风中坠楼”的消息，引发关注。
经属地公安部门调查，该信息系网民高某某（男，60 岁）为博取流量，运用 AI 软件生成涉台风相关视频，编造以上虚假信息并发布，造成不良社会影响。目前，高某某已被依法处以行政拘留。（“警民直通车-浦东”微博账号）
5、“青岛大学新校徽像旭日旗”？
有网民发布视频称，“青岛大学新校徽被指像旭日旗，校方紧急撤下”，引发关注。
经查，网传校徽图样并非青岛大学校徽，青岛大学现校徽为 2013 年 5 月启用，以蓝色为主基调，由中英文校名和建校年份等三个基本元素组成，交替出现的四部分色块寓意学校主体由四所学校合并而成。青岛大学表示，该校自 1909 年建校起均未使用过网传视频中的校徽，近期也没有组织过新校徽设计、征集、发布等工作，网传所谓新校徽图片纯属造谣。
该不实信息系违法行为人龙某为博取流量利用 AI 技术编造，并在网络平台发布，扰乱公共秩序。目前，龙某已被公安机关依法行政拘留并处罚款。（青岛互联网联合辟谣平台、“崂山公安”微信公众号）
6、湖北鄂州一快递员被罚款 100 元后结束生命？
近期，有网民发布信息称湖北鄂州“葛店一快递员因工作罚款 100 元等问题结束生命”，引发关注。
经当地网信、公安部门联合核实，该消息为编造的虚假信息，当地未接到相关警情和报警。目前，网信部门对发帖人尹某进行批评教育并责令删除不实帖文。（“湖北网络辟谣”、“这里是鄂州”微信公众号）
7、“没打 HPV 疫苗不能入学”？
近期，部分网络平台和社交群组中出现“入学要查 HPV 疫苗，未接种者可能影响入学”的说法，引发关注。
国家疾控局明确回应：HPV 疫苗接种情况已纳入部分地区入学查验范围，但是否完成接种不是入学门槛，不会影响孩子入学。
2025 年 10 月，国家疾控局等七部门印发通知，将 HPV 疫苗纳入国家免疫规划，为 2011 年 11 月 10 日后出生的满 13 周岁女孩免费接种 2 剂次双价 HPV 疫苗。“纳入查验”不等于“强制接种”，查验旨在核实接种情况、提醒补种，查的是接种记录，而不是卡入学资格。是否接种由家长知情、自愿决定。国家疾控局明确：HPV 疫苗免费接种遵循自愿原则。（“全国教育辟谣”微信公众号、国家疾病预防控制局）
8、“安徽霍山磨子潭水库泄洪死了不少人”？
近期，有网民浏览台风期间磨子潭水库泄洪视频后，在评论区留言“泄洪洞那里听说死了不少人”，引发关注。
经霍山警方调查，该信息不实。安徽六安霍山县衡山镇网民袁某未经核实，故意虚构不实信息，扰乱正常公共秩序，在台风期间易引发居民恐慌，造成不良社会影响。目前，公安机关依法对袁某予以行政处罚。（安徽网络辟谣平台）
9、新疆阿勒泰八月就能滑雪？
近期，有自媒体发布短视频称“8 月 3 日新疆将军山现已开放滑雪，新雪季正式运营”，引发关注。
经核查，网传信息不实。当前，位于新疆阿勒泰的将军山国际滑雪度假区处于夏季运维阶段，平均气温达到零上 20 摄氏度，雪道封闭管控、造雪设备未启动。现阶段仅开放夏季文旅业态，可乘坐缆车观光、观景休闲，暂不具备滑雪运营条件，不存在对外开放滑雪的情况。（“新疆网络辟谣”、“金山网信”微信公众号）
10、浙江温州一建筑被台风吹塌了？
近期，浙江温州一网民在抖音平台发布视频称，“‘白海豚’还没来，楼已塌？”，引发关注。
经温州辟谣侠向属地瓯海区泽雅镇核实情况。经工作人员核实确认，该建筑是位于瓯海泽雅镇的中国寓言文化村板块“融空间”，建筑外观是特意设计的艺术造型，并非发生坍塌。
该网民为博取热度吸引流量，在抖音平台借即将登陆的台风“白海豚”制造瓯海文化新地标建筑被台风提前吹塌的虚假错觉，造成不良社会影响。瓯海网信办已对该网民进行教育训诫。（“温州辟谣”微信公众号）
IT之家注：面对纷杂的网络环境，请保持审慎，切勿跟风转发真假不明的信息。

title: 整治 AI 虚假账号，Instagram 推出全新 AI 个人资料标签
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，社交媒体 Instagram 今天宣布将原本的“AI 创作者”标签更新为“AI 生成个人资料”，使用户能够一眼分辨出眼前的创作者究竟是真人，还是 AI 生成的虚假人物。
IT之家了解到，该标签适用于高度拟真且从未主动披露虚拟身份的 AI 生成账号。真实创作者使用 AI 编辑工具处理照片、撰写标题，不会受到影响。
Instagram 表示，用户已经对一些看似真人、实际上是 AI 虚构的账号感到厌倦。今后如果有创作者不主动披露 AI 虚构身份，平台算法将不再将其内容推荐至 Reels、Explore 页面的非粉丝用户。如果平台自动标记算法出现偏差，用户可以联系官方客服申诉。

title: 比亚迪方程豹熊甜波：方程 S 和方程 S GT 将在 9 月上市
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，比亚迪集团-方程豹事业部总经理熊甜波今日透露，方程 S 和方程 S GT 将在 9 月上市。
据IT之家此前报道，8 月 20 日，两款新车开启全国预订，预订价格区间 23～28 万元。
在 2026 成都车展上，比亚迪方程豹全新轿跑车型方程 S 和方程 S GT 两款新车完成实车全球首秀。
工信部申报信息显示，方程 S 长宽高分别为 5060×1967×1483/1458mm，轴距 2960mm，整备质量 2140kg，总质量 2580kg，最高车速达到 240km/h。该车搭载一台峰值功率 245kW 或 300kW 的单电机，还有 190/300kW 的双电机可选，匹配磷酸铁锂电池。
方程 S GT 长宽高分别为 5025/5095×1967×1483/1458mm，轴距 2960mm，整备质量 2170kg，总质量 2595kg，最高车速达到 240km/h。该车搭载一台峰值功率 300kW 的单电机，或 190/300kW 双电机，匹配磷酸铁锂电池。
据介绍，方程 S 系列首发搭载比亚迪智慧生态 2.0，全车配备 PIN 口、磁吸及螺纹接口，实现座舱可定制、可进化、可成长。

title: 消息称长鑫存储开始试产 HBM3E 内存，有望数周内大规模量产
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，据《The Information》今日报道，长鑫存储已启动 HBM3E 内存的风险试产工作。
据报道，长鑫存储当前计划扩大产能。预计到今年年底，该公司的 DRAM 制造能力将达到每月 35 万片晶圆，未来几年的产能还将继续提高。目前长鑫的 HBM3E 生产规模依然十分有限，这意味着他们刚刚进入风险试产阶段。
虽然我们还不清楚长鑫存储 HBM3E 的具体规格。但根据 JEDEC（IT之家注：固态技术协会）规范，HBM3E 应采用 1024-bit 位宽，单引脚速率介于 9.2Gbps 至 12.4Gbps 之间，大多数标准配置的目标速率为 9.6Gbps。
在 9.6Gbps 的典型配置下，HBM3E 的总带宽可达 1.2TB/s。在采用 8 层堆叠（8-Hi）、单层 24Gb DRAM 芯片的情况下，其单个堆栈容量为 24GB；采用 12 层堆叠时，容量可达 36GB。
考虑到长鑫存储此前已具备从风险试产快速过渡到大规模量产的能力，因此其 HBM3E 有可能在数周内进入大规模量产阶段。
此外，长鑫存储在晶圆厂洁净室建设速度方面拥有明显优势。其建设一座晶圆厂洁净室仅需 12 个月，其他厂商通常需要两年。

title: 火星地下存在巨大“热异常”：南半球内部温度比北半球高 400℃
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，一项针对火星内部结构的新研究再次表明，这颗红色星球实际上是一个由两个截然不同“半球”组成的世界。
研究发现，在火星南半球深处，其内部温度可能比北半球地下高出最高 750 华氏度（约 400 摄氏度），进一步加深了人们对火星奇特南北二分现象的疑问：为什么北部是一片相对平坦的低地，而南部却分布着崎岖的高原？
“科学家通常假设，行星天体的内部结构总体上具有球对称性，但事实并不一定如此。”论文第一作者、曾任职于加州理工学院、现就职于亚利桑那大学的亚历山大 · 伯恩在一份声明中表示。
伯恩及其团队重新分析了美国宇航局三艘火星探测器的历史数据，包括“火星全球勘测者号”、“火星奥德赛号”和“火星勘测轨道飞行器”。研究人员通过寻找这些探测器轨道速度的细微变化，分析火星引力场可能存在的差异。
研究团队采用了伯恩开发的一种名为“潮汐层析成像”的技术。该方法还考虑了火星沿椭圆轨道绕太阳运行时，太阳引力对火星产生的不断变化的影响。借助这一技术，研究人员得以推测火星内部的结构和温度分布。
研究发现，各探测器所经历的火星引力场随时间发生的变化，与火星内部完全呈球对称结构时的理论预期存在明显差异。
为解释这种差异，研究人员认为，火星南半球下方的地幔温度必须比北半球高出约 390 至 750 华氏度（约 200 至 400 摄氏度）。南半球地幔的温度甚至可能高到部分区域至今仍处于熔融状态。
这一发现可能会影响科学家对火星宜居性以及火星火山活动持续时间的理解。
事实上，火星南北内部存在差异或许并不令人意外，因为科学家早已知道，这颗星球的表面本身就高度不对称。
火星北部主要由广阔的低地平原组成，而南部则覆盖着大量陨石坑高地。平均来看，火星南部的地壳比北部厚约 15.5 英里（25 公里）。科学家还认为，北部低地在远古时期可能曾经存在过一片巨大的海洋。
论文第二作者、加州理工学院的阿米尔侯赛因 · 巴盖里表示：“理解火星南北之间的这种二分现象非常重要，因为它能够帮助我们了解影响火星水文环境的各种过程，包括那些可能形成并曾经储存液态水的盆地。”
更高温的南半球地幔，也可能解释火星上其他一些令人困惑的发现。
美国宇航局的“洞察号”火星着陆器于 2022 年 12 月结束任务，其搭载的地震仪曾发现，地震波在火星南部衰减得更快，而较高的地下温度可以解释这一现象。
此外，火星南部富含铁矿物中发现的磁异常，如今也有了新的解释方向。
如今的火星已经没有全球性磁场，但在 40 多亿年前，这颗星球曾拥有全球磁场。如果来自更高温南部地幔的上涌物质加热地壳，使其温度超过所谓的“居里温度”，那么材料就会失去自身固有的磁性，其内部残留磁化状态也会发生变化。
这一过程可能正是火星南部富铁矿物中那些神秘磁性残留形成的原因之一。
伯恩表示：“了解行星天体的内部结构，有助于我们揭示塑造它们形成和演化过程的机制。”
不过，火星南北差异的真正起源仍然没有答案。科学家甚至还无法确定，火星表面的南北差异是否与内部结构的差异由同一种机制造成。
目前最受关注的一种解释认为，这一切可能源于 40 多亿年前的一次巨大撞击。
按照这一理论，火星北部低地实际上是一个规模极其庞大的撞击盆地。那次撞击在火星北部挖出了一个巨大的凹陷，同时释放了大量内部热量，使北半球地幔的冷却速度快于南半球。
另一种可能是，火星南部较厚的地壳形成了一层高效的“盖子”，阻止地幔内部的大量热量向外散失。
这一假设实际上可以通过未来的观测进行验证。如果岩浆从地下向上涌动时遇到厚重且致密的南部地壳，其上升过程可能会受到阻碍，并在地表下形成熔融岩浆侵入体。未来更高分辨率的火星重力数据，或许能够帮助科学家寻找这些地下结构。
这些问题仍有待未来的火星探测任务进一步解答。不过，研究人员开发的“潮汐层析成像”技术也可以应用于其他天体，从水星到木星的大型卫星，都可能成为研究对象。
伯恩表示：“随着我们获得更多的重力数据，我们将能够确定行星内部结构更加复杂的三维细节。这些推断结果反过来又可以为未来任务和相关天体的科学探索提供蓝图。”
IT之家注意到，这项关于火星地下巨大“热异常”的研究成果于 8 月 27 日发表在《自然》杂志上。

title: 特斯拉 FSD 即将迎来重大升级：马斯克称“避坑”功能很快上线
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，特斯拉的 FSD 即将迎来一项重要改进 —— 自动避开路面坑洼。特斯拉 CEO 埃隆 · 马斯克近日表示，这项功能“很快就会推出”。
事实上，“避开坑洼”已经在 FSD v14 的更新说明中出现了一段时间，被列为即将加入的改进功能。
道路上的坑洼大小、形状各不相同，但所有驾驶员对此都有一个共同的态度：都希望尽可能避开。车辆驶入或碾过坑洼，轻则可能造成轮胎和轮毂损坏、四轮定位出现问题，严重时甚至可能导致车内乘员受伤或车辆遭受重大损坏。
马斯克在当地时间上周日晚间发布的一篇帖子中表示，FSD 的自动避坑功能“很快就会推出”。
尽管已经发展到最新、功能最完善的版本，FSD 仍然存在一些短板。
目前，FSD 在避开道路障碍物方面已经表现得相当不错，例如纸箱、马粪、车辆零部件以及其他道路杂物等，都能够较好地识别和规避。不过，对于某些特殊路况，FSD 似乎仍然存在识别困难。
其中，路面坑洼以及道路布局突然发生的变化，仍是 FSD 目前比较容易遇到问题的场景。
这可能意味着，FSD 的三维环境建模系统仍需要更多数据训练，或者需要加入新的算法逻辑，以便识别那些人眼很容易发现、可能对车辆造成损坏的坑洞和道路凸起，并及时采取避让措施。
IT之家注意到，马斯克谈论“自动避坑”实际上已经有很长一段时间。早在 2019 年 4 月，就有一名特斯拉车主首次提出希望车辆能够自动避开坑洼。当时，马斯克回应称，特斯拉“肯定会”开发这项功能。
到了 2020 年 8 月，马斯克又表示，特斯拉正在对道路上的凸起和坑洼进行数据标注，让车辆能够根据情况自动减速，或者直接绕开这些路面障碍。
对于 FSD 而言，能够避开道路上的严重坑洼和其他异常路况，是实现更高级别自动驾驶不可或缺的一项能力。
尤其是在特斯拉正朝着完全自动驾驶的目标迈进之际，未来的理想状态是，车内所有乘员都可以在行驶过程中睡觉、工作或休闲，而无需关注车辆的驾驶过程。
而这一愿景将从本周开始迈出新的重要一步 —— 特斯拉计划于本周四推出 Cybercab。

title: 福特中国首款出口欧洲等发达市场的纯电动商用车，全新福特 Transit City 在江铃小蓝工厂下线
content:
IT之家 8 月 31 日消息，福特中国今日宣布，全新福特 Transit City 下线仪式今日在江铃汽车小蓝工厂举行，首批约 1,000 台车辆即将装船发往海外市场。
据介绍，全新福特 Transit City 由福特中国与全球工程团队以及江铃汽车协同开发，是福特中国首款出口欧洲等发达市场的纯电动商用车，提供 L1H1 厢式车、L2H2 厢式车和单排底盘车（Chassis Cab）三种车身形式，有效载荷最高可达 1,600 公斤，货厢容积最高可达 8.5 立方米，可灵活匹配多样化的城市配送场景。
IT之家获悉，新车搭载 56 千瓦时磷酸铁锂电池与 110 千瓦前置电机，WLTP 工况续航里程最高可达 254 公里，快充 10 分钟可补充 50 公里续航。相比传统柴油车型，其预计维保成本可降低约 40%，高压部件享有 8 年或 16 万公里质保。
车辆标配自动紧急制动、车道保持辅助、智能限速辅助、自适应巡航控制等驾驶辅助技术，并配备支持 Apple CarPlay 和 Android Auto 的 12.3 英寸中控触摸屏，全面对标发达市场的安全与智能配置要求。
该车型已于 2026 年第二季度在欧洲市场开启订购，首批车辆预计将于年底前开始交付当地用户。

Thüringer Forschungsprojekt will ein kostengünstiges, nachrüstbares Prüfsystem für Sägewerke entwickeln
Mit dem Start des Forschungsprojekts DatMuSSS – Datengetriebene Multimodale Sortierung von Stammholz im Sägewerk wollen das Fraunhofer-Institut für Digitale Medientechnologie IDMT, die Technische Universität Ilmenau, die Unternehmen Vision & Control und PREMETEC Automation sowie das Sägewerk Schwarzmühle die automatisierte Holzsortierung voranbringen. Gemeinsam erforschen die Thüringer Partner, wie sich die Qualität von Rundholz mithilfe künstlicher Intelligenz zuverlässig bewerten und daraus automatisiert die passende Sortierung ableiten lässt.
Ziel des Forschungsprojekts soll die Entwicklung eines kostengünstigen und nachrüstbaren Prüfsystems sein, das vor allem kleinen und mittleren Sägewerken eine wirtschaftliche Automatisierung der Sortierprozesse ermöglichen soll.
Wenn ein Holzlieferung im Sägewerk eintrifft, entscheidet die korrekte Bewertung jeden einzelnen Stamms über dessen Qualitätseinstufung und somit über seinen späteren Verkaufspreis und seine Verwendung.
Bis heute erfolgt die Begutachtung der Qualität insbesondere in kleinen und mittleren Sägewerken häufig durch erfahrene Fachkräfte mittels Sichtkontrolle. Innere Schäden wie Hohlräume oder Fäule bleiben dabei jedoch oft verborgen. Gleichzeitig erschweren Fachkräftemangel und steigender Kostendruck die zuverlässige Qualitätskontrolle. Genau hier setzt das neue Forschungsvorhaben DatMuSSS an.
+++ Wie kann ein Baumstamm innerhalb weniger Sekunden zuverlässig bewertet werden? +++
Im Projekt werden erstmals akustische, geometrische und bildliche Informationen von Holzstämmen gemeinsam ausgewertet. Kameras erfassen die Stirnseiten und Mantelflächen der Stämme, akustische Messungen liefern zusätzliche Hinweise auf die innere Holzstruktur und Laserscanner werten Informationen zu Größe und Form aus.
Aus diesen Daten lernt eine KI, die Holzqualität automatisch zu bewerten und daraus die Grundlage für eine automatisierte Sortierung abzuleiten.
Es soll eine robuste Lösung entstehen, die unter realen Produktionsbedingungen arbeitet und einfach in den laufenden Betrieb integriert werden kann.
+++ Thüringer Partner entwickeln Lösung gemeinsam vor Ort +++
Das Forschungsprojekt DatMuSSS verbindet regionale Partner aus Forschung, Technologieentwicklung und Industrie, um gemeinsam eine praxistaugliche Lösung für die automatisierte Holzsortierung zu entwickeln.
Das Fraunhofer-Institut für Digitale Medientechnologie IDMT leitet das Forschungsprojekt und bringt seine Expertise in der KI-basierten Analyse und Auswertung akustischer Signale für Industrieanwendungen ein. Im Projekt entwickelt das Institut Verfahren, mit denen die erfassten Messdaten verknüpft und zur automatischen Bewertung der Holzqualität genutzt werden.
Das Fachgebiet Qualitätssicherung und Industrielle Bildverarbeitung der Technischen Universität Ilmenau entwickelt optische Verfahren und KI-Methoden zur Erfassung und Auswertung sichtbarer Holzmerkmale.
Die Vision & Control GmbH unterstützt das Vorhaben mit ihrer langjährigen Erfahrung in der industriellen Bildverarbeitung und bei der Auswahl der passenden Kamerasysteme für die Erfassung der Bilddaten.
Die PREMETEC Automation GmbH entwickelt eine automatisierte Einheit mit der gezielt die Holzstämme in Schwingungen versetzt und so akustisch vermessen werden können. Das Unternehmen kümmert sich außerdem um die Integration dieser akustischen Prüfeinheit in bestehende Sägewerksanlagen und -prozesse.
Das Sägewerk Schwarzmühle stellt als Anwendungspartner die Testumgebung und die akustischen und optischen Daten für Entwicklung und Validierung des Prüfsystems bereit. Außerdem bringt das Unternehmen sein Wissen zur Bewertung von Rundholz ein und unterstützt damit die Zuordnung der automatisch erfassten Daten zu den tatsächlichen Holzqualitäten.
»Die regionale Nähe aller Projektpartner ist ein großer Vorteil für das Projekt. Sie ermöglicht uns, die entwickelten akustischen und optischen Sensoren, KI-Modelle und Automatisierungslösungen schnell unter realen Bedingungen im Sägewerk zu erproben und gemeinsam weiterzuentwickeln. Gleichzeitig können wir die Integration in bestehende Anlagen und laufende Betriebsprozesse direkt vor Ort testen und frühzeitig prüfen, wie sich die Lösung wirtschaftlich und zuverlässig in der Praxis umsetzen lässt«, erklärt Projektleiter Florian Klein vom Fraunhofer IDMT.
+++ Ziel: Entwicklung einer kostengünstigen und nachrüstbaren Alternative zu aufwändigen Prüfsystemen +++
Für die Bewertung von Rundholz kommen aktuell häufig Röntgen- oder Computertomographie-Systeme zum Einsatz. Diese CT-Systeme ermöglichen detaillierte Einblicke in den Stammaufbau, sind jedoch teuer, benötigen viel Platz und lassen sich im laufenden platzintensiv und rechnen sich für viele Sägewerke Betrieb kaum.
DatMuSSS verfolgt deshalb bewusst einen anderen Ansatz: Es wird ein einfach nachrüstbares Prüfsystem für bestehende Sägewerksanlagen entwickelt. Unternehmen sollen die Technologie ohne grundlegende Umbauten in ihre vorhandenen Prozesse integrieren können. Eine vergleichbare Kombination aus akustischer und visueller Sensorik für die automatisierte Holzsortierung ist derzeit am Markt nicht verfügbar.
»Wir wollen vor allem kleine und mittlere Betriebe dabei unterstützen, die Holzqualität künftig schneller, objektiver und wirtschaftlicher zu bewerten. Mit der KI-basierten automatischen Holzbewertung wollen wir dafür eine wichtige Grundlage schaffen. Bereits jetzt erreichen uns Nachfragen von Sägewerken und holzverarbeitenden Unternehmen aus anderen Regionen Deutschlands. Das zeigt uns, dass der Bedarf unseres Ansatzes weit über Thüringen hinausgeht«, freut sich Florian Klein.
+++ Förderung und Projektlaufzeit +++
Das Verbundprojekt »DatMuSSS – Datengetriebene Multimodale Sortierung von Stammholz im Sägewerk« wird vom Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) im Rahmen des Programms »WIR! – Wandel durch Innovation in der Region« im Bündnis Holz-21-regio unter dem Kennzeichen 03WIR3620A gefördert. Das Vorhaben läuft von August 2026 bis Januar 2028.
