title: AI is Driving the Future of Battery Supply Chains
content:
Battery Manufacturing
Materials
Components
Design & Manufacturing
Aclara Resources and Argonne National Laboratory leverage advanced modeling and digital twins to enhance manufacturing processes for next-generation battery materials.
August 31, 2026
6 Min Read
AI and critical materials shaping future battery supply chains.
AI illustration generated for Battery Technology.
As global demand for more efficient and affordable batteries continues to grow, the conversation is expanding beyond battery chemistry alone. Successfully serving those markets at scale also depends on something equally important: resilient, domestic supply chains for the
critical materials
needed by the industries and technologies that rely on advanced batteries.
Manufacturing products powered by advanced batteries – including industrial equipment, defense systems, consumer electronics and transportation technologies – requires not only traditional battery materials but also a broader portfolio of relatively low-volume yet strategically important materials, including rare earth elements.
As a result, developing the next generation of energy storage technologies is no longer just about battery performance. It also requires a deeper understanding of how the availability and production of critical materials influence the broader supply chains and downstream technologies they support.
Related:
LG Energy Solution North America President on Battery Market Pivot
A new collaboration between rare earth mineral company
Aclara Resources
and the U.S. Department of Energy’s
Argonne National Laboratory
highlights how artificial intelligence, advanced process modeling and public-private partnerships can help address that challenge.
Looking beyond discovery to deployment
For decades, battery innovation has focused on developing better materials with higher energy density, longer lifetimes and improved safety. Today, however, many of the industry’s greatest opportunities lie in commercialization.
How can promising laboratory discoveries be manufactured consistently at industrial scale? How can complex chemical processes be optimized before companies invest hundreds of millions of dollars in production facilities? And how can manufacturers reduce technical risk while accelerating time to market?
Answering those questions is driving growing interest in digital engineering tools that combine scientific understanding with operational data.
Among the most promising are AI-enabled digital twins – virtual representations of manufacturing processes that allow engineers to simulate, analyze, and optimize operations before making changes in the physical world.
A case study in critical materials
Aclara and Argonne are applying that approach to one of the most technically challenging areas of critical materials processing: heavy rare earth separation.
Through an R&D agreement, the partners are developing an AI-enabled digital twin of Aclara’s separation process using data generated at the company’s pilot facility, which was developed in collaboration with Virginia Tech University.
Related:
Inside LGES's New $2B Michigan Battery Plant
Argonne brings expertise in artificial intelligence, advanced computing, process modeling, and solvent extraction science. Together, those capabilities will be used to model the behavior of Aclara’s separation process under a wide range of feedstock compositions, allowing engineers to evaluate potential improvements virtually before implementing them at commercial scale.
Those insights will support Aclara's planned $277 million, first-of-its-kind heavy rare earth separation facility in Louisiana, which is expected to begin production by mid-2028. The facility will process feedstock from the company's ionic clay deposits into separated heavy rare earth oxides, including dysprosium, terbium, and yttrium, helping to strengthen the domestic supply chain for these strategically important materials.
For Aclara, the collaboration is intended to improve process performance, reduce the technical uncertainty that accompanies scaling a sophisticated separation process from pilot operations to commercial production, and ultimately help accelerate deployment of domestic critical materials production.
“This partnership with Argonne is a critical accelerator for Aclara’s strategy to establish a reliable US-based supply chain for heavy rare earths,” stated Ramón Barúa, CEO of Aclara Resources. “By combining our proprietary separation technology and pilot-scale data with Argonne's world-class capabilities in advanced computing, we are significantly reducing scale-up risk, accelerating industrial deployment and strengthening the foundations of a secure domestic supply of these critical minerals.”
Related:
Anthro Energy Breaks Ground on US Facility
Why battery manufacturers should care
At first glance, heavy rare earth separation may seem only indirectly related to batteries. After all, dysprosium and terbium are not active materials in today’s lithium-ion battery cells.
Yet they are essential components of high-performance permanent magnets used in many electric motors that power battery-electric and hybrid vehicles, as well as numerous industrial, defense and clean energy technologies.
More broadly, the collaboration illustrates an important reality for the battery industry: resilient downstream supply chains depend on a much larger critical materials ecosystem.
Manufacturers increasingly recognize that bottlenecks affecting any strategically important material – not just those inside a battery cell – can slow product adoption, increase costs and complicate long-term research and development.
Strengthening domestic processing capabilities across that ecosystem helps create more use case opportunities for advanced battery technologies.
Aclara has indicated that its planned Louisiana facility could ultimately supply more than 75% of US demand for dysprosium and terbium needed for electric vehicles (EVs), reducing dependence on overseas processing while supporting a growing domestic manufacturing base.
Picture:  Aclara’s Separation Pilot Plant at Virginia Tech, US. Courtesy of Aclara.
The bigger opportunity: Smarter manufacturing
Beyond the immediate rare earth application, the collaboration offers a glimpse into how AI could reshape manufacturing throughout the battery industry.
Many of the challenges confronting battery supply chains share common characteristics. Whether refining lithium, producing cathode precursor materials, separating nickel and cobalt, or recovering valuable elements from recycled battery black mass, manufacturers must optimize complex chemical processes while maintaining product quality, controlling costs, and scaling production efficiently.
Historically, much of that optimization has relied on iterative physical testing – a process that can consume considerable time and resources. Digital twins offer a different approach.
As additional operating data become available, the models continue improving, creating a feedback loop that supports continuous optimization throughout the life of a manufacturing facility.
While the production methodology being developed through the Aclara-Argonne collaboration is unique, digital twins have potential applications across a wide range of battery-material manufacturing and recycling processes.
Accelerating commercialization through partnership
The collaboration also demonstrates the complementary roles that industry and national laboratories play in strengthening US manufacturing.
Companies bring commercial insights, operational experience and real-world production challenges. National laboratories contribute multidisciplinary scientific expertise, advanced computing resources and specialized research capabilities that can help solve problems that extend beyond the scope of a single organization.
Together, those strengths can help bridge one of manufacturing’s most difficult transitions: moving innovative technologies from successful pilot operations to dependable commercial production.
“By combining real-world industry needs with deep expertise in the science of scale-up at national laboratories, we can speed the deployment of advanced technologies that strengthen domestic supply chains,” stated Claus Daniel, associate laboratory director for Argonne’s Advanced Energy Technologies directorate. “This work reflects Argonne's role in building regional industrial innovation hubs, such as the Gulf Coast and the Midwest, and leveraging complementary research capabilities to support U.S. competitiveness.”
For the battery industry, the science of scaling production through innovations in manufacturing, process engineering and critical materials production is becoming increasingly important as demand continues to grow.
Projects like the Aclara-Argonne collaboration demonstrate that artificial intelligence can contribute significantly. By combining advanced modeling with industrial expertise, the partnership helps build the manufacturing capabilities and resilient supply chains that will support the success of battery technology.
About the Author
Alex Mitchell
Head of Communications – Science and Technology Partnerships and Outreach, Argonne National Laboratory
Alex Mitchell supports Argonne’s partnerships with industry. Through these collaborations, companies gain access to world-class expertise, advanced research facilities, and tailored solutions that help them solve complex challenges, accelerate innovation, and bring new technologies to market.

title: Meeting AI Demand: Alternate Power, Design, and Site Strategy
content:
As artificial intelligence accelerates the transformation of industries, it is also reshaping the very infrastructure that supports it. Developers, architects, and engineers are taking bold steps toward the future by designing data centers specifically to meet the immense computational and energy needs of AI-driven workloads.
Driven by the immense power demands of AI, traditional approaches to power, site design, and infrastructure are no longer sufficient to meet AI’s needs. Developers must deliver forward-thinking engineering and architectural solutions to redefine how data centers are planned, powered, and positioned for long-term resilience and growth.
The following article showcases strategies that integrate cutting-edge energy solutions, AI-optimized floor plans, and site-selection methodologies that anticipate future demand.
Strategies to Meet AI’s Energy Demand
Related:
OpenAI’s Proposed IPO: A Trifecta of Opportunities, But Don’t Lock In Yet
Training sophisticated AI models and running inference for systems like ChatGPT require power densities far exceeding typical data center norms. Recognizing the limitations of existing utility infrastructure, developers must consider alternative energy sources to ensure reliable, 24/7 service.
On-site generation systems
can be engineered to scale with AI workloads while providing redundancy and sustainability. To curb the reliance on gas plants and coal-fired plants, many tech companies are considering low-carbon energy sources such as nuclear power. The implementation of small modular reactors (SMRs) can reduce emissions and the demand for water as a coolant. Tech companies have signed new contracts for more than 10 GW of possible new nuclear capacity in the last year, according to
Goldman Sachs
. Data centers can also operate behind the meter by co-locating load and clean energy generation, reducing the need for grid upgrades and fossil-fuel pollution.
“By planning beyond the boundaries of traditional utility service, facilities can meet customers’ needs without being bottlenecked by local grid capacity or reliability issues – a critical differentiator as AI adoption accelerates,” said Chris Hastings, Vanderweil Engineers’ Power Group Managing Principal.
Related:
How Changing AI Workloads Are Redefining Data Center Design
Design Solutions for Supporting Alternative Power Sources
High energy demand, power density, and complex AI workloads are rapidly changing how we design data centers. Optimizing a data center for AI isn’t simply a matter of adding more server capacity. The design, site, and floor plan must handle AI’s high-density computational requirements, with spaces that support the necessary cooling, power distribution, and flexibility for future upgrades.
The history of designing and constructing programmed spaces and site layouts for data centers has changed over the years, and significantly in the past year. Twenty years ago, the ratio of data halls to support space was 50/50. Today, we’re seeing the building size reduced significantly, but the site area remains the same or increases drastically to accommodate cooling equipment and on-site power generation.
These changes are driven by
increasing rack densities
– from 25-30 kW per rack to as much as 600 kW per rack – as well as moving support space, such as utility power supply and power rooms, outside. As building size changes with higher densities, cooling requirements are rising sharply. Having enough cooling equipment on roofs to prevent the facility from overheating becomes infeasible.
Related:
Preparing Enterprise Data Centers for AI Adoption
“The challenges of site and building planning are tied to the mechanical and electrical system design now more than ever,” said Dutch Wickes, Ci Design, Inc., Principal and Global Mission Critical Practice Leader. “All the variables make a Rubik’s Cube look easy! Especially when you throw in on-site power generation, whether it is bridging power or permanent power. The typical rules of thumb are moot.”
Once a potential site is identified, informed decision-making requires a conceptual plan developed with the client, input from mechanical and electrical engineers, and architectural planning. An integrated, on-site power generation and distribution system that harmonizes with the facility’s architecture could ensure not only operational efficiency but also scalability, enabling the end user to expand capacity without redesigning core systems. These innovations align with broader goals of resilience and sustainability, ensuring the facility is future-proofed against both technological and regulatory change.
Strategic Site Selection
Beyond the traditional criteria of connectivity, proximity to users, and
climate risk
, data center locations must be evaluated for their ability to accommodate off-grid power infrastructure, access to alternative fuels, and regulatory environments supportive of innovative energy solutions.
“Utilities significantly impact data center site selection decisions. We’re seeing data centers emerge in more remote locations that have access to less strained grids, but the lack of adequate power interconnection and infrastructure can pose issues,” said Mason McPike, Provident Data Centers’ Executive Director of Vertical Development & Delivery. “Finding a successful data center site starts with building strong relationships between the end user, government entities, utility companies, and the local community.”
Smart site selection ensures that each facility is located where it can deliver maximum value – not only today, but as AI demands grow exponentially in the coming years. Facilities built close to power plants can overcome these issues, but data centers that generate their own off-grid power using technologies such as fuel cells, batteries, renewable energy, and SMRs may be a more sustainable solution for the environment and surrounding communities.
Positioning for the Future
Early collaboration among the end user, developer, architect, and engineer can position a data center project at the forefront of a rapidly evolving industry. By addressing energy constraints head-on, designing for AI’s unique operational needs, and selecting sites that support a bold, off-grid vision, the industry can set a new standard for how data centers can and should evolve.
“The changing market demand allows us to have an adaptive perspective in how we approach data center development,” McPike said. “Everything has to work in tandem, from finding the right site to sourcing power supply and creating an efficient design. We have to rapidly evolve as the online world continues to grow in response to new technologies.”
For data center professionals, these lessons underscore the importance of rethinking traditional assumptions and embracing integrated solutions that bridge power, design, and location strategies. As AI continues to redefine what’s possible, these forward-looking strategies will define the next generation of mission-critical infrastructure.

title: SLB’s $4.1B Kelvion Deal Expands AI Data Center Push
content:
SLB will spend $4.1 billion to acquire thermal management company Kelvion, expanding its data center business into cooling and heat rejection as AI workloads drive higher power densities.
The deal adds heat exchangers, heat rejection equipment and other thermal management technologies to SLB’s engineering, modular manufacturing, offsite construction, power integration and digital capabilities.
SLB said Kelvion will more than double its revenue opportunity per gigawatt of delivered data center capacity. The combined data center business is expected to generate more than $2 billion in revenue in 2026, with SLB targeting $4.5 billion to $5 billion in revenue by 2028.
“It’s less about what SLB sells today and more about what it becomes,” said Alex Cordovil, research director at Dell’Oro Group.
Until now, SLB has been a relatively small data center player focused on prefabricated modular capacity and integrating third party equipment into delivered facilities, Cordovil said.
Related:
Solid-State Transformers Power Next-Gen AI Data Centers
“Kelvion turns SLB into an OEM in one of the fastest growing corners of the thermal chain,” he said.
SLB’s Data Center Solutions business has grown at a compound annual rate of more than 90% from 2024 through 2026. The company expects cumulative delivered capacity to exceed 2 GW by the end of this year.
Kelvion expects 2026 revenue of $2.3 billion to $2.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $350 million to $400 million. Its data center business is expected to generate $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion.
Heat Rejection
AI cooling discussions have focused heavily on direct to chip technologies such as cold plates and coolant distribution units. But heat captured at the chip still has to move through the cooling loop and ultimately leave the facility.
Kelvion gives SLB a larger position in that part of the system.
“Most of the attention has gone to cold plates and CDUs, but the segment repricing fastest right now is heat rejection,” Cordovil said.
He pointed to rising rack densities and pressure over data center water consumption as drivers for dry coolers and hybrid or adiabatic systems, areas where Kelvion has established technology.
SLB said modern GPUs are already pushing rack power densities above 100 kW, while some announced chip architectures could approach 1 MW.
Higher densities increase the amount of heat cooling systems must move and reject at the facility level. Kelvion also has technologies for waterless cooling applications, giving SLB additional options in markets where water availability or community opposition limits conventional cooling approaches.

Trump Targets Foreign Grid Equipment as Data Centers Expand
Integrated Cooling
SLB plans to integrate Kelvion’s thermal technologies into its modular infrastructure rather than treating cooling as a separate system added later.
Management said that would bring thermal management into the design process alongside SLB’s engineering and manufacturing capabilities.
“This creates a more integrated infrastructure architecture with better alignment across performance requirements, configuration choices and deployment timing for customers,” said Gavin Rennick, president of SLB’s New Energy and Industrial business.
SLB pointed to its work as a modular design partner for Nvidia AI factories as an example. Management said Kelvion’s thermal expertise could help optimize cooling as those systems are designed and fabricated.
Cordovil said integration will determine whether the acquisition produces a lasting competitive advantage.
“Durable differentiation sits in system design and controls rather than in individual components,” he said. “So the test is whether SLB can integrate, not whether it can manufacture.”
Kelvion also supplies components to other companies in the thermal management market, potentially leaving SLB competing with companies that buy Kelvion equipment.
Related:
DOE Retreat on Transmission Corridors Tests the Case for Building Ahead
“SLB now sits as both competitor and supplier to parts of the ecosystem,” Cordovil said.
Beyond Cooling
SLB also sees the acquisition as a potential entry point into other parts of the data center infrastructure stack.
CEO Olivier Le Peuch said the company could combine its modular and cooling capabilities with partnerships for behind the meter generation and other power solutions.
SLB also identified potential opportunities involving geothermal and carbon capture.
“The more interesting question is whether cooling is the entry point rather than the destination,” Cordovil said. “SLB’s core competence is energy, and a growing number of data centers are having to generate their own power.”
The company said it sees an opportunity to offer hyperscalers integrated power, cooling and modular infrastructure as operators seek to secure the infrastructure needed for large AI deployments.
Market Expansion
SLB estimates the data center infrastructure market it can address will exceed $150 billion by 2030, excluding IT and silicon.
Dell’Oro uses a narrower definition and expects the data center physical infrastructure market to surpass $80 billion by 2030, Cordovil said.
Kelvion also expands SLB’s geographic reach. SLB has built its data center business primarily in the US, while Kelvion has established operations and customers in Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
Le Peuch said the US will remain the foundation of the business, followed by Europe and then Asia and the Middle East.
Kelvion’s non data center business also gives SLB exposure to thermal management applications in energy and industrial markets, including heat pumps, renewables, carbon capture and processing.
The Deal
SLB will pay about $3.4 billion in cash and assume about $700 million of Kelvion debt. The transaction values Kelvion at about 11 times estimated 2026 adjusted EBITDA before synergies and about 8.5 times after expected synergies.
SLB expects about $120 million in annual EBITDA synergies within three years of closing. About $70 million will come from cost savings, with the remainder expected from revenue opportunities.
Cost savings are expected from supply chain efficiencies, manufacturing optimization, logistics, service centers and G&A. Revenue opportunities will come from expanding Kelvion technologies across SLB’s customer base and into new geographic markets.
The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.
SLB expects the combined data center business to generate $700 million to $800 million in adjusted EBITDA in 2028 alongside its $4.5 billion to $5 billion revenue target.
For SLB, the acquisition moves data centers from a modular construction business into a broader infrastructure strategy spanning engineering, thermal management and potentially power.

title: Enel secures grid connection for 356 MW/2.1 GWh BESS in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Chile’s National Electricity Coordinator has issued the Connection Authorization Report for Enel Green Power Chile’s BESS Guanchoi project, which comprises a 356 MW battery energy storage system with six hours of duration, equivalent to 2,136 MWh of energy capacity. The BESS will be integrated with the existing Guanchoi PV plant so that the combined facility operates as a Renewable Generation Plant with Storage Capacity (CRCA). The BESS will connect to the 33 kV cells at the Bella Mónica substation, which is owned by Enel Green Power Chile. Under the conditions communicated for the authorization, Enel must comply with the technical and regulatory requirements established by the Coordinator and obtain a construction declaration for the project from the National Energy Commission (CNE) before September 2027. Once the connection has been completed, use of the dedicated transmission infrastructure capacity will be indefinite. The project represents a considerable expansion from the initial plans known for adding storage to Guanchoi. Documents published by the Coordinator in 2023 referred to a “Guanchoi PV plant storage system” of 42 MW, also connected to the Bella Mónica substation at 33 kV. The new project advanced through the permitting process this year. Chile’s Electricity and Fuel Superintendency (SEC) records an application by Enel Green Power Chile for a definitive electricity concession for the Guanchoi 33 kV Underground Power Line. The application was submitted in April and declared admissible in June 2026. Separately, at a hearing held on April 16 and recorded on the official Lobby Law platform, representatives of Enel Green Power discussed the electrical easement associated with BESS Guanchoi with officials from the Ministry of National Assets and reported a planned investment of $350 million for the storage system. Guanchoi is located in the commune of Diego de Almagro in the Atacama region. The PV plant began commercial operations in July 2023 with 398 MW of net installed capacity. Enel estimates that it can produce more than 1,100 GWh annually, and the facility has around 900,000 bifacial solar modules. The addition of BESS Guanchoi will expand Enel’s storage portfolio in Chile. The company recently started construction of the 100 MW Finis Terrae BESS and is also building the roughly 205 MW, four-hour Las Salinas system and the 94 MW/372 MWh Azabache BESS. Enel said in mid-August that it had more than 730 MW of storage in operation and under construction, a figure that did not yet include Guanchoi as a project under construction. title: Engie reaches 663 MW of operational BESS capacity in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Engie Chile has announced the commercial operation date (COD) of BESS Libélula and BESS Los Loros, two battery energy storage systems located in the Metropolitan and Atacama regions, respectively, with a combined maximum gross power output of 251 MW. With their addition, the company now has 663 MW of BESS capacity in operation in Chile. The larger of the two systems is BESS Libélula, located in the municipalities of Colina and Tiltil, about 40 km north of Santiago. It has 203 MW of maximum gross power and 1,034 MWh of storage capacity, distributed across 208 lithium-ion battery containers, with a five-hour discharge duration. The system is part of PV & BESS Libélula, Engie Chile’s first project in the Metropolitan Region and the company’s first project designed from the outset as a hybrid solar and storage facility. The full complex represents an investment of $320 million, of which $219 million corresponds to the BESS. While the battery system has reached COD, the solar plant is fully energized and continues the process of obtaining authorization for commercial operation. The solar plant has a maximum gross power output of 140 MW and comprises 245,560 modules. Its grid connection infrastructure includes a step-up substation and an approximately 16 km, 220 kV transmission line to the El Manzano substation. As reported in April, during construction Engie reported 151 MWp of solar capacity and 199 MW of storage capacity for Libélula. The figures now reported following the start of operations correspond to maximum gross power outputs. The plant also includes 2,311 Nextpower NX Horizon Low Carbon solar trackers, manufactured using steel produced in an electric arc furnace. Engie said the solution reduces emissions associated with the equipment by approximately 30% compared with conventional manufacturing methods. BESS Los Loros, meanwhile, is integrated into the Los Loros Solar Park in the municipality of Tierra Amarilla, Atacama region. The system required an investment of $64 million and has a maximum gross power output of 48 MW and 275.23 MWh of storage capacity. The installation comprises 63 containers with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries and stores part of the solar plant’s daytime generation for subsequent delivery to Chile’s National Electricity System. In March, BESS Los Loros was reported as energized, with Engie citing 46 MW of installed power and 230 MWh of capacity and expecting commercial operation in the second half of this year. The company now reports maximum gross power and capacity of 48 MW and 275.23 MWh, respectively, following COD. “Hoy estamos construyendo la infraestructura necesaria para una nueva etapa de la transición energética, donde no basta con incorporar más energías renovables, sino que también debemos desarrollar capacidades que permitan gestionarlas de manera eficiente y segura”, said Juan Villavicencio, CEO of Engie Chile. The new projects add to Engie’s growing storage portfolio in Chile. Recent facilities to enter commercial operation include BESS Tocopilla, with 116 MW/660 MWh , and BESS Arica, with 25 MW/150 MWh . title: Germany breaks ground on major battery storage projects - Energy Storage
content: HyperStrong has broken ground on the GigaBattery Boxberg 400, a 400 MW/1.6 GWh battery energy storage system in Saxony, Germany, acting as turnkey contractor for project owner LEAG Clean Power. The facility is being built on a six-hectare remediated site at the Boxberg power plant location. HyperStrong’s German subsidiary signed the EPC agreement with LEAG in November 2025. The project will use HyperStrong’s liquid-cooled HyperBlock III system, configured for four-hour duration, and will connect to the 50Hertz transmission grid through a new 380 kV substation. Upon completion, LEAG says the facility could theoretically supply electricity to approximately 640,000 households for four hours. The project is one of Europe’s largest battery storage projects currently under construction. It forms part of LEAG’s planned GigaBattery pipeline, which also includes the 1,000 MW/4,000 MWh GigaBattery Jänschwalde project; combined, LEAG’s announced GigaBattery projects total 1.4 GW/5.6 GWh. Separately, Sunotec has started construction on a 100 MW/441 MWh standalone battery storage system in Stendal, in the German state of Saxony-Anhalt, after the project reached ready-to-build status in the second quarter of 2026. Sunotec is acting as full turnkey provider, covering engineering, installation, and long-term operations and maintenance, with commissioning targeted for the first quarter of 2027. WT Energiesysteme will build a new 110 kV substation at the site to provide the grid-connection infrastructure. Around 65 guests from politics and the energy industry attended the project’s official groundbreaking last week. The storage system is intended to increase grid flexibility, absorbing electricity during periods of high solar and wind generation and discharging it when demand requires. Sunotec has reported several developments in Germany this year. In January, it secured a contract for the first of four construction phases of a 230 MWh storage system for Seac. In April, investment firm Blackstone acquired a stake in Sunotec for €250 million , with the company’s founders remaining majority shareholders; the funds are intended to accelerate Sunotec’s European expansion. title: Korkia advances Chilean storage pipeline across two projects for 1.55 GWh - Energy Storage
content: A 750 MWh standalone battery energy storage system (BESS) dubbed the Beltrán project, located in the Valparaiso region, has reached ready-to-build (RTB) status. The standalone system, situated close to the La Pólvora substation, is being developed by Korkia in partnership with Solar Ray. Korkia also confirmed progress on its Mellizas hybrid project, a 218 MW solar power plant with a co-located 800 MWh BESS. Mellizas has received environmental approval, enabling the company to proceed to the next phases of development. Developed along with its Chilean development partner Ciudad Luz, Mellizas will cover approximately 300 hectares, with Korkia claiming it will be “one of the largest solar PV developments in Pemuco in the Ñuble region.” “These milestones reflect the tangible progress we are making in Chile, advancing projects through key development and de-risking stages. Mellizas and Beltran also demonstrate the strategic role that energy storage will play in building a more flexible and resilient energy system and enabling the continued growth of renewable energy in the country,” said Rodrigo Ackermann, vice president LatAm​ at Korkia. In August 2026, Korkia and joint venture partner Semecon sold their 125 MW Kukonkyla BESS project in Finland to Enlight Renewable Energy.  It was also granted a grid permit for 550 MW project in Romania . Korkia’s renewable energy pipeline spans 15 GW of mature utility-scale solar, wind and BESS assets, with a further 9 GW progressing through early-stage development in Europe, North America, and South America. Earlier this year, Solar Ray received environmental approval for its 150 MW / 750 MWh Paicavi BESS. title: Leag starts building 1.6 GWh battery storage system - Energy Storage
content: Construction of the “GigaBattery Boxberg 400” battery storage system has officially started with a groundbreaking ceremony. The 400 MW/1,600 MWh system is being built at the Boxberg power plant site in Saxony and is part of Leag’s so-called GigawattFactory, which will include numerous large-scale PV and wind power plants as well as battery storage systems. For the project, Leag is using a six-hectare remediated site at its former Plant II. The battery storage system is being built jointly by the main contractors Leag Clean Power, Siemens Energy, and Hyperstrong International (Germany), a subsidiary of Beijing Hyperstrong Technology. Hyperstrong will supply the lithium iron phosphate batteries, integrate the electrical systems, and construct the storage facility. The project will use the “HyperBlock III” storage system, which was specifically developed for large-scale, power plant applications. In parallel with the battery storage system, Siemens Energy will build a new gas-insulated 380 kV switchgear system (GIS). This will provide the connection to the transmission grid operated by 50Hertz. It will also connect renewable power generation around the Boxberg power plant site to the storage system, the companies said. title: In Sept, Tesla will re-launch 3 products it launched a decade ago, for a stock pump
content:
Tesla has a packed September ahead of it, with two confirmed and one rumored product launches. For a company that has gone so long without new products, it would be a big month… if all three of those products hadn’t been launched years ago already.
It’s September 2026, and we’ve got a lot to look forward to in the EV space.
First up, we’re finally going to see the launch of the Tesla Cybercab this Thursday, September 3. The Cybercab is a small, two-seat vehicle intended to be used fully autonomously as a robotaxi, and doesn’t even have a steering wheel or pedals, as it’s meant to operate without a driver at all times.
Second, Tesla has confirmed that late this month it will roll out the Tesla Semi, a fully-electric heavy duty semi truck. This promises to make goods delivery more efficient, which is important given that larger vehicles are responsible for well more than their fair share of the pollution that harms human health. There are other electric semis, but Tesla claims to offer a better value proposition than the rest of them.
Finally, there’s the specter of the next-gen Tesla Roadster. While nothing is announced yet, Tesla designer Franz von Holzhausen said the Roadster is coming “very soon,” and we have heard some rumors suggesting the month of September. The Tesla Roadster is meant to be a fully electric hypercar with bonkers performance specs, which CEO Elon Musk has said will be the “last best driver’s car” but also says that it will be able to “fly” (which doesn’t make sense).
It would be an exciting month… if we hadn’t been hearing about all of these products for years now.
Cybercab unveiled in 2024, but the idea is much older
The Cybercab is the newest of the three, having been originally revealed in 2024. That’s an acceptable time between reveal and production, if actually even a little quick (well, as long as we’re not comparing to China’s EV timelines).
But that ignores the years of robotaxi-related talk from Musk, who originally suggested way back in 2016 that Tesla owners who purchased FSD (software which the company sold for as much as $15,000 and still has not delivered) would be able to send their cars out as autonomous taxis to make them money.
At the time, this was meant to apply to Tesla’s consumer vehicles, and Tesla called the concept “Tesla Network.” Now, it’s branding it as “Robotaxi,” and Tesla has sent out its own vehicles to make money using FSD, but still won’t let you do it, despite that it sold software on the promise that you could (and that this software would turn cars into an “appreciating asset” due to gradual technological unlocks).
Tesla even cancelled the planned Model 2, an affordable consumer vehicle, to make room for the stripped-down Cybercab, which we have no indication will be purchaseable by consumers.
And don’t forget: Tesla has not solved self-driving. Neither the consumer-available FSD nor the Robotaxi-exclusive version that allows operation without someone in the driver’s seat is truly capable of unattended operation at all times, or even in more than a few geofenced areas. Releasing a car with no steering wheel makes no sense before you solve that problem.
So while we’ll soon see the Cybercab in some sort of action, it is based on a concept that is more than a decade late, it still doesn’t deliver on its promises, and Tesla turned it from something that would be publicly-available and that people spent tens of thousands of dollars on into something that Tesla alone can operate and potentially profit on, while consumers are restricted from doing the thing they were promised when they bought their product.
Tesla Semi was first shown in 2017, almost a decade ago
The Tesla Semi does stand to revolutionize trucking – or at least, it did 9 years ago when it was first shown with a planned 2020 release.
Electrek attended that event, and heard the pronouncements about how the Semi would take over trucking. It would beat diesel trucks in all-in cost per mile, so there’s really no reason a fleet manager should bother buying a diesel truck ever again.
Except, of course, that the Semi has not been available. Despite a whole bleacher full of fleet managers being invited to that event for dealmaking purposes, the Semi took its sweet time to get to scale.
Tesla did deliver its first Semis in late 2022, late but not so late, and that first batch went to PepsiCo and its subsidiary Frito-Lay. And then… not much happened. We didn’t get official counts, but by looking through recall paperwork, it was clear that Semis were being assembled at a glacial pace, if at all.
Since 2021, Tesla has also said that a dedicated Semi production line was being worked on at its Nevada battery factory. Over the years there has been progress on that line, but it has been quite slow.
Finally, this year, the first truck rolled off the dedicated high-volume line, and Semis have been trickling out to other customers over time (and we finally got to ride in one at ACT Expo last year).
So Tesla’s new event to “rollout” the Semi is a little confusing, given that the truck was already unveiled at an event in 2017, delivered at an event in 2022, and the factory started working in April 2026. We’re not really sure what the purpose is for this event, although the next product might give us more of a hint…
The Roadster might get launched, or might get pushed back… for stock pumping reasons
The Roadster is another continually delayed product. First unveiled in the same event as the Tesla Semi in 2017, it was promised to be the car that gave a “hard-core smack down to gasoline powered cars.” But now in 2026, we still don’t have a definitive idea of when it will be released.
Now, perhaps you’ll say that the Roadster doesn’t fit in this article, since there’s no announced launch in September like the other two products. But there was supposed to be a demo in August, which ended yesterday, and a demo has been announced and pushed back many times prior.
(But even if we do skip the Roadster, we could throw in FSD being able to avoid potholes as a planned product upgrade, which was first announced in 2019, and which Musk said this week is “coming soon”)
But more importantly, another recent statement from a former Tesla president could shine some light on the real reason for all these events: that the Roadster delays have all been about bringing Tesla and SpaceX closer together.
The connection is particularly clear in the case of the Roadster, which Musk said early on would be available with a “SpaceX package” to increase performance further, which Musk said would be demonstrated by “the end of next year” in 2019 (hmm, where have I heard that phrase before…).
Originally, that SpaceX package was marketed as using cold gas thrusters to help performance. This is theoretically possible and could be beneficial, if they were used for lateral thrust or additional downforce and if weight was kept down.
But later Musk started saying nonsense like the car would be able to “hover” or “fly“, which does not actually provide a performance benefit (nobody is ever looking for “upforce”). We’ve found other performance patents that would actually be kind of cool, but all the rhetoric has been about SpaceX, flying, rockets and so on.
So why talk about all this stuff if it doesn’t help performance? Well, maybe it’s about a different kind of performance: stock performance.
This is all probably about a merger, which in turn is about getting Musk more money and power
As time has marched on, and especially after SpaceX’s recent IPO, it has become more and more apparent that Musk’s goal is to merge SpaceX and Tesla. This would be beneficial for him personally, because it would allow him to cheat on the goals laid out in his ridiculous stock packages, giving him potentially trillions of dollars in stock value without meeting any of the operational milestones attached to the stock grants that shareholders unwisely voted to adopt.
And if that’s the goal, then there needs to be both a reason for this to happen, and hype that makes investors in one stock want to be involved in the other.
Marketing the Roadster as something that could only be achieved by closer collaboration between the companies offers a possible reason for the merger to happen, and other product unveilings are necessary to give the impression that a company that has only delivered one new product in the last 5 years(and it’s a huge flop) has something going for it in the future.
And the more buzz associated with both companies, the better off Elon Musk will be. The companies won’t necessarily benefit from it – usually in an all-stock merger (as is expected), you want your company to have more value and the other company to have lower value, so you’re getting a better deal; if both go up in value, you’re not really gaining anything. But Musk benefits from higher market caps, because that’s what triggers his stock awards.
The higher the market cap, the more stock he gets personally, and the more every other shareholder’s stake is diluted in order to pay out the worst and most overpaid employee at either company (or any company, for that matter).

title: Tesla confirms Full Self-Driving was active in a crash that killed a mother of five
content:
Fred Lambert
| Sep 1 2026 - 7:52 am PT
A Tesla Model Y turning left at an intersection collided with a pickup truck in Batavia, Illinois, killing a passenger in the Tesla — Maggie Espinosa, 37, a teacher and mother of five. It was reported as an ordinary intersection crash.
But Electrek was able to confirm that Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says the car’s driver-assist system was engaged as it made that turn. This is part of an
ongoing Electrek investigation
matching reported crashes to Tesla’s redacted NHTSA data.
What happened at Randall and McKee
Around 4:19 p.m. on March 25, 2026, a Tesla Model Y heading south on Randall Road tried to turn left onto McKee Street and struck a Dodge pickup traveling straight in the opposite direction, according to Batavia police. A Nissan SUV was also caught up in the crash.
Espinosa, a front-seat passenger in the Tesla, died of her injuries. A former kindergarten teacher, she left behind five children, including 2-year-old twins; a
GoFundMe for the family
raised more than $100,000. The Tesla’s driver and two others were injured.
What Tesla told the federal government
Under a NHTSA Standing General Order, automakers must report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact. Tesla filed a report on this crash — and it’s revealing.
Tesla marks the automation “Engagement Status” as
“Verified Engaged,”
and lists the 2026 Model Y’s pre-crash movement as
“Making Left Turn”
at 24 mph, at an intersection. It says the Tesla struck the front of the pickup, which had the right of way going straight. And it confirms Tesla holds the
event-data recorder, telematics, and video
of the crash.
Then it redacts the parts that would explain it: the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area — all as “confidential business information.”
We’ve laid out the complete record below — everything Tesla disclosed, and everything it blacked out.
Electrek
contacted Batavia PD to let them know that Tesla confirmed its ADAS was active during the crash and ask for an update on the investigation. Batavia PD said that the crash “remains under investigation and is currently under review by the Kane County State’s Attorney’s Office.” No charges have been filed. And in the public account, there was no mention of Autopilot, “Full Self-Driving,” or any driver-assist system.
Tesla Full Self-Driving vs Autopilot
This one points more directly at “Full Self-Driving” than the highway cases we’ve covered. An
unprotected left turn across oncoming traffic at an intersection
is a City-Streets maneuver — something FSD does, and something basic Autopilot cannot. Basic Autopilot is a highway lane-keeping system; it does not turn a car left onto a cross street. So a driver-assist car that was
verified engaged while making a left turn
was, in all likelihood, running FSD.
However, that doesn’t mean FSD was at fault in the crash, but we don’t know without all the data, and Tesla is the one gatekeeping it. It didn’t even want the public to know that FSD was active in the crash until we were able to connect the NHTSA report to the media and police reports about the crash.
How we matched it:
the NHTSA record is unredacted on location (Batavia), vehicle (2026 Model Y), the left-turn-into-a-pickup mechanics, the fatality, and the month — a combination unique to this crash. One caveat: the incident time Tesla logged (12:54 UTC) does not cleanly convert to the ~4:19 p.m. local time police reported, unlike the other crashes we’ve matched, so we’re flagging that discrepancy rather than relying on it; every other identifying detail lines up.
Electrek’s Take
A teacher and mother of five is dead, a county prosecutor is weighing whether anyone should be charged, and the single piece of evidence that would show what actually happened in that intersection, did the software make the turn, or the driver?, is sitting in Tesla’s servers.
Tesla is testing software it calls ‘beta’ on public roads, turning every road user into an unwilling lab rat. At the minimum, and really, that’s all we are advocating for here, is to get all the details about what happens when it goes wrong.
We know Tesla is quick to release data and massage it when it looks good for the company, but it hides everything else.
If you are going to market the product as “self-driving” and encourage users to “use their phones”, you can’t hide the data when the system is involved in a fatal crash.

title: Tracking the fatal Tesla Autopilot and FSD crashes hidden in its data
content:
Tesla reports its Autopilot and “Full Self-Driving” crashes to the federal government, as it’s required to — and then blacks out almost everything in those reports, so the public never learns what happened in those crashes. Tesla always end up blaming the driver.
We’re matching those redacted reports, one by one, to real fatal crashes that were covered in the news as ordinary accidents. This is a running investigation, and we’ll add each crash we confirm to this page. You can view this as an investigative hub keeping track of our ongoing investigation.
What the data shows
Under a 2021 NHTSA Standing General Order (SGO), automakers must report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was hurt, killed, or a vehicle was towed. Tesla accounts for roughly 85% of the entire industry’s reports — nearly 4,000 crashes — and the count climbs every year.
We believe that between FSD and Autopilot, Tesla has more mileage on ADAS than any other automaker and therefore, it’s not necessarily a problem that it has more crashes, but it’s nonetheless worrying that crashes are reaching new records each month.
The problem is what Tesla does to those reports. On virtually all of them, it redacts the crash narrative, the software version, and the field for whether the road was within the system’s approved operating area — all as “confidential business information.” It has blacked out the narrative on 99.9% of its reports every single year since 2019.
Almost no other automaker does this. GM, Ford, Honda, and Toyota redact essentially none of their narratives. Tesla is the only high-volume reporter that hides everything.
How we’re doing this
The reports do leave a handful of fields unredacted: city, state, month, vehicle, roadway, a pre-crash speed, and an incident time logged in UTC. That’s enough to match many of them to specific, named crashes covered in the local press.
So we do. We convert the UTC timestamp to local time and line it up against the time police gave; we confirm the city, the vehicle, and the fatal outcome; and we check that it’s the only matching crash that month. Where a case checks out, we lay it out in two columns — everything Tesla told the government, and everything the public was told — and we file public-records requests with the investigating agencies for what Tesla won’t release, including whether police received Tesla’s raw telemetry or only Tesla’s own interpretation of it.
The crashes we’ve confirmed so far
Each of these was reported publicly as an ordinary crash, with no mention of Autopilot or FSD — until Tesla’s own redacted NHTSA report revealed the system was engaged.
- Clute, Texas — Steven Alvarez, 23, died when his Model 3 left the road and hit a park pool. Police called it a possible medical episode. Tesla’s data: driver-assist verified engaged at 104 mph — a speed that appears nowhere in the public record.
- Lake Mary, Florida — a 43-year-old man died when his Model 3 sat stopped in a live I-4 lane and a semi rear-ended it. Troopers said they couldn’t explain why the car was stopped. Tesla’s data: driver-assist verified engaged, at 0 mph.
- Mesa, Arizona — weeks later, a near-identical case: another 2020 Model 3, stopped at 0 mph on Loop 202 at 3 a.m., rear-ended, its driver killed. Same signature, driver-assist verified engaged — and Tesla holds the video.
- Batavia, Illinois — Maggie Espinosa, 37, a teacher and mother of five, was killed as a passenger when a Model Y turning left at an intersection struck a pickup. Tesla’s data: driver-assist verified engaged while making the turn — a maneuver that points to “Full Self-Driving.” The case is now under review by the Kane County State’s Attorney’s Office, and Tesla holds the video.
We’ll update this list as we confirm more.
Why this matters
This is not an abstract transparency fight. Tesla is, more aggressively than ever, encouraging owners to treat a Level 2 driver-assistance system as if it were autonomous. It sells the software as “Full Self-Driving,” Elon Musk repeatedly promises unsupervised autonomy is months away, and the marketing invites drivers to trust the car to drive itself.
But legally and technically, it is still Level 2: the human is driving and is responsible at all times. Tesla’s own actions confirm the gap — it has not removed the supervision requirement from consumer FSD, and its robotaxi service remains a handful of closely monitored vehicles. The technology is not what the branding says it is.
That gap is dangerous, because it breeds complacency — drivers who over-trust the system and stop paying attention. And when things don’t go well, Tesla blames the drivers for abusing the system and releases limited redacted data so we don’t even know what happened.
Tesla is pushing owners to believe the car can handle things itself; it is hiding the records that would show how the system actually behaves when things go wrong. The public is asked to trust the marketing while being denied the data.
Electrek’s Take
Tesla is blacking out the single most important fields in a federal safety database — what its car did, which software was running, and whether the car was even supposed to be operating that way — in reports about crashes that killed people. It justifies this by claiming it would “suffer financial harm” if the information became public. In other words, Tesla is telling regulators that the commercial value of its secrecy outweighs the public’s right to know how its cars behave in fatal crashes. That is indefensible.
Top comment by oldgeek
There's a less charitable interpretation of the claim that tesla would suffer financial harm if more of its crash information was made public. Namely that there's something both really bad and actionable hiding in that data, so that the company would both lose sales and face additional liability.
(Not exactly on point, but in litigation when a defendant destroys or refuses to produce required information, jurors are generally allowed to assume that the information would have damaged the defendant's case.)
You can’t use public roads to test software that you admit is “beta” and then keep the public in the dark when it fails, and someone dies.
It is also selective. When the data makes the software look good, or Tesla can present the data in a way that makes its system look good — as in the fatal Katy, Texas crash, where Tesla could point to the driver overriding the system, the details come out. When they don’t, the report is sealed. A company confident in its technology would not need to hide what its cars did when things go wrong while broadcasting it when they go right.
Tesla is already under NHTSA investigation over how it reports these crashes, and its own AI trainers have told Reuters they don’t trust its safety stats. Electrek’s position is simple: Tesla should stop redacting its SGO crash narratives and software versions, and NHTSA should stop accepting the redactions. As long as it keeps them sealed, we’ll keep doing this the hard way — matching the crashes one at a time, and adding them here.

title: Volvo's cheapest EV can now power a campsite or coffee maker
content:
Volvo EX30
Peter Johnson
| Sep 1 2026 - 8:51 am PT
Volvo launched a software update that gives
the EX30
new capabilities, including the ability to power external electronics with vehicle-to-load (V2L).
Volvo EX30 gains V2L and more in latest update
Starting this week, EX30 drivers will be able to use their vehicle for more than just getting from point A to point B.
Volvo Cars is rolling out its latest over-the-air software update, giving the EX30 the ability to be used as a power bank on wheels.
With bidirectional charging, including vehicle-to-load (V2L), the EX30 can power external devices, such as a laptop, coffee maker, the fridge if the power goes out, or even a campsite using energy from the vehicle’s battery.
Delivering up to 3 kW at 16 amps, Volvo said the system can power “a wide range of everyday equipment.” It can be used when needed, but once the battery level drops below 20%, the system will automatically cut off the energy supply to save energy.
Volvo EX30 gains new features via OTA update (Source: Volvo Cars)
How does it work? With a separate adapter, you can connect it to the charge port and then plug in the device to draw power from the vehicle’s battery.
The V2L functions will not be available for EX30 drivers in the US, Canada, Mexico, Korea, Taiwan, or Japan. In the EMEA, APAC, and Latin America markets, it will use the CCS2 charging standard.
Volvo EX30 gains new features via OTA update (Source: Volvo Cars)
Volvo’s latest update also introduces a new user experience with a customizable contextual bar and redesigned settings menu.
In certain European markets, Volvo is introducing Plug & Charge capabilities for EX30 drivers. The ability streamlines public charging and eliminates the need for a physical card or extra app. It will only be available on 2026 models or newer.
Electrek’s Take
Adding bidirectional charging and V2L is a big update for the EX30, a feature that should already be offered on all EVs.
While it is disappointing to see those in the US will miss out, it’s not much of a surprise given Volvo announced it was
discontinuing the EX30
in the US after the 2026 model year.
Other entry-level electric vehicles, like the
2027 Kia EV3
, will fill the void left by the EX30. The 2027 Kia EV3 starts at $30,000, offers up to 321 miles of range, and comes with standard V2L.

title: Waymo opens robotaxi rides to the public in 3 new cities, now 14 total
content:
Fred Lambert
| Sep 1 2026 - 8:22 am PT
Waymo opened its driverless ride-hailing service to the general public in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa on Monday, bringing the Alphabet-owned company to 14 US cities.
Tens of thousands of people in each market had already signed up before the doors opened, and Waymo says it will let them in gradually over the coming weeks.
This isn’t the first time these three cities have shown up in a Waymo announcement. We reported in July that Waymo had
flipped Las Vegas to fully driverless and lined up Denver, San Diego, and Tampa as the next markets
. Back then, the service was still limited to employees and invited guests.
Now anyone can hail a ride. Riders in Denver and San Diego are getting Waymo’s new Zeekr-built vehicle, the roomier minivan-style platform running the company’s next-generation Waymo Driver, while the fleet fills out over the coming months.
Waymo has launched commercial service in seven new cities since March 2025, and it’s doing all of this while pushing toward a stated goal of 1 million paid rides a week by the end of the year. In May, the company
expanded its coverage area by more than 20% to over 1,400 square miles
, and in August it
won California approval to operate across 18 counties
The company leaned on its safety record for the rollout, saying its vehicles have been involved in 94% fewer serious-injury crashes than human drivers over the miles it has driven. To be fair, Waymo’s service mainly operates in lower-speed areas.
“From coast to coast, we’re focused on making everyday transportation safer, easier, and more accessible,” said Suzanne Philion, Waymo’s chief marketing officer.
Local officials showed up for the launch. Colorado Governor Jared Polis tied it to air quality, saying “Waymo’s launch helps us achieve cleaner air sooner,” and Tampa Mayor Jane Castor called it “another effective – and exciting – way to get around.” Waymo also worked with AARP Florida and the San Diego chapter of the National Federation of the Blind on accessibility ahead of the launch.
Tampa is where it gets interesting
One of these three cities isn’t like the others. Tampa is now a market where Waymo and Tesla are both running paid, “driverless” ride services at the same time.
added Tampa and Orlando to its Robotaxi service in July
, but the comparison isn’t close. Tesla’s active fleet is extremely limited, and its own Q2 chart
showed the service’s growth going flat
even as the company insisted it was expanding. Waymo is showing up in the same city with no one in the driver’s seat and tens of thousands of people already on the list.
Electrek’s Take
It does feel like Waymo is seriously scaling now. Adding three metros at once, with tens of thousands pre-signed in each, and now 14 cities total. Waymo isn’t running a pilot anymore. It’s running a business, and it’s compounding.
The Tampa overlap is the clearest scoreboard we’ve had. Tesla has spent two years promising that its camera-only approach would let it scale robotaxis faster and cheaper than anyone. Instead, it’s the one still babysitting a couple dozen cars with remote monitoring, while Waymo drops a fully driverless, public service into the same Florida market and moves on to the next one. The gap isn’t closing. It’s widening.
None of this means Waymo has won. The Zeekr-built vehicle needs to prove it can be produced at the volume a million weekly rides demands, and the unit economics of a hardware-heavy sensor stack across a growing but still limited market are still an open question.

title: 超2.3GWh！楚能新能源等6企储能订单集中落地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期储能市场订单及项目签约持续落地，楚能新能源、库博能源、蜂巢能源等企业相继获得储能订单，覆盖电芯供应、储能系统及EPC等业务。
楚能签署多项合作协议，获1.5GWh电芯订单
8月25日至27日，在南美智慧能源展上，楚能新能源与运达、Intermepro、ION Energy、JSN Energia四家企业签署合作协议，进一步拓展巴西、阿根廷等拉美市场。
8月25日，楚能与阿根廷Intermepro签署谅解备忘录，双方将围绕美洲区本地仓储、物流、现场交付、调试及售后服务等环节展开更紧密的协同，服务范围覆盖美国、波多黎各、墨西哥、中美洲及南美洲。
同日，楚能与巴西ION Energy签署谅解备忘录。双方将依托ION Energy在巴西本土的系统集成及运维能力，共同拓展农业灌溉、工商业用电等储能应用市场。
8月26日，楚能新能源与运达能源科技集团签署1.5GWh电芯框架协议。根据协议，运达在巴伊亚州卡马萨里建设了首个海外储能工厂，设计年产能1.5GWh，楚能将作为电芯核心供应商，服务运达巴西本地化制造基地，共同打造拉美本地储能产业链协同生态。
8月27日，楚能新能源与巴西JSN Energia签署谅解备忘录，双方围绕储能设备销售展开合作，共同拓展巴西大型储能及工商业储能市场。
库博能源助力捷克120MWh储能项目投运
近日，捷克利普尼采（Lipnice）57MW/120MWh电池储能项目正式商业投运。库博能源（Cubenergy）为该项目独家储能系统供应商，提供全套电池储能系统及核心技术支持。
项目位于捷克索科洛夫地区，由SUAS GROUP与EIF投资集团联合打造，总投资约4亿捷克克朗，储能规模为57MW/120MWh，配套配置144个储能电池柜、18套PCS及9套一体式箱变设备，采用库博能源FlexCombo电池储能系统。
蜂巢能源供货贵州80MWh工商储项目并网
8月25日，贵州瓮安80MWh工商业储能项目完成并网。蜂巢能源为项目提供16台5.16MWh短刀液冷储能集装箱系统，总容量约80MWh。
项目位于贵州省黔南布依族苗族自治州瓮安县，主要服务当地工业用电需求。项目共部署16套蜂巢能源5.16MWh短刀液冷储能集装箱系统，采用短刀叠片电芯、液冷温控等技术方案。
拓嘉新能源320kWh储能系统落地赞比亚
近日，拓嘉新能源一套320kWh储能系统在赞比亚项目现场投入运行并实现发电，进一步拓展非洲储能市场。
该项目采用两簇160kWh储能电池系统，总容量320kWh，搭配125kW锦浪逆变器。系统可与光伏协同运行，将白天多余电能储存，并根据负载需求进行放电，实现电能灵活调度。
陕西中昊电气集团签约独立储能项目
8月28日，陕西中昊电气集团与山东嘉阳新能源科技有限公司签署沂源县大张庄镇嘉阳200MW/382.5MWh独立储能项目合同，合同总金额约5.2亿元。
项目总规模为200MW/382.5MWh，其中包括190MW/380MWh磷酸铁锂电池储能系统和10MW/2.5MWh飞轮储能系统，同时配套建设220kV升压站、送出线路及附属道路。
此次项目采用电化学储能与飞轮储能组合方案，陕西中昊电气集团将参与项目EPC合作实施，服务范围覆盖储能系统及相关配套设施建设。
尚方能源签约240MWh独立储能项目
8月21日，北京尚方智慧清洁能源有限公司与上海怡云智慧能源有限公司、横琴华通金融租赁有限公司签署怡云60MW/240MWh独立储能项目合作协议。
项目位于上海市奉贤区，规划建设规模为60MW/240MWh，占地约19亩，采用磷酸铁锂和半固态电池两种技术路线，其中磷酸铁锂储能系统规模为35MW/140MWh，半固态电池储能系统规模为25MW/100MWh，并配套建设110kV升压站。
此次项目采用EPC总承包模式，尚方能源负责项目勘察设计、设备材料采购、建筑安装、调试试验、涉网试验、电力外线协调及竣工验收等工作。

title: 近1GW！晶科/通威/华晟/弘元新签组件订单一览
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期晶科、通威、华晟、弘元绿能相继斩获海外及国内订单，覆盖大型地面电站、工商业分布式等应用场景。
晶科连续斩获290MW海外组件订单
近日，晶科能源连续签署多项海外组件供货协议，项目覆盖保加利亚、希腊及肯尼亚市场，累计订单规模超过286MW。
其中，晶科能源与保加利亚项目方签署110.28MW高效组件供货协议，产品全部采用飞虎系列N型双面组件，用于保加利亚东南部大型地面电站建设。
与此同时，晶科能源与希腊可再生能源开发商签署176.14MW高效组件供货协议，同样全部采用飞虎系列N型高效双面组件，主要用于希腊中部大型地面电站建设。
除大型地面电站项目外，晶科能源飞虎3组件还入选肯尼亚私营医疗领域光伏项目。该项目由Cytek与Redington Green Energy作为独家供应商，联合肯尼亚城乡私营医院协会（RUPHA）推进，计划覆盖肯尼亚全国780余家私营医院，首阶段覆盖100家医院，单家医院平均配置约40kWp光伏系统及80kWh储能系统。
通威净界防积灰组件首批发运，订单超50MW
近日，通威净界防积灰组件在通威太阳能科技盐城基地完成首批发运，首批订单规模超过50MW。目前，相关产品正陆续发往江西振业新能源、安徽中浩能源电力等分布式战略合作伙伴。
据悉，截至目前已有16MW完成项目发运，产品将应用于河北某污水处理厂、赣州某工商业屋顶项目，主要面向污水处理、制造等高粉尘工商业应用场景。
通威净界防积灰组件采用短A面全包裹防积灰边框设计，并搭配双玻结构，以减少边框积灰、积水带来的发电损失及运维压力。此次首批产品完成发运，标志着该产品正式进入规模化市场应用阶段。
华晟新能源获缅甸13.7MW组件订单
近日，华晟新能源获得缅甸直通市光伏项目13.7MW组件订单，采购方为HB Vantage，项目全部采用华晟新能源Himalaya PLUS高效异质结组件，计划于8月底完成交付。
此次订单也是Himalaya PLUS继海外首单后再次实现海外项目落地，进一步拓展华晟新能源在东南亚市场的组件业务。
弘元绿色中标准格尔旗600MW光伏项目
8月25日，内蒙古准格尔旗光之源600MW光伏项目光伏组件设备采购项目中标候选人公示，弘元绿能为第一中标候选人，投标报价约5.04亿元，投标单价0.698元/W。
根据招标公告，该项目计划采购N型单晶硅双面双玻光伏组件722.61MW，单块组件正面功率为725W。
按照计划，项目组件交货时间为2026年8月15日至10月25日。

title: 阳光电源、比亚迪等4企半年业绩盘点：储能海外收入成亮点
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，阳光电源、比亚迪、中创新航、禾迈股份披露2026年半年报，储能行业整体呈现增量扩容、出海提速、营收结构优化的趋势。
业务端，头部企业储能主业占比提升，阳光电源储能收入占比首次突破50%，成为第一大业务；禾迈股份储能收入占比达78.29%，储能成为其核心营收支柱。出海成为重要增长主线，比亚迪、禾迈股份海外营收占比分别突破52%、66%。
图：2026年上半年储能企业业绩(亿元,%)
阳光电源：储能系统收入占比50%
8月28日，阳光电源发布公告，披露2026年半年度业绩情况。今年上半年，阳光电源实现营收309.12亿元，同比下降28.99%；归母净利润52.59亿元，同比下降32.01%；扣非净利润42.75亿元，同比下降42.96%。
报告显示，2026年上半年，阳光电源储能系统发货量达到25GWh，较去年同期增加约5.5GWh。但是，值得关注的是，同期的储能系统实现收入154.56亿元，同比下降13.18%；毛利率为32.43%，同比下降7.49%。
图：阳光电源营业收入整体情况图源：企业公告
上半年，阳光电源储能系统上半年发货量同比增长28%，储能系统收入占阳光电源营收的比重首次达到50%，正式超过光伏逆变器业务，成为阳光电源第一大收入来源。
目前，阳光电源已在全球设立七大研发中心、四大制造基地，加码布局欧洲、美洲、亚太、中东非、中国市场，已在海外建设了超30家分支机构。其中，海外光伏逆变器产能已达50GW。
比亚迪：海外营收占比超52%
8月28日，比亚迪发布半年报。2026年上半年，比亚迪实现营收3448.15亿元，同比下降7.13%；归母净利润123.25亿元，同比下降20.54%；扣非净利润123.73亿元，同比下降9.02%。
储能业务方面，比亚迪年报显示其储能系统2026年上半年出货量位居全球第一，产品进入110多个国家和地区，覆盖源网侧储能、工商业储能、户用储能和AIDC算力储能等场景。
上半年，比亚迪与阿联酋可再生能源企业Masdar签署11.275GWh储能供货协议；智利Elena 3.5GWh光储电站投入运行。
值得关注的是，集邦光储观察发现，此次半年报中一个非常重要的结构性变化，上半年海外市场贡献了比亚迪一半以上营收。
财报披露，2026年上半年比亚迪境外营业收入1812.68亿元，上年同期为1353.58亿元，同比增长33.92%，境外收入占总营收比重达到52.57%。
中创新航：上半年净利润同比增长102.2%
8月28日，中创新航披露2026年中期业绩报告。上半年，中创新航实现营收270.84亿元，同比增长65.0%，实现期内利润人民币15.23亿元，同比增长102.2%。
报告期内，中创新航收入增长主要是由于集团新客户、新应用场景拓展，以及新产品在乘用、商用、储能等领域持续上量，业务规模持续增长。
从收入结构来看：动力电池的销售收入为165.06亿元，占总收入的60.9%，同比增长54.8%，主要由于销量快速增长。储能系统产品及其他的收入为105.79亿元，占39.1%，同比增长83.8%，增长主要是由于持续开拓储能系统产品业务领域。
在储能领域，中创新航电池出货量持续增长，海外装机量持续提升，新一代「至久」600Ah+储能长循环大电芯完成规模化量产交付，绿电直连、零碳城市等新业务布局与AIDC高倍率产品开发均取得突破。电力储能方面，将持续加强与国电投在集团层级的深度合作，持续深化与华电、大唐、三峡等央企场景合作。
禾迈股份：储能收入占比78.29%
8月29日，禾迈股份发布2026年半年报，2026年上半年，禾迈股份实现营收约为17.80亿元，同比增长77.09%；实现归母净利润约为-1.64亿元，同比下降1107.86%；扣非净利润为-1.78亿元，同比下降1887.25%。
禾迈股份在财报中披露，营收同比增长主要系报告期内优化产品结构，储能项目业务规模扩大所致。利润总额同比减少主要系公司加大人才储备、增加研发和市场投入，以及汇率波动影响汇兑损益所致。归母净利润及扣非净利润同比大幅下降，主要系销售产品结构变更且受汇率影响较大，同时公司加大人才储备、增加市场投入所致。具体如下：

title: 隆基/爱旭/弘元披露2026年上半年业绩
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近日，隆基绿能、爱旭股份、弘元绿能相继披露2026年半年度报告。受行业供需矛盾及国内需求回落影响，三家企业上半年均面临盈利压力。
8月30日，隆基绿能披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入270.45亿元，同比下降17.58%；归母净利润亏损36.84亿元，扣非净利润为亏损40.32亿元。
隆基绿能表示，2026年上半年光伏行业供需矛盾持续突出，仍处于深度调整期，国内终端需求阶段性回落，带动公司硅片、组件产品国内销量下降。同时，行业供需失衡导致开工率不足、产品毛利率持续处于低位，叠加一季度银价上涨、联营企业投资损失以及人民币升值带来的汇兑损失等因素，公司业绩承压。
出货量方面，2026年上半年隆基绿能实现硅片出货量48.91GW，其中对外销售18.98GW；组件出货量29.93GW；电池对外销量0.86GW。
虽国内市场需求回落，但公司在海外市场业务保持增长。报告期内实现组件海外销量同比增长超过26%，海外收入占比提升至65%以上；其中，美洲、欧洲及亚太市场组件销量分别同比增长超过36%、34%和20%。同时，在欧洲、拉美、东南亚以及巴基斯坦、阿联酋等重点市场取得领先地位。
BC组件成为公司上半年出货增长的重要支撑。报告期内，隆基绿能BC组件销量达到19.55GW，同比增长125%，占组件出货量的比例提升至65%以上；BC组件国内集采入围规模超过10GW，同时海外高端市场订单快速放量。
技术方面，报告期内公司自研的ACM技术实现GW级电池、组件规模化投产，可使BC电池量产转换效率提升0.2%至0.3%，目前已开始规模化交付。此外，公司自主研发的晶硅—钙钛矿叠层太阳电池经欧洲太阳能测试机构认证，转换效率达到35.5%。
与此同时，隆基绿能进一步推进光储业务布局。2026年以来，公司推出覆盖大型电站、工商业及离网微网等场景的光储一体化产品，上半年储能累计签单量超过3GWh，并在德国、意大利、芬兰等地多个项目实现并网。
8月28日，爱旭股份披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入91.83亿元，同比增长8.72%；归母净利润亏损7.54亿元，扣非净利润亏损8.51亿元。
2026年上半年，爱旭股份N型ABC组件出货量达到9.39GW，较2025年下半年环比增长50%以上，其中第二季度出货量较第一季度增长约30%，公司ABC组件业务收入占营业总收入的79%。
海外市场成为ABC组件出货增长的重要支撑。报告期内，公司组件海外销售量占比超过55%，同比增长超过90%。公司主要拓展欧洲、日韩、澳新等市场，同时向中东、非洲等集中式市场延伸。截至2026年6月底，公司已在全球79个国家建立近百家一级渠道伙伴。
订单方面，爱旭股份表示，自2026年初以来新签订单保持增长，滚动在手订单超过10GW，客户意向采购规模已持续超过公司现有产能交付能力。与此同时，公司ABC组件在法国、芬兰、捷克、埃及、罗马尼亚等海外市场获得集中式项目，并在国内获得大唐、电建、华电、京能、浙能等央国企集采订单。
8月30日，弘元绿能披露2026年半年度报告。报告期内，公司实现营业收入42.83亿元，同比增长32.65%，主要系积极拓展电池片及组件销售市场所致。其中，归母净利润为亏损6.79亿元，扣除非经常性损益后的净利润为亏损4.84亿元。
其中，硅片业务仍是公司亏损的重要来源之一。上半年，弘元新材实现营业收入17.18亿元，净利润亏损5.69亿元；弘元徐州主要从事硅片、电池片业务，实现营业收入29.99亿元，净利润4563.58万元。
在组件业务方面，弘元绿能持续推进产品升级。报告期内，公司江阴基地HT 3.0高效四分片组件正式下线并实现批量出货，该产品基于TOPCon 3.0电池平台。同时，公司已进入国家能源投资集团、国家电投、中国能建、中国电建等央国企供应链体系，并中标中国华电、中国电建集团贵州工程公司等项目。
产能建设方面，截至6月底，公司在建工程账面价值8.46亿元，其中包括徐州25GW单晶硅金刚线切片及14GW高效晶硅电池项目、包头年产10GW单晶硅拉晶项目以及16GW太阳能光伏组件项目等。

title: Here's Our Best Look Yet At The Volkswagen ID.4 Successor
content:
A boxier face, normal door handles, updated underpinnings and a new (but familiar) name are all coming to VW’s electric SUV.
Photo by:
Autogefühl
12:44pm ET
This is the successor to the Volkswagen ID.4 and ID.5, which looks a lot more like a Tiguan.
YouTuber Autogefühl got a peek at a lightly camouflaged model.
It's part of VW's plan to make its EVs better align with its gas car offerings, in style and naming.
The Volkswagen ID.4 and its coupe-like brother, the ID.5, have proven popular, with over 900,000 units delivered combined since the 2021 debut through February of this year. However, since its launch, VW has had a change of heart about making its EVs look quirky and futuristic. So the ID.4 is getting a major makeover to more closely resemble the combustion-powered Tiguan.
We’ve known this is coming for a while, but now we've gotten our first glimpse of what the heavily revised,
Tiguan-ized ID.4
will look like. German YouTuber Autogefühl posted a short video showcasing the vehicle’s exterior and interior design, both still partly hidden by camouflage.
The exterior gets a wrap that hides some of the new details, but we can clearly make out the boxier, more upright Tiguan-like shape. It looks nothing like the current ID.4, and the same goes for the rear, which has also been completely reimagined, adopting the same squared-off style as the front and most of the current VW lineup.
Thomas doesn’t show the side of the vehicle. But we can see that the door handles are now more conventional.
Volkswagen likely had to work within the same hard points as
the ID.4
but make the new model look completely different. Even with the camouflage, it looks like the manufacturer may have just pulled it off.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
We don’t get a look inside the new vehicle, but we expect a makeover there too. VW executives have spoken at length about
bringing more physical buttons
into its interiors. The new ID. Polo got a redesigned steering wheel with lots of actual buttons. Plus it features four window switches by the driver for all four windows, rather than the frustrating capacitive setup found on the current ID.4.
This heavily revised ID.4 is part of VW’s broader move away from making its EVs look like a separate, futuristic family. Its new electric models are being styled much more like their combustion-powered counterparts and
borrowing their names
The ID.2all concept
, for instance, became the more conventionally styled
ID. Polo
. The IG Metall auto workers union in Germany has
the new model will be called the ID. Tiguan, but VW hasn't confirmed that.
Volkswagen is expected to unveil this electric SUV in full on October 9, when we’ll learn whether the technical overhaul is as extensive as the visual one, and if the ID.4 name will be dropped.

title: Honda And Nissan Team Up To Make The Brains Of Future Cars
content:
Honda And Nissan Team Up To Make The Brains Of Future Cars
The companies will develop common hardware and software for vehicles coming in 2029 and beyond.
- Nissan and Honda's merger collapsed last year, but they're working together in a new way.
- The two companies announced they would develop common computers and operating systems for software-defined vehicles.
- Vehicles on these new platforms should roll out starting in 2029, the companies said on Monday.
It's finally happening: Honda and Nissan are officially joining forces. The Japanese automakers nearly merged, but those negotiations fell through last year. Now the companies have announced concrete plans to work together on software-defined vehicles, as they both work to combat what's coming out of China and Silicon Valley.
On Monday, the companies said they have entered into a joint development agreement to standardize core electronic control units (ECUs), vehicle operating systems, middleware, and vehicle control software for future vehicles. Specifically, the ECUs include high-performance main computers and zonal ECUs that control specific areas of the vehicle.
"Recognizing the need to strengthen competitiveness through faster development cycles and more efficient investment, the two companies have conducted extensive studies on potential collaboration in the software domain," the companies said in a press release.
While Honda's press release doesn't explicitly mention EVs, it says that the new ECUs and vehicle operating systems will underpin SDVs coming in 2029 and beyond. The press release also says that both brands will continue to explore technologies that "accelerate progress toward carbon neutrality."
The partnership may be welcome news for two automakers that have struggled as of late—especially in EVs. Honda recently posted its first annual loss in its history as a public company and blamed, in part, fast-moving, high-tech competition in China. Honda's Prologue is following the Acura ZDX out the door in the U.S., leaving the company without an EV in the country. Nissan's global sales have fallen for six of the last seven fiscal years. It still has the Leaf but the Ariya died, too. Both brands working together may help them catch up to competitors like Hyundai, Toyota, and General Motors—not to mention BYD and Tesla.
Perhaps more importantly, this helps Honda and Nissan take on the growing Chinese market, where having good software-defined technology is crucial. This partnership might not be the last such team-up we see in Japan either. Toyota recently said that Japanese automakers should partner up if they want to survive against Chinese carmakers.

title: Nissan's 'Home Run' Hybrid SUV Arrives In November To Rival Toyota RAV4, Honda CR-V
content:
Nissan's 'Home Run' Hybrid SUV Arrives In November To Rival Toyota RAV4, Honda CR-V
The Japanese automaker has missed out on the hybrid sales boom. That could soon change with the Rogue e:Power.
- The Nissan Rogue e:Power arrives this November to rival the Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V Hybrid.
- The Japanese automaker has moved up its launch timeline twice.
- Hybrid sales are booming in the U.S. due to high gas prices.
Despite being an early electric vehicle pioneer with the first-generation Leaf in 2010, Nissan has been notably absent from the powertrain Americans are gravitating toward most: hybrids. The Japanese automaker does offer the Rogue plug-in hybrid in the U.S., but that’s basically a rebadged Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV. Now, Nissan is preparing to launch the fourth-generation Rogue in the U.S., with the hybrid arriving first, followed by non-hybrid versions.
The automaker has fast-tracked the launch of the Rogue e:Power twice, bringing its U.S. arrival forward from mid-2027 to January and now to November of this year, Automotive News reported Monday. Nissan told InsideEVs at the New York Auto Show in April of this year that the Rogue hybrid was expected to arrive in late 2026.
The urgency is stemming from Nissan’s need to capitalize on the booming demand for hybrids and finally take on a segment that Toyota and Honda have dominated for years. Hybrid sales have surged this year as higher gas prices, fueled due to the U.S. war in Iran, have pushed more buyers toward more efficient vehicles. Sales were already growing before the conflict, but the war has provided a fresh boost.
“We believe this hybrid is a home run, so we did everything we could to bring it earlier,” Tiago Castro, the senior vice president of U.S. marketing and sales at Nissan told Automotive News.
Gallery: 2027 Nissan Rogue
The Rogue e:Power will have a different hybrid setup than the systems used by its Japanese rivals. Unlike Honda’s parallel-hybrid setup or Toyota’s power-split system, the Rogue will use a pure series-hybrid configuration. In other words, it will drive much like an EV, with electric motors powering the wheels, while the gas engine keeps the battery charged or directly feeds power to the electric motors. There’s no plug-in port, so the battery is charged solely by the engine and regenerative braking.
Automakers also call these extended-range electric vehicles,(EREVs) but the Rogue e:Power is not to be confused with the big battery plug-in vehicles that are on track to launch in the U.S. soon, like the Jeep Grand Wagoneer EREV or the next-generation Ford F-150 Lightning.
The Rogue’s 1.5-liter turbocharged three-cylinder engine acts primarily as a generator, feeding a relatively small 2-kilowatt-hour battery that supplies power to the electric motors. The wheels are driven exclusively by those motors. The gas engine’s job is simply to power the battery and the e-motors and keep the system operating in its most efficient range.
"The driving dynamics, the packaging, the acceleration, it's all electric," Ponz Pandikuthira, chief product and planning officer at Nissan Americas, told InsideEVs in an interview earlier this year. "The internal combustion engine never drives the wheels."
Nissan expects the Rogue e:Power to deliver upwards of 40 miles per gallon, which would put it roughly on par with the Toyota RAV4 and slightly ahead of the Honda CR-V Hybrid. If Nissan can deliver on that promise while retaining the Rogue’s familiar practicality, it could have a compelling alternative to the established hybrid heavyweights.
The Rogue already has plenty of momentum in the U.S. Sales rose 24% year over year in the first six months of this year, reaching 135,970 units. That still puts it well behind the CR-V, which sold 226,114 units during the same period, with hybrids accounting for 55% of those sales. Toyota sold 153,955 RAV4s over the same period, a 35% year-over-year decline. That drop is largely due to the sixth gen RAV4’s production ramp up. The RAV4 is now offered exclusively as a hybrid or a plug-in hybrid.
Despite being a latecomer to the hybrid SUV party, the timing couldn’t have been better for the Rogue e:Power’s arrival. Now whether it can close the gap with the RAV4 and CR-V will be the real test starting in November.
