title: Grenergy completes $475 million sale of Chilean solar-storage project - Energy Storage
content: Grenergy has completed the sale of its 272 MW solar and 1.1 GWh battery storage project in Chile to CVC DIF for an enterprise value of $475 million. The transaction was first announced in September 2025, when Grenergy disclosed a value of up to $475 million and said the transfer was conditional on the asset entering operation. At the time, Gabriela was under construction and expected to reach commercial operation in the first half of 2026. The facility combines 272 MW of solar PV capacity with 1,100 MWh of battery storage. Grenergy announced its energization in February, paving the way for commissioning and completion of the sale. Gabriela is also backed by a 15-year hybrid power purchase agreement (PPA). Construction was financed through a $324 million green loan provided by BNP Paribas, Natixis, Société Générale, Scotiabank, SMBC, Bank of America, BBVA, JPMorgan, KfW IPEX, Rabobank and ICO. Under the terms of the transaction, Grenergy will continue providing operations and maintenance (O&M) services for the assets for five years. Oasis de Atacama is Grenergy’s hybrid solar and storage platform in northern Chile, comprising multiple PV plants paired with battery systems. The company currently plans up to 2.5 GW of solar and 14 GWh of storage across several phases, including Gabriela, Víctor Jara, Quillagua and Elena, with long-term power supply contracts associated with some of the facilities. The Gabriela sale follows Grenergy’s December 2024 sale to ContourGlobal, a KKR-backed company, of the Víctor Jara and Quillagua I and II phases. That transaction covered 451 MW of solar and 2.5 GWh of storage and had a value of up to $962 million. Grenergy said the two transactions together represent around 25% of the Oasis de Atacama platform and have a combined enterprise value of nearly $1.5 billion. The divestments form part of Grenergy’s asset rotation strategy under its 2026-2028 strategic plan, which targets €800 million in proceeds from asset sales during the period. The company updated the plan in May, increasing its planned investment through 2028 to €3.7 billion. It also announced expansions of its Oasis platforms in Chile and the development of Iberian Oasis in Spain. Together, the platforms are expected to reach 5 GW of solar and 22 GWh of storage. title: Cratering oil use in China shows the death spiral that could end oil
content:
Chinese oil use dropped drastically in Q2 of this year, leading to an overall drop in emissions for the country. That alone is a big deal – but the potential effects of the world’s second-largest oil consumer rapidly passing peak oil could have massive effects on the world’s oil markets.
For the past few years, it has seemed that China was in the midst of a plateau in both emissions and oil use. Nobody was ready to declare that it had passed the peak of either, wondering whether the graphs might turn upwards from here. But with new Q2 numbers showing a drastic drop in oil use and a consequent drop in total CO2 emissions, it might be that time.
New numbers released by the National Bureau of Statistics of China and analyzed by Carbon Brief tell the tale: in Q2, overall oil use dropped by a whopping 9% in China, and an even more incredible 16% for transportation.
Combined, the drop in oil use was enough to pull Chinese CO2 emissions down by 1%. This may seem like a minor drop, but it happened despite an uptick in coal use. Usually, when countries reach peak emissions, it’s due to dropping coal use, and this is the first instance Carbon Brief could find where lower oil use, rather than coal, was the driver of a reduction in emissions.
It would be tempting to blame the drop in transportation emissions to a disrupted global oil market which has fallen victim to an ill-considered war of choice, spiking energy prices globally, especially for Far East nations. As oil prices spike, perhaps Chinese consumers are using their vehicles less, causing only a temporary drop in oil use.
But transportation levels have in fact increased in China. Part of this has been due to increased public transit, which could be a result of Chinese people being priced out of private gas-powered transit.
But a large portion is due to the boom in electric vehicles and collapse in ICE vehicle sales in the country, meaning transportation is simply getting more efficient in the world’s largest auto market. Not only are more EVs on the road, but EVs are being used more than non-EVs (partially due to a rise in electric taxis).
In fact, in the first six months of this year, EVs in China displaced more oil than all of the UK used in the same period. A massive rise in electric heavy truck sales was responsible for the largest part of this oil displacement.
Huge numbers like a 9% drop in oil use and 16% drop in transportation oil use are generally considered anomalous, the type of drop that is usually an outlier. These are Q2 2020-level numbers – when COVID was at its strongest, and nations around the world dropped oil use and emissions significantly.
China seems to be past peak oil consumption
So we wouldn’t necessarily expect to see these numbers every quarter from here on out, but it does seem like we’ve finally passed peak oil consumption in China.
This is a milestone which many have expected to come for years now. Sinopec, China’s state-owned oil company, predicted in 2024 that Chinese oil demand would peak before 2027, but last week said that actually, it probably already peaked in 2025.
“Next year, even if the US-Iran conflict eases up, things might recover, but it won’t hit last year’s level. So it’s very likely demand peaked last year.”
-Hou Qijun, Chairman, Sinopec
Going forward, this could be a huge influence on oil markets. China’s high level of electrification (and its release of its petroleum reserve) has already been credited for “quietly saving the world” from what could have been a much larger oil shock related to the ill-advised war in Iran.
So having the world’s second-largest oil consumer (the US consumes more oil than China, despite having only 1/4 of China’s population) suddenly stop using nearly as much oil is the sort of shock that gets oil traders to stand up and notice (or to stick their fingers in their ears and shout “I’m not listening”).
China’s CO2 and oil peaks come much earlier than the US’ did
If oil use and CO2 trendlines continue as they have, this means that China will have peaked its per capita CO2 emissions at about a third of the US’ peak. US CO2 emissions peaked at around 22 tons per capita, a number reached in the 70s and nearly reached again in 2000. Meanwhile, Chinese per capita emissions are currently just over 8 tons per capita.
In terms of total emissions, China is still ahead – that’s because China has 4 times as many people living in it as the US does, and because the US has been gradually reducing emissions since the early 2000s, whereas China is later in its development curve.
And in terms of oil usage, China’s peak consumption was 17.35M barrels/day in 2025. Meanwhile, USA’s was 19.4M in 2025, and previously peaked at 20.53M in 2005. This means that every American is currently using more than 4x as much oil as every Chinese person, along with making almost 2x as much CO2 (USA’s current per capita emissions sit around 14 tons per year).
So if China truly has passed the peak for both of these numbers, then it has done so at much lower levels than the US did. Showing that a country can develop into a major world power while still pulling the arc of its CO2 emissions in the right direction.
How this could trigger the death spiral that can end oil
It’s a trend that I saw in Norway in 2023, where massive EV adoption led to cratering motor fuel sales. I declared (with a very similar headline as today’s article, sorry) that this trend showed “the death spiral that can end oil,” and this is how that could work.
While many have mentioned that higher oil prices lead to increased demand for EVs and decreased consumer demand for oil (as we are seeing now, in China and elsewhere, with phrases like “permanent demand destruction” being bandied about), relatively less attention has ben put on the supply side of this equation, where low oil prices reduce the incentive to explore and drill for oil.
If oil demand goes down, and oil prices go down, it suddenly becomes less economical to open new wells, and potentially even uneconomical to operate existing oil extraction operations in some areas. This, then, can cause a larger positive environmental effect than increased EV use does, because it means that oil projects will be cancelled or won’t be proposed in the first place, and that oil will stay in the ground where it absolutely, positively, objectively needs to remain.
That previous article was about Norway, which has been the world standout in electrification, but at the end of the day is a tiny country which wasn’t going to affect global oil consumption that much.
But China is anything but a tiny country. China is the sort of country that can really change world oil markets. And it’s not far behind Norway in terms of EV sales percentage – and way ahead in total number of EVs and total displaced oil use.
Oil crashes have happened for less. The 2014 crash in oil prices, wherein oil lost about half of its value, was blamed on an oversupply of roughly 2 million barrels a day globally. Meanwhile, China’s 9% drop in oil consumption in Q2 represents about 1.5 million barrels a day worth of avoided oil use. That’s just one country, in which about 25% of cars on the road are electric (up from around 18% this time last year). Just wait until that number continues to go up in China, and everywhere else too.
We’re not seeing a global supply glut right now because supply is constrained by the war in Iran, which has allowed oil companies to opportunistically put up record profits. But going forward, if the disruption from that war ends and supply normalizes, it’s going to have to normalize at a lower supply number and/or a lower price. Either of these are good news for the environment, and could hopefully trigger cascading effects (like making oil companies rethink drilling in the arctic).
An actual free market – one where externalities are priced – would help this happen
It is a possibility that a future where oil prices drop significantly will result in a return to oil as a cheaper-than-present form of energy. But that could be avoided by ending the subsidy, in the amount of trillions of dollars globally per year, that fossil fuels get by not having to pay the full costs they impose on society.

Drove a friend's EV ~ 5 years ago and was instantly hooked. Getting back into my gas-mobile felt like going back in time. Haven't bought gas in over three years and don't miss it for a second.
The superior drive in an EV is worth it alone. Saving $16,000 in gas (after paying for electricity), using my own solar to power, reduced CO2, significantly reduced maintenance are all icing.
In the past two weeks I've driven two rental cars on work trips. An old-fashioned gas car and an old-fashioned hybrid gas car. Absolutely terrible by comparison: noisy, slow, inefficient.
This could be solved by finally properly pricing oil globally. In countries that have implemented a realistic carbon price, pollution has dropped and societal wellness has increased. The IMF estimates that pollution pricing would increase world GDP by eliminating market inefficiencies.
In contrast, the artificially low gasoline costs in the US (yes, US gasoline prices are still artificially low, even at today’s “high” prices) work to buoy consumer oil demand. Removing the ~$750 billion in yearly implicit subsidies received by the fossil fuel industry in the US alone would help ensure that fair market conditions could prevail, and consumers would have a clear choice about what the better and cleaner option is.
And if we finally let the market work freely, after more than a century of both direct and implicit oil subsidies that have coddled this lying, deadly industry, we could finally see it spiral into the oblivion it deserves.

title: EVs outsell petrol in Australia for the first time, led by China
content:
Fred Lambert
| Sep 3 2026 - 5:33 am PT
Electric cars outsold petrol cars in Australia for the first time in August. Battery-electric vehicles hit 27,078 sales, or 24.9% of the new-car market, ahead of both petrol (25,824) and diesel (23,608).
The Tesla Model Y topped every model on sale. But look past it, and Australia’s EV record is almost entirely a Chinese one.
An EV record, and combustion becomes the minority
BEV sales were up 171% year-over-year, according to VFACTS and Electric Vehicle Council data. Add hybrids and plug-in hybrids, and electrified vehicles took 51.8% of the market. It’s the first month combustion-only cars have been in the minority in Australia.
Europe crossed that line last year, when
EVs outsold petrol across the EU even as Tesla’s sales collapsed
. Australia is now on the same path, and getting there faster.
The overall market grew 4.9% to 108,760 vehicles. EVs did the heavy lifting.
The eight best-selling EVs are all built in China
Here’s what the record actually looks like, model by model:
Australia’s best-selling EVs, August 2026. Source: VFACTS / Electric Vehicle Council data via The Driven.
Seven of the eight top sellers are Chinese brands: BYD, Geely, Zeekr, and Chery’s Jaecoo. The BYD Sealion 7 alone moved 2,213 units and finished sixth across the entire market, ahead of household nameplates. The Geely EX5 jumped more than 385% year-over-year.
The other two are Tesla’s Model Y and Model 3. Except they’re not really exceptions. Tesla builds every right-hand-drive car it sells in Australia at Giga Shanghai, so all eight of the country’s best-selling EVs rolled off a Chinese production line.
We flagged this shift in July, when
Australia’s seven best-selling EVs were already all Chinese, even Tesla’s
. A month later, it’s the full top eight.
Tesla wins the month, but BYD wins on breadth
The Model Y sold 6,414 units, up 176% year-over-year, and it was Tesla’s third monthly sales win of 2026. As a brand, Tesla climbed to third with 7,685 sales, up 163%.
BYD sat right above it in second with 8,231, up 68.8%, and it got there with a far wider lineup than Tesla’s two-car range.
BYD outsold Tesla 10-to-1 in Australia back in January
. The gap has closed as Tesla recovered, but the Chinese brand is still ahead.
Toyota led all brands with 19,712 sales, down 5.2%. The legacy volume brands, Toyota, Mazda and Kia, are all sliding while the Chinese EV makers post double- and triple-digit growth.
Electrek’s Take
This is a real milestone. But this is a Chinese EV boom. Seven of the eight top sellers are Chinese brands. The other two, the Teslas, are built in Shanghai. So the cars powering Australia’s EV record are, without exception, made in China. Toyota, Mazda, and Kia are going backward while BYD, Geely, and Zeekr add new nameplates every few months and take their share.
Australia has almost no tariffs on Chinese EVs, unlike the US or the EU. That’s why Australians get cheap, capable EVs, and why adoption is moving this fast. It also makes Australia the clearest preview anywhere of what an open, tariff-free EV market actually produces.
Opening up to Chinese EVs will result in a faster phase-out of combustion engines. Autralia is the proof.

title: Ford wants to sell 100,000 Fathoms in the $30k EV truck's first year
content:
Ford Fathom
Jameson Dow
| Sep 3 2026 - 2:30 am PT
Ford Fathom EV pickup prototype (Source: Jim Farley)
Ford has set a goal to sell 100,000 of its upcoming Fathom electric truck in the model’s first year of sales, which would put it among the best-selling EVs in America, and the best-selling non-Tesla EV.
Ford has been preparing its Fathom electric truck for a few years now, even establishing a “skunkworks” development center to revolutionize its manufacturing methods. (We
took a tour of the design studio
this May, but didn’t get to see the truck… yet).
As 2027 creeps closer, Ford has been drip-dripping more information about the truck. We learned in July that the truck would have a NACS port, as it was
spied at a Tesla Supercharger
. Then we learned last month that the truck would
be called Fathom and start just under $30k
And just this week, we got
a closer look
at the Fathom driving in some (pretty ugly) camouflage in the streets of Las Vegas. The truck was supposedly doing hot weather testing in the area, and decided to take a detour through the city.
get a tiny glimpse of the truck in similar camouflage when we routed Ford’s Long Beach facility, but nobody was allowed to use cameras on that tour)
But now another piece of information comes via WSJ, which cites “people familiar with the matter” who say that Ford has set an internal goal of 100,000 vehicles sold in the first year.
This would immediately make the Fathom a best-seller. As of yet, no automaker has sold more than 100,000 units of a single model in a single year in the US except for Tesla. So the Fathom would be in third place (assuming other sales numbers stay similar), and would add a new digit that no non-Tesla automaker has yet added to its sales tally.
Ford has previously had a
best-selling electric pickup in the US
, the Ford Lightning. But that truck never reached nearly the sales numbers that Ford
originally expected
, partially due to a much higher launch price than was
originally promised
. Despite
outselling the Tesla Cybertruck
, it was eventually canceled.
But the company says it has learned a lot of lessons since then, primarily around keeping costs down. Given that it plans to start production in Q1 2027, just a few months from now, hopefully the recently-announced starting price will remain firm this time around, instead of
catching everyone by surprise
like last time.
And if it does, it will immediately compete on price with the
other most affordable EV in America
, the refreshed Chevy Bolt (and may take wind out of the sails of the
upcoming $25k Slate truck
). If Ford can pull it off, it will be an impressive price… but we’ll have to see it and drive it first to tell you how much of a value the final product will be.

title: Kia turns its electric van into a mobile grocery store for free food delivery for those in need
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 3 2026 - 7:47 am PT
Kia’s electric van really can do it all. The
was converted into a mobile grocery store to deliver food and other necessities to those in need for free.
Kia PV5 becomes a grocery store on wheels
The PV5 is about the closest thing to a real-life transformer. Kia’s electric van comes in a variety of top hats customized for business and personal use.
Beyond the standard Passenger, Cargo, and Chassis Cab body styles, Kia has introduced several unique conversion models, including a refrigerated van, mobile gaming rig, AI patrol vehicle, and even a light camper.
Most recently, Kia converted the PV5 into a mobile grocery store to deliver food in rural parts of Korea, where fresh food and groceries are scarce.
As part of its new “Move to You” initiative, Kia used its electric van to provide free food delivery and connect residents with care services.
The project started in Uiseong-gun, South Korea, where the population is rapidly aging and access to fresh food is becoming more difficult. Although the region is roughly twice the size of Seoul, its population is only about 47,000.
(Source: Hyundai Motor Group)
To make matters worse, over 50% of residents are projected to be over the age of 65, meaning one out of every two who live there is considered elderly.
The rapid population decline has caused local shops, hospitals, schools, and infrastructure to disappear. Residents now have to travel hours just to get a carton of eggs.
Kia converted the PV5 into a mobile grocery store to deliver fresh food and other convenience items to those in need. Based on the PV5 Cargo, Kia modified the electric van with flexible racks and a portable refrigerator.
Kia converts the PV5 into a mobile grocery store (Source: Hyundai Motor Group)
The setup enables Kia to deliver groceries and other daily necessities to the homes of the elderly in the region every week.
Kia’s electric van can conquer the winding, narrow farm roads of the mountainous region, where access was previously limited.
Currently, Kia has eight PV5 mobile grocery stores in operation or being prepared for deployment, delivering food to about 70 villages every week. Residents come together to catch up and help each other find necessary items.
Park Hyang-sook, one of the local residents who uses the program, said it’s especially helpful because “Many elderly people find it difficult to place phone orders,” adding that “Move to You is convenient because a car comes right to the front of the community center on designated days.”
Kia is also partnering with public health centers and various welfare programs to establish an integrated care system that will go beyond food delivery to include health exams and more.
While Kia plans to continue expanding the service, it’s also considering using the larger PV7 electric van (
set to debut this month
), which will offer more space once it’s launched.

title: PG&E expands V2X program with Tesla, Volvo, Nissan and $17K incentives
content:
Bidirectional Charging
Fred Lambert
| Sep 3 2026 - 7:48 am PT
Massachusetts Vehicle to-Everything (V2X) Demonstration program Photo: The Mobility House
PG&E just expanded its Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program, adding EVs from Tesla, Kia, Volvo, Polestar, and Nissan and opening up as much as $17,000 in incentives to turn a car into home backup power.
The California utility brought in Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex as approved partners, and drivers now have until June 30, 2027 to enroll.
New vehicles, new chargers
V2X lets a compatible EV work as a mobile battery. With a bidirectional charger, you can pull electricity out of the car to run your house during an outage or push it back to the grid when demand spikes, and shave your energy bill along the way.
Until now, PG&E’s Eligible Products List covered Ford, Tesla, Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac. The expansion adds several new vehicle-and-charger combinations:
Nissan Leaf (2018-2025) with a DCBel Ara charger. Volvo EX90 (2025) with a DCBel Ara charger. Polestar 3 (2025) with a DCBel Ara charger. Kia EV9 (2024 and newer) and Kia EV6 (2025 and newer), both with the Wallbox Quasar 2. PG&E also folded in three more GM models: the 2027 Chevrolet Bolt, the Cadillac Celestiq, and the Cadillac Escalade IQL.
“This expansion is all about choice,” said David Almeida, Director of Clean Energy Transportation at PG&E. He said broadening the mix of eligible vehicles and chargers helps customers “turn their EV into a home backup and a grid asset.”
The incentives, stacked
Here’s where the money is. Residential customers get $2,500 upfront, or $3,000 if they live in a disadvantaged community, plus a $1,500 Early Adopter Incentive for the first 250 people to enroll. The new DCBEL and Wallbox combinations also qualify for up to $13,000 in additional funding through a California Energy Commission grant, subject to eligibility.
Stack those and an early adopter is looking at roughly $17,000. That’s real money against hardware that still runs thousands of dollars, and it’s the whole point of a program like this.
Commercial customers get their own tier: $2,500 to $3,000 for a 3-phase bidirectional charger under 50 kW, and $4,500 to $5,000 for one at 50 kW or above.
V2X is finally crawling out of the pilot phase
The idea of using an EV to power a house isn’t new. The Nissan Leaf has technically been a vehicle-to-grid car for more than a decade through CHAdeMO, and it’s a little funny that it’s only now landing on PG&E’s approved list. The hardware and the utility programs are what took forever.
That’s been changing fast in California. We covered PG&E’s
original V2X pilot with GM Energy
last year, and in April the
Cybertruck became the first AC vehicle-to-grid asset in the state through PG&E
. Tesla’s Powershare is still Cybertruck-only for now. A
2024 California law
is also pushing automakers toward making bidirectional capability standard.
PG&E is running the same play on the commercial side. It’s backed
electric school bus fleets in Fremont, Oakland, and San Francisco
that can feed the grid. The utility notes that more than 90% of the nation’s 500,000 school buses still burn diesel or gas, putting out over 8.4 million tons of greenhouse gases a year.
Electrek’s Take
Is V2X finally scaling? It looks like it. This is one of the most comprehensive programs I’ve seen to date.
What it lacked was compatible cars, affordable bidirectional chargers, and utilities willing to pay for the service. California is knocking down all three at once, and adding the Leaf, EV9, EX90, and Polestar 3 widens the funnel to cars people are actually buying.
I am in favor of the idea that if you buy an EV, you can do what you want with its battery pack, including using it for backup power or to service the grid for revenue.
If you’re powering an EV at home, pairing it with rooftop solar is how you get the fuel cost close to zero, and a bidirectional setup like this lets that car back up your house on top of it. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. title: Rivian’s futuristic ALSO e-bike may be at its ultimate delay
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 3 2026 - 7:16 am PT
Rivian spin-off ALSO is pushing back the delivery timeline for its highly anticipated TM-B electric bike yet again, with reservation holders for the flagship Launch Edition now being told to expect their bikes to arrive by early November at the latest.
In a new update sent to customers,
says its Launch Edition bikes are “now shipping”, with deliveries expected to arrive “in waves between now and early November.”
Social media
is astir
with questions about what that “now shipping” label really means, with some asking if bikes have been delivered to real customers outside of influencers, family, friends, and others connected to the company.
The announcement follows the
most recent delay last month
, when the company had already pushed back deliveries to mid-September, i.e., a few days from now.
Now it sounds like this could be the ultimate delay – assuming the bikes do actually land in driveways during the next two months.
ALSO recently opened up regular orders to its reservation holders, but the company now says those bikes won’t begin shipping until after the Launch Edition units. Deliveries for reservation holders are expected to begin in early November and continue through the end of the year, depending on when the order was placed and which configuration was selected.
That appears to mark yet another slip in the TM-B’s delivery timeline.
ALSO says it will begin sending customers more specific timing updates throughout September and plans to update its online ordering system with delivery estimates based on individual bike configurations.
While the company hasn’t shared many details about the sources of the delays, they’ve attempted to assuage customers by sharing encouraging progress, including adding images to their website showing bikes already in production at the company’s Asian factory.
The TM-B is an unusual and ambitious e-bike, featuring the company’s proprietary DreamRide drivetrain, a large integrated display, modular accessories, and a design that blurs the line between conventional e-bike and electric moped.
The biggest headline feature is likely the drive-by-wire design, which replaces traditional direct linkage from the pedal cranks to the wheel with an electronic alternative comprised of a generator powered by the pedals and a motor nearby then that powers the rear wheel through a belt drive.
Those innovative and high-tech features have helped make the TM-B one of the more interesting new electric two-wheelers in years. But for reservation holders who have been waiting since last year, the wait just got a little longer.
As ALSO Chief Commercial Officer Ben Steele put it in the update, “I’m confident your TM-B will be worth the wait.”

title: This new anti-theft device can keep your e-bike protected for up to a year straight
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 3 2026 - 2:48 am PT
E-bike theft is one of those problems where a good lock is only half the battle. Since no physical lock can ever give you a 100% guarantee of safety, if a thief actually gets away with your bike, knowing where it went can suddenly become a lot more important.
Now connected e-bike specialist Comodule has unveiled its latest solution, known as Astra, and one of its most interesting tricks is the ability to keep tracking an e-bike for up to 12 months – even when the bike is sitting in storage.
There are a lot of e-bike trackers out there, and while simpler versions like AirTags may have long battery life, solid GPS trackers that can pinpoint a bike’s location can rarely last more than a month or two without a recharge. That might be fine for everyday use, but bikes that are left in storage or just bikes that keep being moved after a theft are prime examples where longer tracking periods without necessary recharges are critical.
And Astra sounds like it could provide just that solution.
is Comodule’s next-generation IoT hardware designed to be built directly into e-bikes, giving manufacturers a way to add a host of connected features ranging from live location tracking to smart locking and even electronic immobilization.
The company is currently offering demonstrations to manufacturers developing model year 2028 e-bikes.
Perhaps the biggest upgrade for riders worried about theft, beyond the impressive 12-month battery life, is Astra’s improved location technology. In addition to conventional satellite positioning, the system adds Wi-Fi Locate, which Comodule says improves positioning accuracy in dense cities, indoors, and other locations where GNSS reception can struggle.
That could be particularly useful in an actual theft scenario. GPS trackers are great when a stolen bike is sitting outside, but things get trickier when it disappears into an apartment building, warehouse, or parking garage. In those cases, knowing the rough X/Y coordinates aren’t enough, and more precise location data becomes the key to actually located the bike.
Astra also upgrades to Cat-1bis cellular connectivity, designed to provide more reliable connections indoors, in dense urban environments, and in remote locations.
Then there’s that 12-month figure, something of a headline feature. Comodule says smarter power management allows bikes equipped with Astra to remain trackable during long storage periods for up to a year. That doesn’t necessarily mean your bike can be ridden around for a year without charging – Astra normally draws power from the e-bike’s electrical system – but it means the security hardware can remain useful even when the bike itself has been sitting unused for an extended period.
And tracking is only part of the security package.
Depending on how a manufacturer integrates Astra, riders can access the bike’s live location and status through an app, use smart locking functions, receive alarm notifications, share the bike’s location or digital access, and even electronically immobilize the bike. Comodule also supports digital bike passports, recovery services, and integrations that can provide insurance benefits.
The module itself is smaller and more power efficient than Comodule’s previous hardware, while CAN connectivity allows it to communicate with an e-bike’s drive system and other smart components. Manufacturers can either use Comodule’s branded app and back-end platform or integrate Astra into their own software using the company’s API and SDK tools.
This isn’t Comodule’s first rodeo, either. The Estonia-based company says its technology has already connected more than 850,000 e-bikes, e-scooters, and other light electric vehicles over the last 11 years. While the name doesn’t carry as much recognition with everyday riders, Comodule is the quiet IoT engine powering the connectivity in major brands throughout the e-bike, e-scooter, and e-moto industry.
Of course, none of this makes a good physical lock obsolete. But I’ve long been a fan of the idea that the best e-bike security comes in layers: make the bike hard to steal in the first place with a
couple of good quality locks
, make the owner immediately aware when someone messes with it, and make the bike easy to locate – and ideally useless to the thief – if they still manage to get away with it.
Astra looks designed to tackle those latter layers better than ever.

title: 当AIDC遇上电网，光储巨头们看到了什么？
content:
AI大模型爆发，先砸中的不是芯片，而是电网。GW级算力数据中心的突发性负载，对现有电力系统的物理稳定性构成了前所未有的冲击。
与此同时，全球贸易壁垒持续抬升，行业从单纯的规模与价格竞争，迈入算电协同与深度本地化的新阶段，光储产业已全面驶入下半场。
在近期举办的2026新能源及新型电力系统先进技术论坛上，TÜV莱茵、阳光电源、上能电气、三晶电气、优优绿能等产业代表性企业，围绕未来3—5年光储产业的核心发展方向展开了深入讨论。
综合各方观点，集邦光储观察梳理出三大演进趋势：AI算力倒逼供电架构重构、出海模式从产品销售升级为标准输出、国内商业闭环亟待机制改革。光储产业的竞争维度，正从制造能力转向标准的定义权。
AI算力倒逼电网重构，算电协同打开新增市场
算力数据中心（AIDC）的高功率密度与突发性负载，对现有电力系统的物理稳定性带来了前所未有的冲击。
阳光电源AIDC电源事业部总裁张迪指出，在电网发生剧烈扰动时，算力中心若缺少故障穿越能力，服务器电源会因自保机制瞬间切断连接。GW级算力负载瞬间离网所带来的甩负荷效应，会对电网稳定造成严重冲击。
这一矛盾促使美洲NERC、PJM规范及国内电网，将具备故障穿越能力列为算力中心的硬性准入标准。尽管电网侧并未对算力中心做“强制配储”的硬性规定，但在“东数西算”节点与高可靠性诉求下，绿电直连与“源网荷储”一体化的算电协同微电网正加速成为行业标配。
储能的定位由此改变，不再只承担削峰填谷，更是保障算力运行与电网稳定的关键缓冲设施。
在供电架构上，阳光电源张迪表示，阳光电源正推进35kV交流直降整流至800V直流的固态变压器方案预研，并结合800V高压直流机柜电源与板载电源的协同预研，打通从发电侧到芯片的“源到芯”全栈架构。
优优绿能副总经理陈玉龙补充道，优优绿能正将其成熟的800V充电模块平台技术平移至AIDC领域，通过高压直流模块支撑系统集成商，将AIDC打造成公司的第二增长曲线。
然而，技术路线的快速迭代正遭遇检测与标准滞后的现实瓶颈。TÜV莱茵大中华区太阳能与商业产品服务总经理董斌指出，储能与AIDC交织，产品的快速迭代与标准制定滞后的矛盾日益凸显。
更为严峻的是检测资源的短缺，测试平台需求功率从1兆瓦提升至10兆瓦，测试范围也从单电芯热失控扩展至集装箱级大规模燃烧，短期内资质平台建设难度极高。未来AIDC的认证体系需从单一设备的电气安全与EMC，跨越至信息安全、功能安全、电池安全、消防防爆以及系统可用性等多维评估。
全球化迈入本地化2.0，从轻资产运营到标准规则输出
随着拉美、南亚等市场关税政策收紧，及欧美本土化制造门槛提高，传统的国内生产、销往全球的出海模式已难以为继。
三晶电气董事长欧阳家淦研判，本土化运营会是未来很长一段时间的大趋势，但在中东等地区自建工厂重资产投入风险很高。企业可行的思路是打造代工等轻资产制造模式，例如采用本地代工、精简产品SKU、统一产品技术平台，适配不同国家小批量、高效率的本地化生产需求。
此外，除了供应链形态的轻量化与本地化，出海升级还体现在从卖产品转变到标准话语权的建设。行业真正的竞争壁垒，在于掌握规则话语权。
上能电气副总经理孙建峰强调，中东、中亚等弱电网区域对构网型技术需求迫切，实际上，海外市场有需求但缺乏标准。国内头部企业正通过与当地企业沟通，共同制定标准，将成熟的技术方案转化为招投标规范，再逐步推动上升为当地国家技术标准，实现技术标准的输出。
TÜV莱茵董斌对此补充道，当前新兴市场存在标准体系不成熟的现状，TÜV莱茵的做法就是协助企业快速梳理过往相应的标准，并引导当地监管机构通过IEC标准转换或借鉴欧美先进标准理念，制定符合当地情况的并网标准等。
国内光储商业闭环临近，市场化交易是关键变量
把视角转回国内，光伏经济性已经十分突出，储能在“十四五”后期实现规模增长，但工商业光储项目普遍面临盈利测算不稳定的现实困境。
三晶电气欧阳家淦强调，当前国内工商业储能主要依赖固定的分时电价峰谷套利，这种静态机制难以实时反映电力供需的动态波动，限制了光储系统在实时调节中的多元价值释放。
欧阳家淦指出，随着新能源渗透率持续提升，电力现货市场与实时动态电价机制有望在未来几年内加速普及。一旦实时电价信号与市场化交易全面打通，光伏、储能及虚拟电厂的多重收益闭环将被激活，国内工商业储能也将迈入高质量发展阶段。
面对AI算力带来的电力新需求，国内光储产业拥有全球最完整的产业链，市场反应也足够灵敏。光储下半场的角逐，扩充产能已不再是绝对优势。对复合应用场景的物理理解、跨国资源的轻资产整合，以及参与行业标准制定的能力，才是各家企业比拼的核心。

title: 德业股份、上能电气等4企2026半年度储能业绩速览
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近日，德业股份、上能电气、南都电源、珠海冠宇等4企相继披露2026年半年报。各家储能企业经营情况分化，呈现出业绩高增、增收不增利、大幅亏损等不同的发展态势。
德业股份：半年营收首次超过100亿
8月26日，德业股份披露2026年半年度报告。2026年上半年，德业股份实现营收106.41亿元，同比增长92.23%；归母净利润27.17亿元，同比增长78.53%；扣非净利润25.70亿元，同比增长75.81%。
据悉，这是德业股份半年营收首次超过100亿元。关于营业收入的变动原因，德业在半年报中表示，这主要是因为市场需求增长，储能电池包业务规模快速扩大，逆变器业务保持增长带来的业绩增长。
2026年上半年，德业逆变器和储能电池包产品合计贡献了90%以上的收入，其中，储能电池包收入同比增长244.12%。具体如下：
逆变器产品实现营收51.32亿元，占公司主营业务收入的48.36%，同比增长94.09%。储能电池包产品实现营收48.94亿元，占公司主营业务收入46.12%，同比增长244.12%。2026年上半年德业总计销售115.30万台逆变器，其中户用储能逆变器57.03万台，工商储6.05万台。
德业表示，公司逆变器产品在户用光伏及储能安装商群体中积累的客户资源和渠道网络，为储能电池包产品的导入提供了销售基础。已采购公司逆变器的存量客户，在配置或升级储能系统时，对公司储能电池包的接受度和选配率相对较高。
在系统集成方面，德业逆变器与储能电池包在通信协议、能量管理策略和安全保护机制方面完成系统适配，能够为终端用户提供即插即用的系统解决方案，降低安装调试成本，提升系统运行稳定性。
上能电气：海外营收占比超六成
8月27日，上能电气发布2026年中报。上半年，上能电气营收为28.58亿元，同比增长30.84%；归母净利润为2.16亿元，同比增长7.96%；扣非净利润为1.98亿元，同比增长1.98%。
从产品结构来看，上能电气上半年光伏业务营收为21.98亿元，占总营收的76.90%；储能业务营收为5.99亿元，占比20.95%。
分地区来看，上半年，中国大陆营收11.28亿元，占比39.48%；海外营收（包含中国港澳台）为17.30亿元，占比60.52%，占据超五分之三的比例。
ST南都：在手订单未能按期履约执行
8月29日，ST南都发布2026年中报。上半年，南都电源营收为16.99亿元，同比下降56.71%；归母净利润为-11.11亿元，同比下降378.10%；扣非净利润-11.16亿元，同比下降346.53%。
南都电源表示，报告期内，公司因内控被出具否定意见而实施其他风险警示，叠加持续的流动资金紧张、供应链衔接不畅等因素，导致公司生产排产受限、项目交付能力不足，大量在手订单未能按期履约执行，整体业务开展受阻，营收规模同比大幅收缩。
为应对当前经营困境、优化经营质量，南都电源基于现有资源现状主动调整经营策略，进行人员及业务结构性优化，优先保障核心业务生产交付。
同时，公司对2025年度内部控制审计报告否定意见所涉事项予以高度重视，成立整改工作小组，组织各相关部门推进整改工作，争取尽快申请撤销公司股票其他风险警示。
珠海冠宇：半年度营收增长20.16%
8月26日，珠海冠宇披露半年报。2026年上半年，珠海冠宇营收为73.27亿元，同比增长20.16%；归母净利润-2.03亿元，同比减少273.94%；扣非净利润为-3.01亿元，同比减少767.70%。
对于净利润业绩的原因，珠海冠宇表示，主要系受美元兑人民币汇率持续下行影响，汇兑损失显着增加，导致财务费用大幅增长。
另外，珠海冠宇生产成本因原材料价格上涨并处于高位而持续承压，而下游客户同时面临存储芯片等元器件价格攀升的压力，进一步加大成本传导阻力，使得公司产品销售价格的调整相较于原材料价格的上涨存在一定的滞后性。此外，电池产品出口退税率下调，进一步增加外销成本。
上半年，珠海冠宇主营动力及储能类业务的子公司浙江冠宇实现总营业收入为16.20亿元，同比增长66.54%。为了更好地适应市场的快速变化，公司适时调整动力和储能电池项目的建设进度，严格控制产能释放节奏。
报告披露，珠海冠宇将延缓浙江年产10GWh锂离子动力电池二期项目、德阳一期25GWh动力电池生产项目建设进度，避免过度投资导致资源浪费，并有助于公司更加灵活地应对市场需求的变化，保持健康的财务状况和发展势头。后续将根据市场需求，综合评估项目的实施条件后再决定是否恢复建设。

title: Enapter wins electrolyzer order from US drone manufacturer | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
The order comprises units from its 4.1 series of AEM electrolyzers and is scheduled for delivery in the fourth quarter of 2026.
The AEM modules will be integrated into mobile, all-terrain refueling systems that generate hydrogen directly at the point of operation from water and solar power, without a grid connection. This approach removes the need to transport and store hydrogen in large compressed gas cylinders, which has been among the main obstacles to operating hydrogen-powered drones in remote areas.
According to Enapter, hydrogen propulsion gives drones significantly longer flight and mission times compared with battery-electric propulsion, along with rapid refueling capability.
The order is structured as a pilot project. Enapter said it opens up a field of application in which the modular design of AEM technology is well suited, citing a compact footprint, robust operation, and the ability to scale hydrogen production by adding further modules.
Dr Jürgen Laakmann, Chief Executive Officer of Enapter , said: “This order underlines how far the applications of our technology reach beyond classic industrial use. In this case hydrogen is generated flexibly where it is needed – free of complex supply chains and of any fuel logistics. That is exactly what our modular, low-maintenance AEM technology was built for. We see considerable growth potential in mobile refuelling solutions and are pleased to be developing this field together with a technologically leading customer.”
Enapter said the market for drones with long range and long flight times is growing strongly worldwide, and that the pilot project opens up a field of application with scalable demand for the company.

title: Bentley’s First EV Will Be Its Quickest Car. But It Doesn’t Matter
content:
Bentley’s First EV Will Be Its Quickest Car. But It Doesn’t Matter
The Torcal will out-accelerate every Bentley before it, but Crewe says the numbers matter less than how effortlessly it delivers them.
- The Torcal will be Bentley’s quickest, most powerful car, but its output will remain below 1,000 hp.
- It shares its 800-volt platform, 113-kWh battery—and possibly more—with the Porsche Cayenne Electric.
- Bentley says comfort and effortless power, not headline numbers, will distinguish the Torcal from its Porsche sibling.
Bentleys have traditionally felt understressed with ample performance in reserve thanks to their powerful engines. As Bentley moves into the electric age, it wants to imbue its EVs with the same kind of character. In fact, electric power may suit Bentley’s character even better than combustion both in terms of effortlessness and outright performance.
The Crewe-based manufacturer has just revealed that its first EV, the Torcal SUV, will be its most powerful and quickest-accelerating vehicle ever. That means it will sprint even faster than the 771-horsepower Continental GT Speed, which can hit 62 mph (100 km/h) from a standstill in 3.1 seconds.
We don’t know how much quicker the Torcal will be, but we don’t have long to wait since it will officially be unveiled on September 23. A lot is riding on its shoulders, since it may be Bentley’s only EV until 2030, after the manufacturer reportedly abandoned plans to build four out of five EVs.
But as quick as the Torcal will be, Bentley spends little time celebrating this record. In the press release accompanying these teaser shots, it says the Torcal’s performance has been engineered “within the limits of comfort.” Its defining quality is supposed to be how its power arrives: instantly, seamlessly, like in any performance EV, but in this case also without disturbing the people inside.
However, occupants will certainly feel the combined forces from its strong acceleration and cornering ability. The Torcal is built on the same 800-volt platform as the Porsche Cayenne Electric, sharing its 119-inch wheelbase and113-kilowatt-hour battery pack with 108 kWh of usable capacity.
The Cayenne EV delivers bonkers acceleration, especially in Turbo trim with a combined output of 1,139 hp and 1,106 lb-ft (1,500 Nm), sending the 5,831-pound (2,645-kg) SUV to 62 mph in 2.5 seconds. It was independently tested to 60 mph (96 km/h), which it reached in a face-bending 2.1 seconds.
However, the Torcal won’t be quite that quick. Speaking to Evo on the sidelines of a prototype ride event, Torcal product line director Martin Page said Bentley had avoided chasing figures for their own sake and that “there won’t be a model with 1000 horsepower.”
Page confirmed the Torcal would have over 370 miles of WLTP range and more than 838 hp and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm), but didn't give exact figures.
Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric configuration
Comparing photos of camouflaged Torcal prototypes with the already released Cayenne, it appears their connection may run deeper than a shared platform. From the side, the shape of their greenhouse appears virtually identical, as do the doors and the side windows. We’ll have to see both side by side in person to really tell if that's so, but the Torcal may be more of a Porsche than Bentley would like to admit.
It looks like the Torcal has different front and rear ends, and Bentley has changed the overhangs to give it a longer tail and shorter nose, making it look more distinct and more like a traditional Bentley.
Inside, the Torcal will share the Cayenne’s unusual Flow Display, but the rest of the interior will be typical Bentley. It will be available with the finest leathers but also Merino wool upholstery, as well as wood veneer made from walnut offcuts and recycled paper. Its artificial acceleration soundtrack was created from orchestral instruments rather than sampled engine (or motor) noise.
Making an EV accelerate quickly is the easy part. We’ll have to wait and see how the UK manufacturer adopts and adapts the Cayenne EV’s bones and tunes the platform to deliver a distinctly Bentley experience. It needs to be calmer, richer, and more special in order to justify its predictably higher price tag than the Cayenne’s, which starts at $111,350 and goes up to $170,350 before you so much as look at the options list.

title: Ford Wants Its $30,000 EV Truck To Do Something Only Tesla Has Done
content:
Ford Wants Its $30,000 EV Truck To Do Something Only Tesla Has Done
Ford wants to sell 100,000 Fathom pickups in its first year. It won’t be easy.
- Ford has an ambitious sales plan with its affordable new EV pickup, the Fathom.
- The American automaker reportedly wants to sell over 100,000 units in the first year.
- No other car company except Tesla has ever managed such a performance with a single electric model.
Ford is shooting for the stars with its upcoming Fathom electric pickup truck. The American automaker wants to sell over 100,000 units of the affordable EV in its first year of production, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
So far in the U.S., only Tesla has managed to crack 100,000 units annually for an EV. Hitting that goal would quickly make the $30,000 pickup one of the country's top-selling electric models. Setting it signals that Ford is still serious about the EV game, despite canceling the F-150 Lightning along with projects that were in development for years. Whether or not customers will actually show up at dealerships and make this target a reality is still up in the air.
Ford Fathom Prototypes in Las Vegas
It will be a tall task. The end of the $7,500 EV tax credit about a year ago has dampened demand for EVs. Even before all the policy changes, growth in U.S. sales had slowed. As major automakers waded into the U.S. EV market over the last several years with ambitions of taking on Tesla, none of their products managed to come close to the EV leader's sales volumes. The best-selling EV not made by Elon Musk last year was the Chevy Equinox EV, which racked up some 58,000 sales.
Ford itself has overpromised and underdelivered before; at one point, it targeted annual F-150 Lightning production of 150,000 units. In its best year, the truck did about a fifth of that. Now Ford is betting that a lower price point and a new way of making EVs will allow it to crack the EV market like it never has before.
Ford is betting on a new EV platform for its $30,000 Fathom truck.
With the budget Fathom, set to kick off production in the fall of next year, the Blue Oval has reworked the way it makes electric vehicles specifically, and cars more broadly. The goal was to make the truck as cost-effective as possible, as opposed to the previous-generation EVs that the company struggled to turn a profit on.
The first model using Ford's new Universal Electric Vehicle platform, the truck will be produced using a novel assembly technique where the front, middle, and rear of the vehicle are built out on separate lines, then joined together at the end. Ford calls it an "assembly tree," rather than a typical "assembly line," and says it should make churning out EVs more efficient.
Following in the footsteps of Tesla, the carmaker has also employed the use of large castings to keep the number of individual parts as low as possible. The truck's electrical architecture has been developed from the ground up. It will be powered by lithium iron phosphate batteries, which are cheaper than high-nickel options and can be charged to 100% frequently without issue.
Jim Farley, Ford’s CEO, has said in the past that the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, which is one of the best-selling crossovers in the country. The company has always referred to the upcoming truck as being mid-sized, but people who have seen the prototypes up close have said that the Fathom is similar in size to the compact, gas-powered Maverick. The pickup will also be available with either rear-wheel drive or all-wheel drive, and the infotainment system will integrate Apple Maps natively–a first for the company.
Ford Fathom Prototypes in Las Vegas
There’s still a lot we don’t know about the Fathom, and Ford is still trickling out information without revealing anything big. We should learn more in the next few months as the truck gets closer to the streets; orders open up in early 2027, and the pickup will be made at Ford’s assembly plant in Louisville, Kentucky, where the Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair were built until last year. What's clear already is that Ford thinks it has a hit on its hands.

title: New Jersey Just Legalized Cheap Plug-In Balcony Solar Panels
content:
Under the new law, landlords and local governments can no longer block residents and tenants from installing plug-in solar panels.
Photo by:
Yuma Solar
5:26am ET
A fresh New Jersey law cuts red tape, enabling residents to legally install solar panels that plug directly into a household outlet.
The bill bars local governments and landlords from blocking residents and tenants from installing balcony solar systems.
The legislation, signed by Gov. Mikie Sherrill, empowers people to cut their monthly energy bills after minimal investment.
Another American state is making it legal to install cheap balcony solar systems that can lower energy bills. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill signed legislation this week that bars municipalities and landlords from restricting the installation of portable solar panels.
The law, which will go into effect six months from now, allows residents and tenants to install solar systems with a maximum power output of up to 1,200 watts without having to pay additional fees for installation or go through all sorts of approvals.
The legislation, which was approved unanimously in the Senate and Assembly in late June, is aimed at cutting residents’ power costs as electricity prices continue to climb across the state.
Landlords, homeowners associations, housing cooperatives, and similar entities must still be notified about the installation of a plug-in solar system 14 days in advance, and landlords are still allowed to restrict the placement and size of the solar units. However,
the new law
bars local governments from requiring licensing or approvals to install such systems.
“Balcony solar is the ultimate win-win,” said Gov. Mikie Sherrill (D) at a bill signing ceremony in Trenton. “It’s accessible, affordable, safe, and sustainable. These units cost a fraction as much as rooftop solar, but they can still shave up to $50 off the typical monthly bill.”
With a plug-in photovoltaic system, the solar panels are connected either to a microinverter or a bigger unit that also includes batteries for storage. The “brain” of the system is then plugged in directly into a household outlet, with the inverter making sure that no power is sent back to the grid when there’s an outage. That’s important for the safety of the linemen working to restore power for everyone affected.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Balcony solar systems, which are extremely popular in Germany, where over one million systems are online, require a much smaller initial investment compared to rooftop solar and a simpler installation. In New Jersey, for instance, the 1.2 kW limit means that two or three solar panels can be plugged into a compliant inverter, keeping costs down for apartment dwellers.
"Plug-in solar can save a family hundreds of dollars a year, every year, with no cost to the ratepayers,” said Hannah Birnbaum, Co-Founder and Chief of Advocacy at Permit Power. "Governor Sherrill has been going after energy costs since her first day in office, and this law hands families a tool they can use themselves, including the roughly 40 percent of New Jerseyans who rent or live in apartments and have never had a way to lower their own power bill."

title: Passenger Screens Are Everywhere. A Third Of Owners Never Even Use Them
content:
Passenger Screens Are Everywhere. A Third Of Owners Never Even Use Them
A new study shows that 35% of owners who bought a new car with a passenger screen have never even used it.
- More and more new cars are coming equipped with passenger screens.
- A new study shows that more than a third of owners have never actually used them.
- It turns out that while flashy features might help to sell cars, drivers just want under-the-radar tech that actually works.
Automakers have spent the better part of a decade turning the dashboard into something that rivals the television aisle at your local Costco. Tablet-sized infotainment screen! Actually, make it bigger. Not enough? Passenger screen! Might as well digitize the climate control, too. Still need more? Might as well just unify everything across the entire dash.
All of those screens are starting to feel a bit redundant—especially the passenger screen. In fact, according to a recent study by JD Power's 2026 U.S. Tech Experience Index study, a third of drivers who have a car equipped with a passenger screen have never even used it.
Yes, never. Not occasionally, not one time on a road trip. Never. In fact, only 6% of the JD Power's 68,084 owners surveyed who own a car with a passenger screen report that it gets used every time they drive it. We've seen Tesla remove hardware for similar reasons, yet these flashy screens still remain.
Oddly enough, infotainment systems with passenger screens also generate the most user complaints—21.3 problems per 100 vehicles. The results from JD Power show that these screens generated a high number of reported infotainment-related problems in its separate 2026 Initial Quality Study.
One other interesting point that the study calls out is that the boring, low-key tech—smart ignition, climate control, and driver preferences, to name a few—resulted in higher overall satisfaction ratings among drivers while also producing the fewest problems.
Even adding complexity to driver-assistance features moved the needle in the wrong direction for owners. For example, Level 2+ hands-free driver assistance generated lower overall experience and execution scores versus hands-on Level 2 systems. This might just speak to how comfortable drivers are with in-car tech, or it could reflect the real teething issues that come with adding complexity to the cars we use every day.
As for the screens, that's not to say they're completely useless. Having the ability for a passenger to control their own HVAC controls or watch a movie while on a long road trip can be valuable.
While they might not get used, display tech is a relatively cheap and easy way to dress up an otherwise bland dashboard and also make a car appear to be more tech-forward. But the message (or rather lack thereof) from owners is that screens don't make the car—consistent, predictable tech does.

title: Scout Reveals Two New Traveler SUV Concepts As Production Nears
content:
Scout Reveals Two New Traveler SUV Concepts As Production Nears
Each of the concepts show off both sides of the electric SUV: rugged and luxurious.
- Scout Motors revealed two new concepts of its debut vehicle, the Traveler SUV.
- Scout says customer deliveries will start in 2028.
- The company will lead with the extended-range version of the SUV due to high demand.
Scout Motors wants to show off the duality of its electric Traveler SUV with two new concepts: the Mountainside and the trail-ready concept. The former spotlights the SUV's refinement and comfy cabin, while the latter shows off its ability to get dirty. Both will make their debuts at the Jazz Aspen Snowmass Labor Day Experience jazz festival, for fans to see in person.
According to Scout, the Moutainside concept is supposed to be a "warm, refined interpretation" of the electric SUV. It has a cool, sophisticated looking Morning Dusk paint that's apparently a deep "charcoal-brown" with gold metallic flakes. Its 22-inch dish wheels are awesome, if a bit menacing. I'll never say no to a dish wheel, though.
The Scout Traveler Mountainside is a sophisticated SUV with high-end-looking wood trim.
Inside, the light brown leather combines with gray fabric and recycled walnut wood trim to make an interesting combo. It's luxurious but in a snow cabin kind of way. The intricately textured wood looks like a cork board from afar.
The trail-ready concept gets a Galvanized Steel paint, which is supposed to look like bare metal, but the roof is finished in a contrasting paint called Canvas. To prove how tough and capable it is, the trail-ready Traveler gets full-metal front and rear bumpers, an elevated roof rack with trail lights, an integrated front winch, and 18" black beadlock wheels with 35" off-road tires.
Scout's "trail-ready" concept is a rugged off-roader with 35-inch tires.
Its interior's Denim District design will make Jay Leno run for his wallet, and the brick-red leather adds a bit of spice. It's a much more aggressive model than the Mountainside but, again, these two concepts are designed to show off both of the Traveler's personalities.
Both of these Scout Traveler concepts look good, but that's no surprise—the Traveler is a good looking SUV. It walks that line between luxurious and rugged as well as anything from Land Rover, Lexus, and Rivian. Will Scout sell these concepts as packages when the Traveler finally goes on sale? That's unclear. But hopefully Scout will at least sell some of these features as options, like the bead lock wheels and cool roof rack.
Scout says initial production of the Traveler will start next year, with customer deliveries following in 2028. Owing to outsized demand compared with the EV variant, the company has said it'll kick things off with the range-extended Harvester trim of the Traveler. It pairs a four-cylinder generator with a 63-kilowatt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery pack and should deliver 500 miles of range.

title: The U.S. Is A Curbside Charging Laggard. San Francisco Wants To Change That.
content:
The U.S. Is A Curbside Charging Laggard. San Francisco Wants To Change That.
Only 100 curbside chargers will be installed by 2030, so not everyone will get a charger near their home.
- San Francisco wants to have 100 curbside public chargers by 2030.
- It's a win for people who live in apartments without home chargers.
- Residents can pitch the city to get a Level 2 charger on their block.
EVs may be perfect for city driving—but they aren't always perfect for city living. City-dwellers without a parking garage or driveway often need to rely on public plugs, which can be inconvenient or far away. Using DC fast chargers frequently can get expensive, too.
But having a Level 2 charger right on one's block could make electric car ownership a lot smoother. Which is why San Francisco is looking to grow its infrastructure to 100 public curbside EV chargers by 2030. And it's allowing residents to apply to get one on their street.
Compared with some European cities, for example, the U.S. is behind the curve on curbside charging. Much of the focus and investment in the States has been on roadside fast chargers. Those are important, but they're most valuable for long trips where charging quickly is paramount. With more Level 2 charging at the curb, cars could charge slowly for all those hours during which they're sitting unused.
London has tons of curbside chargers. Or consider Oslo, Norway; the world's EV capital is brimming with slower charging posts where people already park. (To be sure, the U.S. has the clear edge when it comes to detached homes with on-site parking, which is its own advantage in the EV transition.)
The San Francisco initiative, announced in late August, is called the Curbside Electric Vehicle Charging Permit program. It's been developed by the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Authority (SFMTA) for residents who don't have access to a private garage. The 100 chargers will be built and installed by qualified vendors, like Hetch Hetchy Power, PG&E, and CleanPowerSF. However, they'll be public chargers to be used on a first come, first serve basis, so even if you apply for one on your street and get it, that doesn't mean you'll always have access to it.
“Starting today, San Francisco has a clear process to bring accessible curbside charging to our residents. This program is a common-sense way to make it easier for San Franciscans to own an electric vehicle and help us achieve our climate goals together,” San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said in a press release.
This is the result of a pilot program from April 2025 that brought a few curbside chargers to the city. The year-long pilot informed the city about what EV drivers wanted, and what others needed to make the switch over to clean EVs. The answer was simple: more public charging.
It's Electric, a Brooklyn startup, installed San Francisco's first curbside chargers in April 2025.
“We heard from the community that one of the biggest barriers to wider EV ownership is the availability of charging stations. With this new program, we will be making it easier for people who rent or live in apartments and condos to charge their car," said SFMTA Director of Transportation, Julie Kirschbaum.
In addition to formal applications, San Franciscans can also use a feedback tool to recommend certain streets for public charging. It features a map of the city with a form to fill out, so the SFMTA can get an even better understanding of where chargers will be most useful.
New York, too, recently announced plans to add 600 curbside chargers across the city, on top of the 88 already in place. The new focus on curbside infrastructure comes as startups launch new hardware targeted towards those kinds of installations. It's Electric makes sleek bring-your-own-cord charging piles that it says are more simple to energize than other chargers. Voltpost specializes in solutions that bolt on to existing lamp posts.

title: Think Chinese Cars Aren't Safe? These New Crash Tests Say Otherwise
content:
Think Chinese Cars Aren't Safe? These New Crash Tests Say Otherwise
The Cupra Raval gets four stars, while its recently tested Chinese competition earns five.
- The Leapmotor B05, Aion UT, and Geely E2 all earned five stars in the latest Euro NCAP testing round.
- Volkswagen's Cupra Raval only earned four stars, but the score rises to five if an optional safety pack is purchased.
- Euro NCAP gave the Leapmotor and Aion lower safe driving scores because their touchscreen infotainment systems lack buttons.
Westerners have historically been skeptical of the quality and safety of Chinese cars. And the concern isn't entirely unwarranted, either. Just look at videos from the 2000s of cars like the Chery Amulet or Geely CK; these compact sedans failed miserably at crash tests. This perception has been a big black eye for Chinese brands that want to sell in Europe. But recent crash tests show that things are very different now.
Euro NCAP, the region's main vehicle-testing organization, on Wednesday released the test results for four new small electric cars, including three Chinese ones. The Geely EX2, Leapmotor B05, and Aion UT all earned five-star ratings. The Cupra Raval, the VW Group brand's take on the new Volkswagen ID. Polo, got four.
The star rating can be adjusted up or down, depending on other features that don’t necessarily have to do with the vehicle’s crash structure or deformation performance. The results also include accident avoidance. The Raval doesn’t have some of the standard crash avoidance features that come on the other cars, like forward traffic alert or adaptive cruise control. Euro NCAP did say that if an optional package of safety features is installed, it performs admirably and raises the overall score to five stars.
The EX2, B05, and UT all have those functions as standard, and they perform admirably. The Aion UT and Leapmotor B05’s crash avoidance scores of 74% and 77%, respectively, beat the Raval’s 72%. The Geely E2 matches the Cupra's with the option package.
It’s hard not to be impressed by the quality, design, or value of Chinese cars, especially for the prices they’re selling for. For example, the Geely E2 starts just under €20,000 (about $23,000), making it one of the cheapest new EVs on sale in Europe. These lower prices have caused some to wonder if these brands are cutting corners on safety or build quality. But the data shows otherwise.
This doesn’t mean that Chinese cars are perfect. Euro NCAP criticized both the B05 and UT for being too touchscreen-heavy when it came to vehicle functions. This is reflected in the safe driving score, a part of the overall test that measures driver and occupant monitoring software, as well as the ease of use for vehicle functions on the move. The Aion and Leapmotor scored only 66% in this category. The team liked that the Geely has a few more buttons for key functions in its infotainment interface than the others, boosting its safe driving score to 79%.
At home, the Chinese government has made safety and quality a bigger priority after years of lightning-fast car releases from dozens of brands. Top government agencies are now scrutinizing potentially problematic car designs—like the electronic door handles that were the subject of a massive recall—more intensely. Plus, they are mandating factory audits to ensure these quickly developed cars aren't cutting corners on safety.

title: Uber And Wayve Beat Waymo To London With UK’s First Robotaxi Service
content:
Uber And Wayve Beat Waymo To London With UK’s First Robotaxi Service
The first Ford Mustang Mach-E EVs fitted with Wayve’s autonomous driving tech can now be hailed in London on the Uber app.
- Uber and Wayve beat Waymo to the punch, launching the United Kingdom’s first public robotaxi service.
- The autonomous Ford Mustang Mach-E EVs can be hailed through the Uber app in London starting today.
- The cars can travel anywhere in the capital, apart from airports.
Uber is the first company to offer autonomous taxi rides in the United Kingdom, after the initial batch of driverless cabs hit the streets of London today, beating Waymo to the punch. Uber’s electric Ford Mustang Mach-E taxis are fitted with Wayve’s autonomous driving technology and can navigate anywhere in the city, except for airports, the ride-hailing company said.
It’s a big deal for the firm that has invested massively in several robotaxi endeavors, and it paves the way for other firms to offer autonomous cab rides in the region. That said, the initial rollout includes licensed private hire drivers sitting behind the steering wheel, acting as safety monitors.
Uber and Wayve's autonomous Ford Mustang Mach-E in London, UK
Wayve, the UK startup that has developed the hardware and software stacks for the vehicles, said that it’s starting with a small number of vehicles, and that the fleet will grow “thoughtfully” over time in line with rider demand, readiness, and regulation.
To ride in an autonomous Mustang Mach-E, Uber users who want to hail an UberX, Uber Electric, or Uber Comfort have to use their app as always. The app may match them with a Wayve ride at no extra cost, but there’s no guarantee that a robotaxi will pick them up. If one does show up in the app, riders have the option to accept or switch to a regular, non-AV ride before the car arrives.
To boost their chances of being matched with a Wayve robotaxi, Uber riders in London can go to the app’s Trip Preferences page under the settings section and opt in for AVs. Once the robotaxi arrives, the doors can be unlocked, and the trip can be started from the smartphone app.
The hardware setup fitted by Wayve to the Mustang Mach-E crossovers doesn’t use lidars and doesn’t require pre-made high-definition maps to navigate, much like Tesla’s vision-only approach. Wayve’s sensor stack includes radars, but the company said that the system was designed to be hardware agnostic, thanks to software that can run on whatever sensors and chips an automaker uses.
Like Tesla’s Robotaxi, Wayve’s AV2.0 system learns while driving, taking in new information with every trip and adapting to all of the weird and wonderful scenarios that can happen on the road.
In London, the electric Ford crossovers will be serviced by Uber in partnership with Otto Car, a UK fleet operator, while Wayve will manage the autonomous driving system.
Waymo, the biggest player in the American robotaxi game, said it will launch its driverless cab service in London by the end of the year.

title: HTC 推出 AI 智能眼镜 VIVE Eagle：主打隐私保护，499 美元起
content:
IT之家 9 月 3 日消息，HTC 今天（3 日）通过官方新闻稿宣布，最新 AI 智能眼镜 VIVE Eagle 正式登陆欧洲、北美和澳大利亚市场，主打时尚设计、AI 功能和隐私保护。VIVE AI 不仅支持语音和文字实时翻译，还能连接智能手机上的 AI 执行操作。
VIVE Eagle 配备蔡司镜片，太阳镜片提供 Cat3 UV400 防护，同时可选择蓝光防护镜片和变色镜片，也能配装处方镜片。
VIVE Eagle 将主打让用户摆脱屏幕和双手操作的限制。眼镜支持语音指令和可编程实体按键，无论在公园骑行还是探索陌生城市，用户都可以继续关注眼前环境，同时记录照片和视频。
隐私保护也是 VIVE Eagle 的一项核心设计。拍摄照片或视频时，LED 灯会常亮或闪烁，并根据环境自动调整亮度，确保周围人员能够看到。多传感器机制可以检测提示灯状态，如果 LED 灯被遮挡、损坏或失效，眼镜将无法拍摄；没有佩戴眼镜时，同样无法录像。用户还可以开启一项功能，让周围不希望入镜的人直接说出“停止拍摄”，VIVE Eagle 随后便会停止录像。
VIVE Eagle 配备 1200 万像素摄像头，最高支持 3K 视频和慢动作录像，同时利用电子防抖和 AI 优化照片与视频。
VIVE Eagle 还可以通过图像转文字翻译识别 70 多种语言，帮助用户快速理解眼前内容。
眼镜配备 4 个麦克风，其中 1 个为指向性麦克风，并结合降噪算法改善视频和通话时的收音效果。
VIVE Eagle 达到 IP54 防护等级，可以应对徒步、参观户外遗迹等使用场景。
VIVE Eagle 配备 4 GB 运行内存，集成多项生产力功能，其中实时翻译支持 96 种以上语言，可以帮助不同语言的用户直接交流。会议期间，用户可以专注于交流本身，再通过 VIVE Eagle 的录音功能获得详细会议笔记。
VIVE Eagle 还可以连接谷歌 Gemini，调用 Android 手机的原生功能；连接 iOS 设备时则可使用 Siri。
音频方面，VIVE Eagle 采用开放式定向扬声器，在增强低音和提供立体声的同时控制声音外泄。用户可以进行私人通话或听音乐，同时保持对周围环境的感知。
VIVE Eagle 连续使用时续航为 4 至 6 小时，待机时间可达 36 小时。眼镜采用磁吸触点充电设计，可以一边佩戴一边充电，无需像部分设备那样摘下后放入充电盒。
即日起，VIVE Eagle 正式通过 vive.com 和指定渠道开放订购，起售价为 499 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 3,361 元人民币）。

title: 《最终幻想 7：启示录》官宣 2027 年 4 月 8 日发售，最新实机演示公布
content:
感谢IT之家网友
x0oo0_0oo0x
9 月 3 日消息，在今天的 PlayStation State of Play 发布会上，Square Enix 公布了《最终幻想 7：启示录》的大量全新游戏实机内容，并确认游戏将于 2027 年 4 月 8 日登陆 PlayStation 5。
这款备受期待的动作 RPG 将成为《最终幻想 7》重制系列最终篇，为始于《最终幻想 7 重制版》、并在《最终幻想 7 重生》中延续的故事画上史诗般的句号。
《最终幻想 7：启示录》将打造一个规模前所未有的开放世界，玩家可以驾驶经典的“Highwind”飞艇，在广阔的星球上展开探索。探索方式并不局限于飞艇。玩家还可以再次依靠忠实的陆行鸟伙伴 Piko。这一次，Piko 不仅可以作为坐骑，还能直接参与战斗。随着队伍不断成长，Piko 也会逐渐变强，并解锁新的能力，在探索和战斗过程中提供更多帮助。
战斗系统也迎来了大幅扩展，游戏加入了全新的“功能集成战术服”（Function-Integrated Tactical Suitwear），简称 FITS 系统。FITS 可以通过配备拥有独特招式组合的新制服，让玩家自由定制战斗风格。
游戏目前提供四种专门化 FITS，分别是战士（Warrior）、骑士（Knight）、黑魔法师（Black Mage）和召唤师（Summoner）。不同 FITS 会大幅改变队伍成员的能力和战斗定位，为玩家带来全新的战术选择。在此次公布的加长版实机演示中，玩家可以看到 Cid 穿戴骑士 FITS、Vincent 穿戴召唤师 FITS 的战斗表现。
FITS 改变的不只是角色的战斗能力，角色的外观也会随之发生变化。这些“outFITS”同样会成为角色展示个性的时尚装扮。
《最终幻想 7：启示录》还将加入全新的动态角色切换功能。玩家在探索开放世界时，可以即时在不同队伍成员之间切换。
游戏的移动和探索系统也得到进一步升级。新增的抓钩枪可以帮助玩家快速登上屋顶，并以更加灵活、帅气的方式穿梭于城市之中。
玩家还可以自行决定由哪名队伍成员负责特定任务。不同选择会影响部分剧情事件和游戏场景的发展，让玩家的决定真正塑造出不同的故事体验。
对于喜欢卡牌游戏的玩家来说，广受粉丝喜爱的小游戏“Queen's Blood”也将在《最终幻想 7：启示录》中回归。这一次，游戏将围绕 Red XIII 展开一条全新的重要剧情线。
玩家将面对实力更强的新对手以及独特的玩法挑战，进一步拓展这款策略卡牌游戏的核心机制。全新的 Queen’s Blood 剧情战役还会加入一些能够大幅改变对局节奏的特殊对手，即使是已经熟悉这套玩法的老玩家，也将面临新的挑战。
《最终幻想 7：启示录》现已在 PlayStation Store 开启预购。所有版本均提供特别预购奖励，提前购买游戏的玩家将获得“机甲陆行鸟与莫古利”召唤魔晶石（Mecha-Chocobo & Moogle Summon Materia）。
此外，游戏还将推出《最终幻想 7：启示录》Premium Edition 高级版，其中包含游戏本体、剧情扩展通行证（Story Expansion Pass）以及提前体验资格。拥有提前体验资格的玩家可以在正式发售前 24 小时进入游戏。
Premium Edition 还包含一件游戏内饰品“Reclaimant Choker”，以及一套可用于帮助玩家度过游戏初期阶段的消耗品。
顾名思义，剧情扩展通行证将提供两款以剧情为核心的 DLC，官方将在之后公布更多相关信息。
《最终幻想 7：启示录》Premium Plus Edition 则包含 Premium Edition 的全部内容，并额外提供数字美术设定集、数字迷你原声带、“Polydroid Alexander”召唤魔晶石、一件游戏内防具“Nymphwing Bracelet”，以及一件游戏内饰品“Risk Taker’s Choker”。
凭借更加广阔的开放世界探索、更深入的战斗系统、全新的壮丽区域以及围绕角色展开的个性化剧情，官方称《最终幻想 7：启示录》有望成为整个重制三部曲中规模最大、内容最丰富的一作。
IT之家注意到，官方只确认了游戏的 PS5 版本，但《最终幻想 7：启示录》将登陆所有目标平台并同步发售，因此 PC、任天堂 Switch 2 以及 Xbox Series X/S 版本也预计会在同一天推出。

title: 发布会前夕，特斯拉 Cybercab 车队现身美国多地
content:
IT之家 9 月 3 日消息，特斯拉 Cybercab 的现身范围正不断扩大，早已不局限于得克萨斯州奥斯汀市中心。公司计划北京时间明日凌晨 05:45 在得克萨斯州发布这款纯电动双座车型，自动驾驶是本次发布的核心。
特斯拉将在得克萨斯州奥斯汀举办专场活动，向一小部分受众开放 Cybercab，目前外界关于这场活动的公开信息还比较少。
不过，随着特斯拉 2026 年自动驾驶业务推进节奏加快，Cybercab 的布局早已跳出奥斯汀市中心，正向美国各地铺开。近日，多组拍摄于不同地点的 Cybercab 车队实拍图开始在网络流传。
最受关注的一组画面，出现在佛罗里达州迈阿密国际机场，现场至少停放着 20 辆 Cybercab。这批车队于当地时间昨晚被人拍到，规模可观，预示着只要完成各项监管审批，Cybercab 就距离正式投放不远。
特斯拉的 Robotaxi 平台已经在迈阿密运营数月，而机场这批 Cybercab，有望在拿到审批后接入该网约车平台。
另有一批 Cybercab 现身宾夕法尼亚州费城近郊的德文市特斯拉展厅。此前已经有多台 Cybercab 在费城都会区开展路测，这点十分值得关注，目前特斯拉在宾夕法尼亚州还没有启用任何 Robotaxi 地理围栏运营区域。
据IT之家了解，费城游客密集、城市幅员辽阔，非常适合开展网约车测试，同时也便于和当地其他网约车企业展开竞争。
综合现有迹象判断，今年余下时间里，规模庞大的 Cybercab 车队会陆续出现在美国各大城市及其周边。特斯拉的态度十分明确：Cybercab 将会大力度、快速落地，但仍会保持理性节奏。安全依旧是特斯拉的首要考量，因此测试阶段还会持续一段时间，普通民众还要再等一等，才能把 Cybercab 当作个人代步出行工具。

title: 徕卡发布 Summicron-M 66mm f/2 镜头：1.09 万美元，全球限量 660 枚
content:
感谢IT之家网友 Hanschen2007 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 3 日消息，徕卡今天宣布推出 Summicron-M 66mm f/2 镜头。这款产品是 20 世纪 60 年代经典名镜 Elcan 66mm f/2 的复刻版，全球限量 660 枚，售价 10,900 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 73,428 元人民币）。
据介绍，Elcan 66mm 这款镜头最初为美国海军设计，一般与徕卡 KE-7A（M4 的军事版本）相机搭配使用，专为需要极致细节的隐蔽拍摄场合设计，当时只生产了 200 枚，是 M 卡口最罕见的镜头之一。
规格方面，Summicron-M 66mm f/2 遵循了原作的光学结构和镜身设计，但针对现代 M 系统进行优化。该产品采用 5 组 6 片结构，光圈调节范围为 f/2-f/16，配备 9 片光圈叶片。镜头长宽约为 60.1*60，重 456g。
此外，这款镜头的机械结构与普通产品有所不同，其光圈环的旋转方向与标准 M 口镜头相反，距离标尺排布遵循军用规格。官方宣称，这款镜头能在全开光圈时呈现“柔和虚化和高对比度”，收缩光圈后可带来“细腻画质表现”。

title: 沙特 HUMAIN 公布前沿阿语模型 humain-m3，由 MiniMax 受托开发
content:
感谢IT之家网友 LL J 的线索投递！
IT之家 9 月 3 日消息，沙特阿拉伯主权财富基金 PIF 旗下人工智能企业 HUMAIN 当地时间今日公布了前沿阿拉伯语模型 humain-m3。该模型由 MiniMax 受托开发。
humain-m3 基于 MiniMax 自家 MiniMax-M3 构建，并进行了 T 级阿拉伯语原生文本 Token（词元）规模的预训练。其在 7 个公开的阿拉伯语基准测试中取得了参测前沿模型中的最高平均分。
humain-m3 率先在 HUMAIN Node 平台以研究和评估预览版本提供。HUMAIN 后续将发布开放权重版本。
HUMAIN 首席执行官 Tareq Amin 表示：
阿拉伯语的使用人口达数亿，但在人工智能前沿领域，它的代表性仍然严重不足。我们正通过 humain-m3 项目来改变这一现状。同时，通过 HUMAIN Node，我们将这种智能技术开放给开发者、研究人员和创新者，让他们能够进行实验、在此基础上进行开发，并创造下一代阿拉伯语人工智能体验。

title: 涉及应用适配：华为鸿蒙 HarmonyOS 7 系统沉浸光感新增生效约束
content:
IT之家 9 月 3 日消息，华为开发者官网 OS 平台行为变更说明今日迎来更新，宣布沉浸光感新增生效约束。针对此次变更，华为官方也给出了原因和影响：
变更原因：为确保性能和功耗体验最优，规范沉浸光感组件使用，沉浸光感对部分组件新增生效范围的约束。
变更影响：此变更涉及应用适配（此变更涉及的接口为 26.0.0 Beta 版本新增接口，因此变更仅在应用的 targetSdkVersion 设置为大于等于 26.0.0 时生效）。

title: 谷歌 DeepMind 发布 WeatherNext 3：分辨率最高 5 公里，号称全球最先进、精准 AI 天气预报模型
content:
9 月 3 日消息，谷歌 DeepMind 和 Google Research 今天宣布推出
WeatherNext 3
，号称是目前最先进、最准确的全球气象模型。该模型可直接从实时观测中学习，能够为影响人类的天气事件提供更及时、更本地化的预测。
该模型可以原始卫星数据为基础，每小时生成一次高分辨率预报，为全球谷歌产品提供可靠的天气预报。
根据介绍，天气预报的实用性往往取决于细节，以及时间和空间的分辨率。WeatherNext 3 可生成多种空间分辨率的每小时预报，从广阔的全球风型到局部地形都能保持物理一致性。
借助 WeatherNext 3，谷歌能够以 5 公里分辨率呈现温度、湿度等关键地表变量，其他地表变量分辨率为 10 公里，风速等大气变量分辨率为 25 公里。
WeatherNext 3 通过接入
实时全球地球静止卫星数据拼图
，让模型能够获得丰富、持续更新的大气视图，使模型可以每小时生成一次新预报，每次预报都基于最新的卫星观测数据，最高分辨率可达 5 公里。
这一点至关重要，因为极端天气往往发展迅速。当风暴、锋面或降水系统突然出现时，快速更新周期和更高分辨率能够提供更早、更详细的洞察，帮助人们采取有效应对措施。
WeatherNext 3
采用稀疏气象站观测数据训练
，这使得模型能够在 5 公里网格上生成全球预报，并充分考虑地形等区域细节。这一突破对于拉美、非洲、亚太地区尤其重要。由于传统区域模型需要高昂的超级计算成本，这些地区历史上一直缺乏高分辨率天气预报。该模型将为这些地区数十亿人和本地企业带来本地化、高保真天气预报。
除了提升分辨率和预报频率，该模型还专门
针对可再生能源生产引入了针对性预测
。模型可以预测 100 米高度（IT之家注：大致对应风力涡轮机高度）的风速，从而精准预测风电产量，同时还能提供高分辨率云量和太阳辐射数据，帮助太阳能电场估算地面接收到的光照。
这些数据对于全球清洁能源规划至关重要，能够帮助电网运营商和可再生能源开发商准确预测清洁能源资产的发电量，并匹配用户需求。
即日起，WeatherNext 3 将正式为谷歌搜索、Gemini 应用、谷歌地图、谷歌地图平台气象 API 和谷歌 Earth Engine 提供气象能力支持。

title: Agriculture relies on fossil fuels. It’s costing us.
content:
Agriculture relies on fossil fuels. It’s costing us.
Could new fertilizers help combat high prices?
If you’ve had to fill up your vehicle’s gas tank or buy a plane ticket lately, you’ve probably felt the effects of rising fossil-fuel prices. But farmers buying fertilizer for their crops are especially aware of just how far the ripple effects of the conflict in Iran have spread.
Fertilizer prices have been on a roller coaster this year, kicked off in part by trade disruptions and high prices for natural gas, a key ingredient in fertilizer production. Let’s take a closer look at why conventional fertilizer prices are so sky-high, and how a few more climate-friendly alternatives could bring farmers some relief.
As fossil-fuel prices go up, nearly all industries are affected, since most of our economy relies on these fuels to move goods and people around.
But fertilizer is even more intertwined with these fluctuations, because natural gas is used as both an energy source and a chemical input in the production of ammonia, a key fertilizer ingredient. So as natural-gas prices have spiked in recent months because of the war in Iran, fertilizer prices have followed. (It’s worth briefly noting here that fertilizer production is also a major source of greenhouse-gas emissions, accounting for about 2% of the global total.)
Fertilizer trade is being directly affected as well, since about one-third of global seaborne trade in fertilizers passes through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed to commercial traffic because of the conflict. Access to fertilizer could get worse for some of the poorest countries around the world because of the strait’s closure, according to a report from the World Bank. While the US largely meets demand for nitrogen fertilizers with domestic production, some imports do come from the Persian Gulf.
At one point in April, the price of urea (the most commonly applied fertilizer) climbed above $850 per metric ton. That’s 80% higher than it was before the conflict and the highest level since 2022, when the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the resulting conflict caused fertilizer costs to hit record highs. Prices have come down significantly, but forecasts remain uncertain.
“There’s just this out-of-control supply chain that’s a lot more volatile than it’s ever been,” says Travis Frey, chief technology officer of Pivot Bio, a company making fertilizer with genetically edited microbes. (For more on these microbes, how they work, and what research is still needed, check out my latest story here.)
Pivot says its products are cost-competitive with chemical fertilizers today. And because they don’t use natural gas as an input, they aren’t subject to the same price spikes. When the war in Iran started, Pivot increased the volume it planned to produce, dropped prices, and allowed farmers to lock in prices for three years, Frey says.
That could be a major help for those farmers, because high prices could be here to stay for a while. Some fertilizer prices could remain high through at least 2028, according to a report from CoBank, one of the largest banks for the agriculture industry in the US.
That’s partly because the war has caused long-lasting damage: 31 ammonia plants in the Middle East have been affected or shut down completely. That’s on top of 20 ammonia plants that have been damaged in Russia in recent years.
Ongoing high prices can be extremely challenging for farmers. “The fertilizer price spikes, and because farmers have paper-thin margins, this is a real problem," says Tim Schnabel, founder and CEO of Switch Bioworks, another company working on advanced microbe fertilizers.
Higher costs can help push food prices higher, causing all of us to pay more at the grocery store. (It’s not just fertilizer, by the way. Farmers are also getting hit with wild diesel prices this year.) As long as we’re relying on fertilizers made with fossil fuels, food prices will be tied up with energy prices.
Switch and Pivot are among the companies looking to make alternative fertilizers that use microbes to provide nitrogen to plants. There’s a limit to how much synthetic fertilizers these products can actually replace: Depending on the crop and conditions, Pivot says, its products can replace about 25% of synthetic fertilizer today, and the company hopes to reach 40% to 50% of the total. But these alternatives could be a start to untangling fossil fuels and food.
“We can’t keep doing it like this,” Switch’s Schnabel says. “There’s no way we can build a society where the basis of the food chain depends on fossil fuels.”
