title: “Lower-Risk” Childhood Cancer May Be More Dangerous Than It Appears
content:
Researchers have found that some rhabdomyosarcomas considered lower risk may harbor aggressive cancer cells that resemble those seen in high-risk disease. Credit: Stock
Researchers have uncovered new clues about why the childhood cancer rhabdomyosarcoma may become aggressive.
Some children diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) appear to have lower-risk disease, yet their cancer can still become dangerously aggressive. Researchers have now uncovered biological similarities that may explain why, raising the possibility of identifying these children earlier and matching treatment more closely to their actual risk.
Childhood cancers differ from many cancers that develop in adults. Rather than being strongly associated with aging or environmental exposures, they commonly arise from developmental changes that increase the likelihood of cancer forming.
RMS is generally divided into two major groups based on whether a tumor carries a particular genetic risk marker. That marker forms when two genes that are normally separate become fused together. Children whose tumors contain this fusion have substantially poorer survival than those without it, even with intensive treatment.
But the usual classification does not explain every case. Some children whose tumors lack this high-risk marker nevertheless develop aggressive disease, leaving researchers with the question of what drives those cancers.
Single cells exposed hidden aggressive disease
Researchers at the Wellcome Sanger Institute, the University of Cambridge, and their collaborators set out to investigate what distinguishes these aggressive cancers in patients who had initially been categorized as non-high-risk.
They compared tumors from children with high-risk and non-high-risk RMS using genomic techniques that allowed them to examine cancer cells in much greater detail. One method, single-cell RNA sequencing, measures gene activity separately in individual cells rather than averaging signals across an entire tumor. That approach exposed aggressive cancer cells hidden within tumors that conventional classification had labeled non-high-risk.
The researchers also used spatial transcriptomics, a technique that preserves information about where cells are positioned inside tissue while measuring their gene activity. This allowed them to see how aggressive cell populations were arranged throughout the tumors.
The results showed that aggressive tumors from children classified as non-high-risk had patterns of gene activity closely resembling those found in high-risk tumors, even though they did not carry the established genetic risk marker.
The researchers also identified rare genetic alterations in aggressive non-high-risk tumors that disrupted the same cellular pathways affected in high-risk disease. This indicates that different genetic changes can ultimately lead cancer cells toward a similar aggressive state.
Different mutations converge on aggressive disease
Finding distinctive markers on these high-risk cells could eventually help researchers develop more targeted treatments. Possible approaches include immunotherapies such as CAR-T cell therapy, which could potentially attack cancer cells more selectively while limiting some of the side effects associated with conventional chemotherapy.
The researchers also hope the findings could eventually improve how children are classified at diagnosis. More accurate identification of aggressive tumors could allow clinicians to intensify treatment for patients most likely to relapse while sparing genuinely lower-risk patients from unnecessary treatment toxicity.
To build on the findings, the researchers are expanding their analysis to hundreds of additional tumor samples. Their goal is to uncover more of the rare genetic routes that can produce aggressive childhood cancer and support the development of more precise treatments for young patients.
Findings could refine treatment decisions
Dr Karin Straathof, co-senior author at UCL Cancer Institute and GOSH, said: “By studying tumors one cell at a time, we uncovered hidden populations of aggressive cancer cells that conventional methods miss. Although these tumors carry different genetic changes, many converge on the same aggressive pathways. This helps explain why some children who appear to have lower risk disease can still have a devastating outcome.”
Sara Wakeling, Chief Executive Officer and co-founder of Alice’s Arc, said: “Every child with cancer deserves the best possible chance of survival. We’re proud to support research into rhabdomyosarcoma showing how cutting-edge technologies can uncover the biology driving aggressive childhood cancers. These discoveries bring us closer to more personalized treatments and better outcomes for children.”
Dr Laura Danielson, Children’s and Young Person’s Lead at Cancer Research UK, said: “Discovery research like this is essential to understand the unique biology of these cancers. This important study demonstrates that aggressive tumors may share similar features, even if they carry different genetic changes. By helping researchers understand what these high-risk cancers have in common, this work adds a vital piece to the puzzle and could help guide future efforts to improve treatment for children and young people with rhabdomyosarcoma.”
Professor Sam Behjati, co-senior author formerly at the Wellcome Sanger Institute and Head of the Department of Pediatrics at the University of Cambridge, said: “This work changes how we think about rhabdomyosarcoma. Rather than a single, abnormal gene, we’ve shown that there is an overarching cell state of aggressive disease that defies conventional classification systems. Understanding this shared biology could help identify children who need more intense treatment to improve their survival.”

title: A Decade Ago I Bet Big on China Coverage. I'd Do It Again.
content: I landed in Beijing in March of 2016, Ubered around dozens of tech companies a week and had nightly drinks with Chinese and U.S. investors at the Rosewood in Beijing. On the weekends, I visited the startups that worked Saturdays (they all did) and wandered the malls and parks. I hopped to Hong Kong for some parties and hikes and barely stopped eating! I was in reporting heaven. I was also confused. By my count, there were as many tech reporters covering Uber in San Francisco as there were reporters for U.S. publications covering technology in Beijing. As an entrepreneur, that gap thrilled me. So even as the entire staff of The Information barely filled a tiny San Francisco office, I decided to invest big in Hong Kong just a few months later. Our coverage stood out instantly. Our reporting on Uber’s withdrawal from China was followed by our coverage of the rise of ByteDance, when only a few knew its name . We broke ByteDance’s revenue and product plans annually and revealed the secret deals Tim Cook was striking with the Chinese government, a historic scoop . Our chronicling of China’s crackdown on its own internet companies, was followed by the rise of Shein and Temu and the oft-discussed “decoupling” of the U.S. and China markets. And all that before the current era of the AI cold war with Nvidia at the center , the rise of DeepSeek and, just this week, China’s new strides in chips . Ten years later, even as the U.S. and China tech worlds have changed dramatically, I am in awe of the team that has done this all and keeps on going. And that same coverage gap—the lack of in-depth reporting about China’s tech businesses—still enthralls me. Other news outlets have pulled back from Hong Kong and Beijing, amid real pressures on the press. We take those threats seriously but are pushing ahead independently. This week, we are celebrating another milestone in the bureau: welcoming our first team member in Singapore, Claudia Chong. Jing Yang, our Asia bureau chief, is a force and keeps pushing ahead. Jing reminds me, 10 years after we first opened the bureau, that the urgency of business leaders globally to understand the China market has never been more intense. And our team is on the front lines. It’s funny to look back and remember how it all began: a plane ticket, some phone numbers to try and the naivete that I could pay for things in China with a credit card. And as The Information has grown into an 80-person global news organization, I’m a bit nostalgic for traffic-jammed Beijing days when I managed to make it from Tsinghua University to Xiaomi before staying up way too late meeting with entrepreneurs who didn’t leave the office until midnight. As a reporter and editor, I’ve been lucky to travel the world. But nothing quite compares to my full China immersion, which looking back was one of the most fruitful periods of my professional life. Within a month after my return to the U.S., I was also pregnant with my first son, an ordeal that had taken longer than I had wanted. Two lessons stand out—both for journalists and entrepreneurs. Take the long game and be patient. The Information’s leadership position in Asia tech today dates back more than a decade to my messaging random entrepreneurs on WeChat. While our reporters have done the hard work, without my decision to pack up and get out, I wouldn’t have found the conviction to build a business there—a decision I’ve committed to again and again as the market has changed. And, especially when reporters can direct growing armies of bots to gather all sorts of information from the comfort of their desks, remember to leave your office and wander far. It is then that you are more likely to see something others don’t. And all good stories—and business ideas—come from that.

title: Anthropic Splits From Google, OpenAI Over State AI Safety Bill
content: Anthropic is at odds with other big tech firms over a Massachusetts Senate proposal requiring big AI developers to hire independent evaluators to assess catastrophic risks posed by their models every four months. The Massachusetts proposal could set a new standard for AI regulation, which state legislators across the country are pursuing aggressively even as congressional lawmakers drag their feet on passing federal legislation. The proposal also comes as concerns are mounting about the dangers of rogue AI agents in the wake of the OpenAI–Hugging Face attack, when hundreds of agents figured out how to communicate with each other and coordinate an attack on Hugging Face. Anthropic and safety groups support the AI language in the Senate version of the legislation, which is opposed by companies such as Google and OpenAI. The legislation is tucked into a broader economic development bill before the state upper house. A conference committee of the two Massachusetts chambers is now meeting to finalize the bill, which will determine whether the AI provision advances into the final text. Previous AI-related state bills have established new floors for safety regulation that were later reflected in other states’ efforts. For instance, an Illinois bill passed in May instituted the concept of annual third-party compliance audits. The Massachusetts proposal would likely have a similar impact on other states. It goes further than the Illinois bill by requiring independent evaluations of companies’ models themselves, as well as increasing the frequency of audits. On July 24, after the Massachusetts Senate passed its version, Anthropic head of U.S. state and local policy Cesar Fernandez wrote in a post on X that it “raises the bar on AI safety while ensuring that innovation is able to continue.” Anthropic has previously been a vocal supporter of other state-level AI safety bills. Anthropic is joined by AI safety organizations including Encode and Secure AI Project, which have engaged lawmakers in Massachusetts and recently sent a letter of support to the members of the conference committee, Secure AI Project policy director Scott Wisor told The Information. Meanwhile, OpenAI has voiced its objection to the Massachusetts language. In previously unreported letters sent on Aug. 18 and 19 to the conference committee and Sen. Barry Finegold, who has spearheaded the AI language, OpenAI policy executives wrote that Massachusetts should consider a requirement similar to the Illinois bill, and added that “fragmented oversight” across the country would represent an “unhappy result.” “A confusing jumble of rules will unnecessarily delay getting the most advanced cyber models into the hands of state and local officials before bad actors with their own powerful AI break in and exploit vulnerabilities,” wrote Donnie Fowler, the company’s head of U.S. state policy and partnerships, and Ann O’Leary, its global affairs vice president. In a statement issued after publication, an OpenAI spokesperson said the company supports independent third-party technical assessments but thinks they are “best established at the federal level.” OpenAI and Anthropic are not the only AI giants active on the ground. In an interview with The Information, Finegold said he has also met with representatives from Google and Meta Platforms, though he declined to comment on their conversations. Google is concerned about states setting up additional testing requirements beyond the audits laid out in the Illinois bill, according to a person familiar with the company’s thinking. The lack of standards for testing models creates uncertainty about results, making compliance difficult until those standards are established, the person said. Google has previously withheld products in specific jurisdictions due to regulations—for example, it delayed offering its AI Overviews in many European countries until this summer—raising the possibility that the same scenario could happen with its models across different states. Though most states, including Massachusetts, have wrapped up their legislative sessions for the year, the conference committee’s work reconciling the economic development bill is expected to pick up after Labor Day, according to Finegold and political strategists working in the state. Finegold said he continues to engage with tech companies on the bill. He traveled to California in August to meet with representatives from OpenAI and Anthropic. The companies’ interest in pending legislation from Massachusetts reflects the rising importance of states’ roles in advancing AI policy. While OpenAI has previously advocated for federal preemption of state rules to prevent a fragmented patchwork of laws, it has since softened its position, including backing the Illinois law that included third-party audits. In a July blog post , OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, argued for what he dubbed “reverse federalism,” or states establishing a “shared direction through a common framework.” Some AI safety advocates saw OpenAI’s rejection of the Massachusetts AI provision as backtracking. “This ongoing fight looks an awful lot like regressing to the mean,” Encode founder Sneha Revanur wrote on X in August. In an interview, Encode policy adviser Ben Snyder, who has worked with Massachusetts lawmakers on the bill, said he was optimistic OpenAI would change its position. “They don’t want to be seen as a company that is opposing these measures, and I think for good reason,” Snyder said. Whether other companies, including Google and Meta, will lobby more aggressively against the language remains to be seen. Wisor said he expects to see more opposition emerge in the fall as the conference committee works on the language. Another industry group, the Andreessen Horowitz and Y Combinator–affiliated American Innovators Network, is urging the committee to reject the AI provision. “The Senate bill includes several additional compliance requirements that will create substantial barriers to scaling for small companies while making it more difficult to use open-weight models in the Commonwealth,” Executive Director Jeremy Kudon said in a statement. But even if the AI provision doesn’t make it into the final version of the economic bill, it could reappear as other states take up their own attempts at regulating the sector. On Aug. 30, the California legislature advanced a bill that would establish a framework for independent evaluation organizations, though it doesn’t set up requirements for audits of AI companies. The bill still needs to be signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom. Finegold said he has been in conversations with lawmakers from other states about advancing new legislation. “As the technology evolves, I continue to see each state leapfrogging the other state to make sure that we’re ahead of this,” Finegold said.

title: Google’s (Small) Antitrust Victory and Microsoft’s Azure Shift
content: We had lots of news today, including Microsoft’s decision to start breaking out Azure numbers, and Broadcom projecting bonanza growth in its AI chip business in the next couple of years. Oh, and the Trump administration threw its weight behind OpenAI in its copyright lawsuit against The New York Times Co. We have more on all those below. Meanwhile, you’ve heard of the world’s smallest violin. Google may now be playing the world’s smallest trumpet, having won a major victory in what’s arguably the least important antitrust case out there. That would be the ad tech antitrust lawsuit, the second of the two antitrust cases brought by the Justice Department against Google in recent years, and the second the government won —in theory. But as with the first case—over search—the outcome of this one has gone Google’s way. Its punishment for being a monopoly in both cases is so light as to be meaningless. A year after the arguments over how to remedy Google’s ad tech monopoly—we’re talking about the Google ad tools used to sell ad space on independent websites—were heard in a Virginia court, Judge Leonie Brinkema issued a tantalizingly brief ruling on Wednesday. She rejected the government’s proposal for “structural remedies”—that is, forcing Google to divest its ad tech businesses—and accepted most of the proposed “behavioral remedies.” In other words, Google can keep its toys but will have to play nicer with others. Big whoop. These toys aren’t worth much—and their value is degrading by the day. The proportion of ad dollars flowing to independent websites was never great (Google search and YouTube as well as Meta Platforms and Amazon swallow up most ad dollars, after all), and it is shrinking steadily. Some of that is due to AI changes Google made to its search engine, which have reduced the traffic going to websites. But some of it is also that ad money is shifting to video-streaming and mobile apps, two ad markets Google does not dominate. (We explained in this story that Google’s ad tech has fallen behind rivals in those markets.) By the numbers, Google’s network ad revenue—which reflects the ad tech business—accounted for just 9% of its ad revenue in the second quarter (and that’s before Google forks over a majority share to the websites). In 2018, network ads accounted for 17% of total advertising. (Much of the evidence presented by the government stemmed from the 2010s, not the present day.) We don’t know the reasons for Brinkema’s ruling, as the full text won’t be released for a couple of weeks, but during the trial last year , she asked whether forcing Google to divest its ad tech businesses could hurt independent websites. It’s a good bet Brinkema took that into account, just as the judge who heard the search antitrust case took into account AI’s impact in deciding how Google should change its ways. Google’s defense was, in fact, that the open web ad market was in decline. It seems the judge listened. All this is a reminder of the flaws inherent to antitrust enforcement of the tech industry, given how quickly technology-driven markets evolve and how slowly antitrust cases take to wind through the courts. Microsoft’s Idea of Transparency Finally! Microsoft is overhauling how it reports its business segments and will start reporting revenue for its Azure cloud unit quarterly, the software giant said on Wednesday. That’s a big deal. Azure is core to Microsoft’s AI business, so we’ll finally get a better picture of how the company is benefiting from AI. It also means we can compare the big three cloud firms, as both Amazon and Google were already reporting revenue for their cloud units. In the June quarter, for instance, we now know that Amazon Web Services generated $42 billion, Azure generated $29.4 billion and Google Cloud, $24.7 billion. But hold the applause. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the changes in segment reporting aimed to provide “increased transparency to investors.” Anytime a CEO says something about increasing transparency, you know things are about to become more opaque. In this case, the changes make it harder to figure out the profit margins on Microsoft’s individual segments. That’s because Microsoft is collapsing three segments into two. It is putting into one segment both Azure and its Microsoft 365 cloud software businesses, which it previously reported in separate segments. We used to see operating margins for those separate segments—the one with Azure had an operating margin of 41% in the fourth quarter, while the one that included Microsoft 365 had a margin of 58%. In the future, we’ll see revenue for individual units like Azure but not their operating income. That suggests we’re likely to see an operating profit that reflects both cloud and software, making it harder to figure out how the profits of both are separately changing. That’s not ideal. Microsoft’s pitch, though, is that both the Microsoft 365 and Azure units are sharing AI chips and cloud computing capacity, and that argues in favor of treating them as one segment for reporting purposes. In other words, investors won’t have to worry about how Microsoft is dividing up the chips. Fair enough, we guess. Trump Finds New Way to Attack the News Media President Donald Trump’s attacks on the news media are legendary, including defamation lawsuits and calls for TV networks to lose their license over coverage he doesn’t like. But on Wednesday, the Trump administration came up with a new tactic to undermine the news industry. The Justice Department on Wednesday filed a brief with the court hearing The New York Times Co.’s copyright infringement lawsuit against OpenAI, arguing that training AI models on copyrighted material—the core of the Times’ case—doesn’t violate copyright laws. The administration argued that if the Times prevailed, its approach to copyright could hurt the AI sector, which wouldn’t be good for the country. “Rules of law that make it significantly more difficult to develop a robust AI industry in the United States therefore threaten national security and give a competitive advantage to foreign adversaries who are not so encumbered,” the government argued. We wouldn’t want “rules of law” to get in the way of anything! In Other News • Broadcom CEO Hock Tan projected that the AI chip designer would double AI revenue to $115 billion in 2027 and potentially double it again to $230 billion in 2028. He made the projections as Broadcom reported 86% higher revenue of $29.6 billion in the quarter ending Aug. 2, a sign that its business helping design AI chips for companies such as Google, Meta and OpenAI is continuing to explode ( more here ). • Uber is laying off 10% of its workforce, or about 3,400 people, in an effort to streamline the organization by reducing management layers. In making the announcement , Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi told staffers that “the vast majority” of remote employees needed to move to an office, reducing the proportion of people who can work fully remotely to about 1%. • Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown called on countries to build more data centers at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina on Wednesday, arguing that adding more computing power would be the best way for governments to benefit from AI gains. He also praised President Trump’s “let data reign” post on Truth Social earlier this week. • World Labs, a startup led by Stanford University Professor Fei-Fei Li, on Tuesday unveiled Atlas, a new world model that can generate and modify photorealistic, interactive virtual environments based on text, image and video prompts. • The Supreme Court may wade into a battle between state lawmakers and prediction markets companies after New Jersey regulators filed a petition with the highest U.S. court to rule on whether sports bets offered by startups like Kalshi and Polymarket fall outside state gambling regulations. • Anthony Armstrong, former chief financial officer at SpaceX’s xAI, is joining Coinbase’s board, Coinbase said. • Nscale is telling prospective investors it has about $103 billion of total contracted revenue after clinching a $45 billion computing deal with Anthropic, ahead of an initial public offering for the neocloud that could take place as soon as this month, according to documents shared with investors and reviewed by The Information. • Shares of Snowflake rose more than 20% late Wednesday after the database provider surpassed its earlier forecast for product revenue—its most closely watched sales metric—by more than $70 million for the second quarter ending July 31. More here. • Meta Platforms announced Wednesday that it’s rolling out another AI model, Muse Spark 1.3. More here. title: Rogo, Hebbia Revenue Rises as Claude Finance Threat Looms
content: AI startups that aim to supplant the grunt work of junior bankers, private equity analysts and corporate finance associates have attracted billions of dollars of funding. They also face nagging doubts about whether Anthropic and OpenAI will annihilate them before long. The two most highly valued finance AI startups— Rogo and Hebbia —have been trying to dislodge the naysayers with a blitz of new products, offices and newly announced customers. Both sell software and AI agents that can take written instructions and create a financial model, memo or a hundred-page pitch deck by plugging into the data providers banks pay for and into a firm's own files. Both use models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google . But their growth has diverged. Rogo recently passed $50 million in annual recurring revenue, according to a person with direct knowledge of its business, up more than three times from $15 million at the end of 2025. The five-year-old startup founded by former investment bankers at Lazard and J.P. Morgan is on track to generate around $100 million in ARR by the beginning of next year, the person said. It employs more than 200 employees and has been hiring in Singapore, Tokyo and Sydney. The New York-based startup has raised $313.57 million from investors including Thrive Capital , Kleiner Perkins and Khosla Ventures , most recently valuing it at $2 billion in April. Meanwhile, Hebbia’s annual recurring revenue has risen to close to $50 million, a person with direct knowledge said. But it’s taken longer to reach that level than Rogo. Hebbia, founded in 2020 by a former Stanford University PhD student, was generating $13 million shortly after announcing its Series B round in July 2024, two people who have seen the pitch deck said. The person with direct knowledge confirmed the figure. Competition between the two firms is likely to heat up. Rogo initially landed customers from the founders’ alma maters as well as banks including Bank of America , Wells Fargo and BNP Paribas . Its flagship product Felix , launched in April, screen deals, write documents used in M&A processes or produce client decks. It’s now moving into selling to private equity, asset management, private credit and corporate development, the person with direct knowledge said. Hebbia, in turn, initially targeted private equity, private credit and hedge funds. It’s now moving into banking, a person close to the company said. A few months ago, Hebbia won a contract with Morgan Stanley that extends to about 5,000 of the investment bank’s workers, after a pilot of at least six months in which Hebbia competed with other vendors including Rogo, a person close to Hebbia said. Morgan Stanley bankers now use Hebbia to to review complex documents, analyze financial data, automate the work of junior banker and scale analysts’ productivity, according to a person close to the bank.  Morgan Stanley is also deploying Matrix , a product Hebbia revamped last week that lets customers build a custom agent and run many copies of it at once. Hebbia hired 100 people since January, opening offices across London, San Francisco and New York, and now employs 180 employees. It raised $159 million from investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Index Ventures , most recently at a valuation of $700 million in October 2024, and has around $70 million of cash left in the bank, according to a person with direct knowledge. The company had exploratory discussions with investors about a fundraising earlier this year but decided to not go through with it, a person close to the company said. Such efforts haven’t dampened persistent rumors about whether Hebbia could be quietly for sale. Hebbia has shot down such claims. “A lot of noise on the market,” as Hebbia CEO George Sivulka noted in a post on X on Tuesday announcing that daily active users had tripled since the launch of Matrix and total usage of large language models had risen fivefold. But neither rival can ignore the threat from the AI labs whose models support their applications. Anthropic launched Claude for Finance in July 2025 and “created the market for AI for finance startups because the models got better,” said Thomas Li , founder of Daloopa , which supplies financial data such as performance indicators or charts to hedge funds and investment professionals, AI labs and AI for finance startups like Rogo and Hebbia. Claude for Finance is “probably bigger than the rest of the market combined,” he said. OpenAI is further behind. But in March it launched a set of tools for financial analysis and investment memos, along with a ChatGPT integration for Excel and connectors to FactSet and S&P Global . In June it added plugins for its coding agent Codex aimed at public equity investors and investment bankers. Rogo and Hebbia argue the labs don‘t know enough about any individual firm to be useful. With agents fed a bank’s own history, Hebbia's agents behave “increasingly like your firm rather than like a generic Claude,” a person close to Hebbia said. The other big headwind comes from the startups’ customers, who are developing their own AI agents using models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others. That said, these AI startups may have room to grow for a while because in-house alternatives aren’t up to speed. Samir Dutta , CEO of Farsight , which competes with Rogo and Hebbia by offering AI-powered agents to make pitch decks and deal documents for investment banks, said financial institutions’ employees are “really good at operating once the use case is very, very well scoped out. But a lot of these banks don't have that yet.” Firms that decide they need no outside help “generally end up coming back full circle,” said Kris Bennatti , founder of Hudson Labs , which uses AI and agents pulls exact figures out of company filings and flags fraud risk to customers such as what kind.— Stephanie Palazzolo contributed reporting. Here’s what else is going on… Overheard Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown called on countries to build more data centers at the G20 Innovation Ministerial in North Carolina on Wednesday, arguing that adding more computing power would be the best way for governments to benefit from AI gains. Elon Musk made similar comments in his virtual remarks at the event on Tuesday. Nscale is telling prospective investors it has about $103 billion of total contracted revenue after clinching a $45 billion computing deal with Anthropic , ahead of an initial public offering for the neocloud that could take place as soon as this month, according to documents shared with investors and reviewed by The Information. Meta is pulling back further from a push to make AI usage a measure of engineers’ performance, telling employees that the company “will not use AI adoption dashboards or token counts to evaluate impact.” In an internal memo Tuesday from executives Maher Saba and Santosh Janardhan , which was reviewed by The Information, Meta announced updated expectations for engineers across the company. The memo removes from Meta’s career expectations guidelines for engineers references to specific AI tools and replaces task-specific AI instructions with expectations focused on work quality and impact. Micro1 , a startup that sells data to improve AI models’ responses, has committed at least $1 million to train former Spirit Airlines employees with AI skills as part of its bid for the bankrupt airline’s corporate data, three people close to the company said. The pledge is part of an effort to convince the court that it will be a better custodian of the corporate data than Google , which in mid-August won an auction for the collapsed carrier’s internal business data and software code. People on the Move Anthony Armstrong , former chief financial officer at SpaceX’s xAI , is joining Coinbase’s board, Coinbase said. Armstrong, who has no relation to Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong , left xAI as CFO earlier this year after joining last fall. Before joining xAI, Armstrong, a former Morgan Stanley banker, advised on Elon Musk’s Twitter takeover in 2022. In 2025, he worked for Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency . Court Watch The Trump administration backed OpenAI in its legal battle with the New York Times , arguing in a brief that barring AI companies from training their models on publishers’ output would be unfair and hurt U.S. technological competitiveness. The legal brief, filed by lawyers for the Department of Justice with the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York , argues that the Times is seeking an overly narrow definition of “fair use” that would improperly restrict how large language models are trained. Earnings Report Microsoft’s cloud unit Azure’s revenue was $101.9 billion in the twelve months ending in June, Microsoft disclosed Wednesday, up 40% from the year prior. Microsoft made the disclosure, and revealed it will start reporting Azure’s revenue quarterly, as part of a broader overhaul of how it reports the financial breakdown of its various businesses. And it comes as Azure’s progress has become a key metric that investors watch to track Microsoft’s AI progress. Broadcom reported 86% higher revenue of $29.6 billion in the quarter ending Aug. 2, a sign that its business helping design AI chips for companies such as Google , Meta and OpenAI is continuing to explode. On an earnings call Broadcom CEO Hock Tan projected that Broadcom would double AI revenue to $115 billion in 2027, from an expected $57 billion this year. And Broadcom has a “line of sight” suggesting AI chip revenue could double again to $230 billion in 2028. Broadcom was on track to exceed $30 in earnings per share in 2028. Last year, Broadcom’s earnings per share was just below $5 a share. Shares of Snowflake rose more than 20% late Wednesday after the database provider surpassed its earlier forecast for product revenue—its most closely watched sales metric—by more than $70 million for the second quarter ending July 31. Snowflake is benefiting as more of its customers use its AI products, which include an AI coding tool and a service for analyzing data to get answers to business questions. More than 9,100 customer accounts are using its AI coding tool, Cortex Code , up from 7,100 customer accounts last quarter. Deals and Debuts See The Information’s Generative AI Database for an exclusive list of private companies and their investors. Nvidia said that it had agreed to acquire open-source model repository Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, confirming a report from The Information. Nscale , an AI cloud company, announced that it had signed a multi-year strategic partnership with humanoid robotics company Figure to deploy up to 100,000 Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs starting in the second half of 2027. The deal has an initial commitment of $3.5 billion of compute and the intent to scale to over $6 billion, the companies said. Nscale said it would become a FIgure shareholder and preferred compute provider. Cornerstone Robotics , a company that develops robotic systems surgeons use to operate through small incisions, received an approximately $700 million strategic investment from Medtronic . Wonderful , a company whose software acts as a shared control layer that lets a large company run AI agents, automated workflows and AI applications across its whole business rather than one department at a time, raised $550 million in a Series C funding round led by Insight Partners . Palo Alto Networks paid $500 million in cash and stock for Console , whose software lets a company describe an operational goal in plain English and then carries out the work automatically, according to TechCrunch. The US Army awarded Palantir and Anduril a combined $192 million in delivery orders to build eight more TITAN mobile ground stations—trucks carrying software that pulls in data from drones, satellites and ground sensors and turns it into target recommendations for long-range artillery, according to Defense Scoop. Lyte , a company that designs the chips, sensors and software robots use to see where they are and what is moving around them, raised $165 million at a $1.6 billion post-money valuation in a Series C funding round led by Maverick Silicon . iPronics , a company that offers optical switches letting an AI data center rewire the connections between its chips on the fly, raised $125 million in a Series B funding round led by Maverick Silicon and Light Street Capital . HiddenLayer , an Austin-based company whose software watches a business's AI models and agents while they are running and blocks attempts to manipulate them, raised $100 million in a Series B funding round led by Delta-v Capital . Elucid , a company whose software reads ordinary CT scans to measure the plaque in a patient's arteries and estimate the risk of a heart attack or stroke, raised $55 million in a Series D funding round from investors including IAG Capital Partners and Elevage Medical Technologies . Capacity , a company whose software answers customer support questions automatically across chat, phone and messaging, raised more than $54 million in a Series E funding round, bringing total funding past $159 million. Conveo , a company whose AI interviewer runs recorded video conversations with consumers and turns them into market research a company can search in plain language, raised $50 million in a Series A funding round from investors including DST Global, Balderton Capital, Visionaries, 6 Degrees Capital and Y Combinator . SciFin , a company whose software pulls a sales organization's scattered information into one continuously updated picture and answers questions about it, emerged from stealth with $44 million in a seed funding round led by Altimeter and Madrona . Locus Robotics , a company whose robots carry orders around warehouses so workers do not have to walk them, has raised $41.6 million so far in a Series G funding round that is still open, chief executive Rick Faulk told Axios. Aitan , a company that develops ground combat robots that run their own AI on board and coordinate as a group, emerged from stealth with $41 million in a funding round led by Deep33 and Dell Technologies Capital . Lasso Security , a company whose software inspects what a business's AI agents say and do and blocks unsafe requests, raised $30 million in a funding round led by ClearSky . Huskeys , a company whose software gives security teams one place to see and set policy, and telling legitimate AI agents apart from AI-driven attacks, raised $27 million in a Series A funding round led by Blackstone Innovations Investments . Moonshot AI , whose Kimi K3 open-source model has become a global hit, has filed confidentially an application for a Hong Kong initial public offering, Chinese media outlet LatePost reported Wednesday. Meta Platforms announced Wednesday that it’s rolling out another AI model, Muse Spark 1.3 . Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang , said in an X post that Muse Spark 1.3, which is available through its coding product Muse Code and the Meta model API, is its “most capable model yet,” with improved agentic and coding capabilities. title: Startups Gravitate to a New, Pentagon-backed Battery to Bypass China’s Chokehold
content: In 2024, the U.S. approved the sale of attack drones to Taiwan, triggering a furious response from China. In retaliation, Beijing blocked the sale of batteries to Skydio, the largest U.S. maker of drones, creating a supply crunch for the company because it had no alternative source of batteries. Beijing’s move, leveraging China’s vast dominance of the world’s battery industry and the supply chain behind it, created worry in Washington and across U.S. businesses. It demonstrated China’s capacity to effectively shut down individual companies, whole industries and some weapons systems. Two years later, SAE International, the standards-setting organization, has released the first formal industry standard for drone batteries. The standard brings uniformity to the dimensions of batteries that power the small drones used most frequently in Ukraine and other war zones. Most Chinese drone batteries are metal cylindrical cells; the new SAE standard version is a flat, rectangular or square battery called a pouch cell. The moves, resembling Thomas Edison’s standardization of the light bulb with the Edison screw, which remains the most common threaded socket, could help juice the small U.S. battery industry by defining the basic building block of drone power systems. If drone makers embrace the standard, battery startups would face lower capital expenses, since it would simplify the cost of setting up and operating a factory. Numerous U.S. battery makers, expecting this drone demand, have already made plans to produce such standard batteries. The standard will also get a boost from the Department of Defense, which backed the effort and appears likely to adopt the standard for the Drone Dominance Program, under which the Pentagon seems likely to eventually buy millions of drones per year. “We want to build an industry outside of China,” said Lisa King, vice chair of the SAE committee that handled the standardization, and head of advanced battery strategy for Leap Manufacturing, a consultancy. King told me that not long after the Chinese blacklisting of Skydio in October 2024, she was leading a battery industry conference in Dayton, Ohio, at which she got into a conversation with an executive from the company. The executive related Skydio’s battery trouble in China and his search for an alternative supply. Skydio was using the Chinese cylindrical cell, known as the 2170 because of its dimensions—21 millimeters in diameter and 70 in length—in addition, in some drones, to a flat pouch cell. The executive was seeking a Western version of the  pouch version. After the conference, King spoke with a Pentagon official whose unit in part funded Leap, the consultancy where she works. This official suggested the standardization effort to bypass China’s battery chokehold, noting that pouch cells were increasingly popular with drone startups for the accommodation of next-generation battery chemistries; such batteries weighed less than the 2170s, a crucial factor in aviation. With the Pentagon’s blessing, King, starting in February last year, began holding conference calls with a group of around two dozen Western companies to decide what the standard should be. The result, in July, was the standard announced by the SAE : The new standard pouch cell would be roughly the same size as the incumbent 2170s when the 2170s were used in groups of six, as is typical in drones. “It is really, really risky to have one single point [of] failure, and that is China, for something as important as power sources,” King said. “Ninety percent of power cells are made in China.” Several battery makers already have plans to make the standard cell. Jaehee Sweeney, chief business development officer at South Korea’s BEI, said the next-generation lithium-metal battery maker already makes one battery that fits the standard and intends to add others. Tom Stepien, CEO of Amprius Technologies, said the silicon battery startup would use the standard cell in an ultrahigh-energy battery it will release in the fourth quarter. The battery will deliver energy density of 500 watt-hours per kilogram, almost twice that of conventional lithium-ion batteries, substantially increasing flight time, Stepien said. Adrian Yao, CEO of Indiana-based battery maker EnPower, told me that even before the SAE standard had been finalized, he began retooling the company’s factory to make more than 2 million of the new pouch cells annually, starting in the middle of next year. He said EnPower has no firm contracts for the batteries but expects them to emerge. He predicts that more battery makers in the U.S. and South Korea will make the standard cell. Drones will not be their only use: “I’m evangelizing this form factor as well for applications like industrial robots, [ranging from the] nonhumanoid to the humanoid,” Yao said. “This is a world in which pouch cells are better than cylindrical cells.” Yao said standardization solves one of the largest problems of getting a battery factory going. When a customer wants to fiddle with a battery’s chemistry or the thickness of the electrodes, it’s no big deal. But changing the dimensions of a cell, even slightly, can involve monstrous cost increases because replacing the manufacturing equipment can cost $30 million. Fixing the dimensions gets rid of that uncertainty. “If we want low costs, if we want to compete, we have to standardize,” he said.

title: Why I’m Launching The Information’s AI Show, AI Deep Dive
content: The Information has become the most trusted source on the AI business by breaking news about the biggest deals in the industry. Now we’re expanding that coverage with a new show called “AI Deep Dive” that will give you a more sophisticated understanding of the technology itself. “AI Deep Dive” will complement our daily coverage with long-form conversations with the researchers and founders working on the frontier of AI. I’m your host. I’ve written about AI at The Information for the past two years, taking advantage of my technical background to uncover and translate highly technical stories in AI and robotics. I studied computer science in college, briefly worked as a programmer and received a crash course in AI research while working at MATS, a mentorship program for AI safety researchers. These days I keep up with AI research in part by discussing a new machine learning paper every week with a reading group. That experience sets me up to guide technical conversations with our guests. To kick off the series, I’ll be talking to Noam Brown, a research scientist at OpenAI, about the challenges involved in creating AI agents that can autonomously take actions on a computer. Each of the following episodes will break down a hard problem on the technological frontier, from training AI models to control robots to studying the neuroscience of their “brains.” As AI barrels ahead, bringing new developments every week, separating hype from real progress has never been more valuable. Understanding which technical problems have researchers stumped and what makes those problems so hard is the best inoculation against the hype. TITV will remain our home for daily coverage of the biggest stories in tech. If you want to better understand the technology behind the business, I hope you’ll tune in when the first episode of “AI Deep Dive” airs on Sept. 14.

title: Why Regulators Are Scrutinizing Prediction Markets' Trading Arms
content: Fast-growing prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket are well known for their consumer apps, where people can bet on everything from sports and elections to the weather and stock prices. But those companies do more than operate consumer apps. Behind the scenes, several prediction markets operate their own exchanges and clearinghouses for the contracts, and some even have trading firms that make bets using the same contracts that are available to customers. Those kinds of setups have caught the attention of U.S. regulators, which have been examining potential conflicts of interest in recent years following the 2022 collapse of crypto exchange FTX and its Alameda Research trading arm. The FTX implosion highlighted the crypto firm’s entanglements between in-house trading and its exchange. Those functions are generally kept separate in traditional financial markets—stock exchanges, for example, typically don’t own the market makers trading on them. More recently, the CFTC has included prediction markets in that scrutiny. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which oversees prediction markets including Kalshi and Polymarket US, is now seeking comments on proposed rules aimed at preventing exchanges from giving affiliated trading firms an advantage over customers. They would require trading and exchange businesses to operate independently and would bar the trading firms from making speculative bets against customers. “It’s really to address a different type of market structure that’s being used by crypto and prediction markets,” said Gabe Rosenberg, a partner at Davis Polk who advises financial institutions. “It’s about how many functions in the market can be done by one affiliated group and what protections need to be in place.” Though the rules would apply across U.S. derivatives markets, the CFTC highlighted prediction markets as an area with recent “practical significance.” The agency said it knows of at least six exchanges that allow trading by affiliated firms, which can be a significant source of liquidity for prediction markets. The CFTC comment period ends in early October, after which the agency could revise the proposal and move toward final rules. For now, some of the most popular prediction markets say their setups provide a level playing field for customers, and any affiliated trading firms are market makers that provide liquidity so contracts can trade easily. In the case of Polymarket, a company spokesperson said it doesn’t have its own market maker, either for its U.S. platform or for its separate, blockchain-based platform for international users. Kalshi, which is the biggest U.S. prediction market and is close to raising fresh cash at a $40 billion valuation , operates its own exchange and also owns Kalshi Trading, which trades on that exchange. A Kalshi spokesperson said the company supports the CFTC’s efforts. “Kalshi Trading is unprofitable and represents a very small percentage of our volume. This is a very common and regulated practice in our industry,” the spokesperson said. Kalshi Trading doesn’t receive preferential treatment and doesn’t share personnel, office space or communication channels with Kalshi, the spokesperson said. “Like any financial market, including the stock market, market makers are industry standard because they help bootstrap liquidity,” the Kalshi spokesperson said. Institutional market makers, including outside trading firms as well as Kalshi Trading, represent less than 5% of volume on the exchange’s most liquid contracts, the spokesperson said. Robinhood until recently relied on outside exchanges, including Kalshi’s. Last year, it invested in Rothera, a joint venture exchange between Robinhood and trading giant Susquehanna International Group, with each holding a 45% stake. Robinhood has since been routing some customers’ orders to the new exchange, and Susquehanna makes markets on the exchange. “In compliance with CFTC regulations, we provide a level playing field with fair, transparent and impartial access for all participants,” a Rothera spokesperson said. The rule proposal comes at a time when prediction betting is starting to resemble serious Wall Street markets, drawing outside market makers and sophisticated traders looking to profit from shifting odds. Prices on prediction contracts can change constantly, especially around short-term outcomes such as who will win the next set of a U.S. Open match. In its rule proposal, the CFTC noted concerns that prediction firms could give their own trading operation preferential treatment over other traders or access to nonpublic information. That could put everyday traders and other market participants at a disadvantage, the CFTC said. Under the proposed rules, an exchange would need to disclose any affiliated trading firm and keep its office space, personnel and information systems separate from those of the exchange. Any exchange that offers an incentive program to affiliate trading firms would have to ensure that unaffiliated members can participate on equally favorable terms. The exchanges also can’t give preferential treatment to affiliated firms under the proposal. For instance, if an independent trader puts in a buy or sell order at a given price, the exchange would have to fill their order first even if an affiliated firm placed the same order earlier. Affiliated trading firms wouldn’t be allowed to make directional bets and would need to put in both buy and sell orders for contracts rather than just taking a one-sided position. The CFTC’s focus on the affiliated trading firms comes amid separate regulatory battles prediction markets are facing over the sports-related trading that makes up the bulk of their trading activity. Kalshi, Polymarket and others are under scrutiny over whether their sports contracts are unregistered gambling offerings that should be subject to state-level registrations. Part of the firms’ argument that prediction markets should fall under federal rather than state regulation’ is that, unlike sportsbooks, they don’t trade against customers and are merely matching orders. The fact that some prediction markets also have affiliated trading firms arguably undercuts that logic. Even if the firms are simply market makers providing liquidity, they’re nonetheless taking the other side of customers’ bets on each trade. That underlines the challenge for regulators as they grapple with how prediction markets fit in with existing financial and gambling rules. title: CRAFT低温系统6 kW@4.5 K氦制冷机调试成功
content:
2026-09-03 15:20 来源：中国科学院等离子体物理研究所
CRAFT低温系统
近日，CRAFT磁体平台氦制冷系统建设取得重要进展。CRAFT低温系统6kW@4.5K氦制冷机主体现场调试及性能测试顺利完成，各项指标均达到设计验收要求。
调试工作重点围绕氦制冷机冷箱的制冷性能、液化能力、控制系统、安全联锁以及关键低温设备运行状态等内容展开系统验证。验收测试期间，氦制冷机在设计工况下完成了连续12小时稳定运行，同时实现了6kW@4.5K+50K@GHe的制冷能力。除设计工况外，项目团队还开展了氦液化工况性能测试，相关温度、压力、流量、加热功率以及杜瓦液位等参数均保持在相应运行范围内，这一结果验证了氦制冷机在复杂负荷条件下的制冷能力和运行稳定性，为后续根据超导负载需求灵活调整运行模式提供了重要技术基础。在性能测试基础上，项目团队对氦制冷机安全功能进行了验证，模拟了停电或紧急停机后的系统重启、真空系统运行等工况，进一步检验了冷箱及相关子系统之间的协同控制、安全保护和故障恢复能力，为系统长期连续、稳定可靠运行提供了保障。
6kW@4.5K级氦制冷机是CRAFT低温系统的重要核心子系统。此次主体性能调试成功，全面检验了氦制冷机在大制冷量、液化等不同运行模式下的综合性能，以及冷箱、压缩机站、控制系统和相关辅助系统的协同运行能力。这一重要节点标志着CRAFT低温系统由设备建设安装阶段进一步迈向系统联调和应用运行阶段。该系统将为超导磁体及相关低温实验装置的系统联调、性能验证和稳定运行提供可靠的深低温条件，并为大型超导磁体、先进低温技术及相关重大科研装备开展实验研究提供重要基础支撑。
此次调试成功，得益于团队在低温工程、自动控制等多学科领域的协同攻关，也为后续承担更大规模低温系统建设与运行任务奠定了人才和技术基础，进一步验证了等离子体所大科学团队在大型氦制冷装备集成、调试及运行保障方面的综合技术能力。

title: 国核自仪45台核级无纸记录仪顺利完成批量发货
content:
2026-09-03 09:02 来源：国核自仪
国产核级显控设备
8月27日，国核自仪45台核级无纸记录仪通过出厂验收，顺利发货。本次批量交付，标志着该产品已完成全流程技术迭代，全链条生产环节全面走向标准化，国产核级显控设备已具备持续稳定的批量供货能力，市场认可度持续提升。
核级无纸记录仪是基于FPGA(现场可编程门阵列)架构的高可靠显控平台核心产品，产品运行全流程无CPU和操作系统参与，从根源上解决了传统显控设备操作系统验证难、易受病毒攻击的行业痛点，天然具备防病毒、不死机、秒启动、响应速度快等优势。源代码完全自主可控，支持图形化二次开发与模块化灵活扩展，可快速开发出适用于各种场景的系列化显控设备。采用模块化技术，支持IO扩展，可实现无耗材高精度数据采集、存储与全链路溯源。自2024年推向集团外市场以来，累计供货量近150台，持续稳定的批量交付能力与久经核电严苛工况验证的过硬品质，充分彰显了产品的成熟度与可靠性。
该技术成果已获得国内行业权威认定。2026年6月，中国核学会组织召开了科技成果鉴定会，由叶奇蓁、于俊崇等4位院士及技术专家组成的专家组一致认定：该成果整体技术达国际领先水平。此外，该成果核心技术斩获上海市优秀发明选拔赛二等奖、全国电力行业管理创新成果一等奖、电力行业高价值专利奖等多项荣誉，获行业权威充分认可。
目前，核级无纸记录仪已广泛应用于核电工程领域的显控场景。下一步，公司将在保障现有订单稳定交付的基础上，以该技术成果为核心，积极拓展核电及核能综合利用等高端工业领域市场，打破场景与客户局限，持续输出国产化高可靠解决方案，助力更多工业场景数智化升级。

title: 秦山核电格栅清理机械手臂完成大修验证
content:
秦山核电格栅清理机械手臂完成大修验证
秦山核电维修四处机械团队自主研发的“无人机智能巡检+机械臂自动清理”设备——格栅清理机械手臂，近日在秦二厂312大修中完成现场验证。该设备面向海水系统取水格栅清理场景，可将原本依赖人工进入深井的作业方式，转变为地面远程监控下的无人化作业。
取水格栅是核电厂冷却水系统的重要屏障，其通畅状态关系机组运行稳定。传统清理方式中，作业人员需要进入地下二十余米的狭窄井道，在受限空间内开展检查和清理，存在作业强度大、效率低以及高处坠落、缺氧窒息等安全风险。
针对这一运维难点，秦山核电维修四处机械团队开展了为期8个多月的技术攻关，形成了集无人机巡检、智能识别和机械臂清理于一体的作业系统。作业前端由搭载高清传感设备的无人机完成格栅区域扫描和识别，生成可视化作业图谱;随后，机械臂依据回传数据自主规划路径，执行抓取、清运等操作，技术人员在地面进行远程监控和指挥。
在秦二厂312大修试用过程中，该机械手臂及时发现一处SEC格栅条破损缺陷，为后续处理争取了时间，降低了大修期间相关安全风险。现场验证结束后，研发团队对设备性能进行了评估，并梳理出后续优化方向。
据介绍，该系统应用后，作业人员无需进入深井，可从源头减少受限空间高风险作业;同时，原本可能需要数小时的清理工作，可压缩至数分钟内完成，有助于降低相关作业对机组运行和检修组织的影响。
此次验证表明，秦山核电在复杂环境下无人机稳定巡检、狭小空间机械臂精准操作等方面取得了阶段性应用成果。该技术路线也可为市政排水深井、大型水利设施、化工能源等存在受限空间作业需求的场景提供参考。

从技术突围到标准引领，《核电海水循环泵用立式齿轮箱设计规范》国家标准的制定落地，明确了设计路径、验证方法和质量准则，将为我国核电装备自主化、标准化、规模化发展奠定坚实基础，从而带动全产业链制造能力整体提升，加速核电装备国产化替代进程，切实守护国家能源安全。

title: Verdera Energy拟出售美国新墨西哥州Treeline铀矿项目全部权益
content:
Verdera Energy拟出售美国新墨西哥州Treeline铀矿项目全部权益
Verdera Energy Corp.近日宣布，已与Americas Uranium Corp.签署矿产资源购买和出售协议，拟出售其位于美国新墨西哥州的Treeline铀矿项目100%权益，交易仍受相关特许权使用费安排约束。
根据协议，Americas Uranium将收购Treeline矿产及相关产权的全部权益。交易对价包括交割时支付10万美元现金，以及在交割后36个月内分期支付总额为200万加元的Americas Uranium普通股，其中90%的股份对价将在该期限内分阶段完成支付。此外，Verdera将保留该项目铀矿净收益1.5%的特许权使用费，以及项目所产其他矿物1.5%的冶炼厂净收益特许权使用费。该特许权使用费可通过向Verdera支付40万加元降至1.0%。
Treeline铀矿项目位于美国新墨西哥州西博拉县和麦金利县。该地区具有铀矿勘探和开采历史，项目东南方向的圣马特奥矿曾开展采矿活动。根据Axiom Exploration Group查阅的2005年1月历史报告，Treeline矿区估计含有102万磅U₃O₈。Verdera同时说明，该估算属于历史估算，并不构成当前NI 43-101标准下的矿产资源量或储量;合格人士尚未完成足够工作将其归类为当前矿产资源，公司也未将其作为当前矿产资源使用。
Verdera首席执行官Janet Lee-Sheriff表示，Treeline项目具有继续扩大历史矿化范围的勘探潜力，但公司当前商业计划将重点放在四个大型矿产项目推进上。她表示，此次交易可为公司及股东带来即时价值，同时公司将继续推进包括West Largo项目NI 43-101技术报告编制在内的重点工作，并对其包含超过20万条钻孔记录的数据库开展数据挖掘，以寻找更多潜在机会。
Verdera Energy Corp.称，公司专注于开发新墨西哥州原地浸出(ISR)铀矿资产，持有约400平方英里的私人矿权，并拥有重要的专有铀数据库。该公司表示，其业务重点与美国国内铀资源开发需求相关。

title: 乌兹别克斯坦一体化核电站完成反应堆厂房基坑开挖
content:
乌兹别克斯坦一体化核电站完成反应堆厂房基坑开挖
乌兹别克斯坦总统新闻处9月2日发布消息称，由俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 承建的一体化核电站项目已完成反应堆厂房基坑开挖，累计清运土方超过100万立方米。
乌兹别克斯坦总统沙夫卡特·米尔济约耶夫 (Shavkat Mirziyoyev) 听取了该核电站建设进展汇报。该项目于今年6月正式启动，目前施工人员已在占地100公顷的施工安装基地完成场地开挖，并浇筑916立方米基础混凝土。项目现场共有450名工人和100台设备参与施工，项目总投资为95亿美元。
根据汇报，核电站配套工人居住区规划占地200公顷，将建设1万套公寓，可容纳近3.3万人。居住区内还将配套建设节能型多层住宅、幼儿园、学校、医疗设施、体育文化设施以及休闲娱乐空间，并采用替代能源和智能照明系统。
该核电站项目还将同步建设388公里输电线路、一座变电站、供水网络，以及近50公里公路和铁路。项目规划配套建设一个工业区，计划引入至少100家从事建筑材料生产的合资企业。
人才培养也是项目推进内容之一。乌方消息称，自2023年以来，俄罗斯国立核研究大学 (MEPhI) 乌兹别克斯坦分校已有216名毕业生，另有100名学生正在乌兹别克斯坦其他高校相关专业学习。
俄罗斯与乌兹别克斯坦于2018年签署在乌建设核电站的政府间合作协议。2024年，双方签署协议修订议定书，将合作范围扩大至在乌兹别克斯坦建设采用俄罗斯设计的小型核电站。按现有规划，小型核电站和大型核电站将在同一场址建设，乌方称该项目将成为世界首座一体化核电站。

title: 乌兹别克斯坦拟将核电项目本地化率提高至30%以上
content:
乌兹别克斯坦拟将核电项目本地化率提高至30%以上
乌兹别克斯坦计划提高吉扎克州综合核电站项目的本地化水平，目标是将本国生产的商品和设备占比由初步估算的21%提升至至少30%。该项目总投资约95亿美元，被乌兹别克斯坦视为未来重要的基荷电力来源之一。
乌兹别克斯坦总统沙夫卡特·米尔济约耶夫 (Shavkat Mirziyoyev) 在视察项目建设现场及规划中的核工业人员卫星城时表示，现有本地化比例仍需提高，并要求扩大本国企业在设备供应、工程建设和配套基础设施中的参与度。按项目总投资测算，若本地化率达到30%，本国供应商品和设备价值将约为28.5亿美元。
该综合核电站项目已于6月4日进入积极建设阶段。目前，反应堆厂房土方开挖已完成，开挖量超过100万立方米;基础底板混凝土浇筑量达916立方米;施工安装基地100公顷范围内的土方工程也已完成。现场约有450名工人和专家参与施工，并投入100余台专用设备。
按照计划，项目将使用约3000种产品和设备。乌兹别克斯坦方面要求，本国企业承担65%的建设和安装工作，项目建设还将需要约7000名当地工人和专业人员。米尔济约耶夫强调，施工质量和核安全必须作为优先事项，所有工作须符合国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 要求和相关国际标准。
为支撑核电项目本地化，乌兹别克斯坦拟在法里什区建设一座占地200公顷的工业区，重点发展建筑材料等配套产业。规划显示，园区内预计将引入至少100家合资企业，并通过技术转让推动15个领域实现本地化生产。相关部门被要求在年底前提交决定草案，为入驻企业提供税收和海关优惠。
项目外部基础设施建设同步推进，内容包括388公里输电线路、一座110千伏变电站、21公里饮用水管道、120公里技术供水管网、39.5公里公路和11公里铁路。乌兹别克斯坦方面提出，相关基础设施采购中的本地产品和服务占比应达到60%至70%。
国际原子能机构于6月22日至26日对乌兹别克斯坦国家核基础设施发展情况开展综合评估任务，并对有关工作作出积极评价。与此同时，乌兹别克斯坦正推进核电人才培养。自2023年以来，俄罗斯国立核能研究大学 (MEPhI) 塔什干分校已有216名学生毕业，其中83人继续赴中国、匈牙利、法国、意大利和韩国高校攻读硕士及博士学位，另有100名专业人才正在乌兹别克斯坦四所高校接受培养。
配套生活设施方面，乌兹别克斯坦计划为核电项目工人、专家及其家属建设一座占地200公顷的卫星城。该城镇规划建设约1万套公寓，可容纳近3.3万人，一期将建设3000套公寓，并配套学校、幼儿园、医疗、体育、文化和休闲设施。项目还计划采用现代隔热技术、替代能源和智能照明系统。

title: 伊朗拟推进一座大型和一座小型核电站项目
content:
伊朗拟推进一座大型和一座小型核电站项目
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 首席执行官阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexey Likhachev) 表示，伊朗布什尔核电站厂区目前已恢复平稳状态，俄罗斯专家正陆续返回现场，参与相关机组建设与维护工作。
据利哈乔夫介绍，目前已有45名俄方人员在布什尔核电站现场，另有约30人正准备抵达。按照计划，9月现场俄方人员将增至100人，主要包括建设项目经理和施工监督人员。
在推进既有项目的同时，俄伊双方正在讨论新的核电合作。此前，双方已就建设另一座大型核电站签署协议。伊朗方面近期又提出建设小型核电站的设想，并已收到一份小型核电站政府间协议草案。
布什尔核电站一号机组的维护工作也在推进。俄方一批专家已抵达伊朗，参与该机组计划于9月中旬开展的预防性检修，检修内容包括更换部分燃料组件。相关燃料已运抵现场。
利哈乔夫表示，双方沟通正在进行，相关工作按计划推进。尽管外部环境仍存在不确定性，俄方认为伊朗核电项目仍有继续发展的空间，并将参与后续合作。

title: 俄罗斯Energopotok工厂8月向多座核电站交付241台设备
content:
俄罗斯Energopotok工厂8月向多座核电站交付241台设备
位于俄罗斯萨罗夫优先发展区的能源波托克公司 (Energopotok) 工厂继续向俄罗斯国内及海外核电项目供应设备。8月，该公司向阿库尤核电站、埃尔达巴核电站和库尔斯克核电站共交付241台设备。
此次供货产品包括截止阀、波纹管阀、节流控制装置、闸阀、止回阀和单向阀等，主要用于俄罗斯设计核电站相关系统。
能源波托克公司目前已将生产布局扩展至萨罗夫优先发展区，并在当地推进投资项目，重点生产面向俄罗斯设计核电站的截止阀产品。
萨罗夫优先发展区位于俄罗斯下诺夫哥罗德州，于2017年4月20日依据俄罗斯联邦第473-FZ号法律设立。目前，该发展区登记居民企业9家，由Atom-TOR公司 (Atom-TOR) 负责管理，Atom-TOR-Sarov有限责任公司 (Atom-TOR-Sarov LLC) 在区内开展运营。

title: 俄罗斯与哈萨克斯坦签署首座核电站建设合同
content:
俄罗斯与哈萨克斯坦签署首座核电站建设合同
俄罗斯原子能建设出口公司(Atomstroyexport)与哈萨克斯坦核电站公司(KNPP)签署巴尔喀什核电站建设合同。该项目将采用VVER-1200反应堆，是哈萨克斯坦规划建设的首座核电站。签字仪式在东方经济论坛期间举行，俄罗斯国家原子能公司(Rosatom)首席执行官阿列克谢·利哈乔夫(Alexey Likhachev)和哈萨克斯坦原子能机构主席阿尔马萨达姆·萨特卡利耶夫(Almassadam Satkaliyev)出席。
根据规划，巴尔喀什核电站将建设两台采用VVER-1200三代+反应堆技术的机组，总装机容量为2.4吉瓦。项目厂址位于哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图州江布尔区乌尔肯村附近。
该核电项目的前期准备已持续数年。2025年6月，俄罗斯国家原子能公司与哈萨克斯坦原子能机构批准项目路线图，内容包括工程勘测、设计文件编制以及EPC总承包合同签订等工作。同年8月，项目在乌尔肯村附近启动工程勘测，以确定最佳厂址。相关勘测工作计划于2027年完成，随后将开展机组运行许可证申请所需文件的编制工作。
合同签署后，俄罗斯国家原子能公司将作为国际财团牵头方，负责项目全周期实施，涵盖设计、建设以及竣工设施交付等环节。
阿列克谢·利哈乔夫表示，俄罗斯国家原子能公司正推进设计收尾工作，并组建国际设备供应商联盟。项目各阶段将围绕建设和投运符合国际安全与效率标准的核电站展开。他表示，俄罗斯核技术将为哈萨克斯坦能源独立和可持续发展提供支撑。

title: 俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站完成2026年检修工作
content:
俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站完成2026年检修工作
俄罗斯库尔斯克核电站 (Kursk NPP) 2026年检修工作已全部完成。该电站在最后阶段将检修工期压缩23.5天，预计可增加发电量约5亿千瓦时。
2026年8月27日，库尔斯克核电站4号机组在提前完成带现代化改造内容的计划预防性检修后，已恢复至额定功率运行。此次检修在确保安全和质量的前提下较原计划提前20天完成。
本轮主要检修工作集中在反应堆厂房和汽轮机厂房，内容包括多重强迫循环回路设备、反应堆应急冷却系统、吹扫与冷却系统检修，以及7号、8号汽轮发电机组检修。反应堆石墨砌体也完成了主要现代化改造工作，以保障其运行参数符合要求。
库尔斯克核电站维修副总工程师谢尔盖·济斯金 (Sergey Zyskin) 表示，检修工期的优化得益于成熟的检修管理技术、俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 生产体系工具的应用以及人员配置优化。用于清洗7号、8号汽轮发电机凝汽器换热管的机器人设备技术性能也得到改进，核电站与承包单位人员协同完成了相关工作。
除4号机组外，3号机组也同步停机，对保障库尔恰托夫市稳定供热的热力装置进行联合检修。该项工作同样提前3.5天完成。至此，库尔斯克核电站2026年度检修计划全部收官。
截至目前，库尔斯克核电站3号、4号RBMK-1000机组以及7号VVER-TOI机组按调度计划功率运行。1号、2号机组因达到规定运行期限，处于无发电运行状态。截至2026年9月2日，库尔斯克核电站发电量较国家任务计划进度超出5.6%。
库尔斯克核电站及周边地区辐射水平处于机组正常运行范围内，未超过天然本底值。该电站隶属于俄罗斯核电运营公司 (Rosenergoatom)，是俄罗斯中央电力系统的重要节点之一。作为RBMK机组替代项目，库尔斯克核电站二期 (Kursk NPP-2) 正在建设采用VVER-TOI技术路线的新机组。

title: 俄罗斯科拉核电站启动核能制氢试验综合体建设
content:
俄罗斯科拉核电站启动核能制氢试验综合体建设
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 旗下科拉核电站 (Kola NPP) 已在厂区内启动制氢台架试验综合体建设，项目计划于明年完工。
该综合体将用于验证大规模水电解制氢技术，以及氢气处理、储存和运输相关技术路线。项目的一项主要特点是使用核电站提供的低碳电力，以减少制氢过程对碳氢化合物燃料的依赖。
根据设计方案，该台架试验综合体制氢能力为每小时200标准立方米。项目将分两阶段实施：第一阶段投运每小时50标准立方米的电解装置，并建设氢气储存和处理基础设施;第二阶段将产能提升至每小时200标准立方米的设计水平。建设过程中，项目将重点采用俄罗斯国产现代化设备。
科拉核电站被选为试点场址，主要基于其备用电力容量、电价条件、既有基础设施以及运行人员经验等因素。科拉核电站主管基本建设的副厂长尼古拉·鲁萨科夫 (Nikolai Rusakov) 表示，利用该核电站的条件开展技术验证，有助于在较高效率下推进项目实施。
水电解制氢是通过直流电使水分子在电解槽内分解为氢气和氧气的电化学过程，其中阴极析出氢气，阳极析出氧气。该工艺不使用碳氢化合物原料;若电解装置由低碳电源供电，制氢过程的二氧化碳排放可进一步降低。
氢气在能源和工业领域已有广泛应用。例如，在电力行业，氢气常用于大型汽轮发电机冷却;在化工领域，氢气可作为生产氨、化肥和甲醇的重要原料;在炼油行业，氢气用于加氢精制和重质原料深加工;在冶金领域，氢气也可用于铁矿石直接还原等工艺。
科拉核电站位于俄罗斯摩尔曼斯克州波利亚尔内耶佐里市，是俄罗斯核电站运营公司 (Rosenergoatom) 的分支机构。该站位于摩尔曼斯克市以南约200公里的伊曼德拉湖畔，现有4台VVER型反应堆机组在运，单机容量440兆瓦，发电量约占当地电力平衡的60%。

title: 俄罗斯称尚未收到匈牙利保克什二期核电站谈判邀请
content:
俄罗斯称尚未收到匈牙利保克什二期核电站谈判邀请
9月2日，俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 首席执行官阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexey Likhachev) 在符拉迪沃斯托克举行的东方经济论坛 (Eastern Economic Forum) 期间表示，Rosatom尚未收到匈牙利政府就保克什二期核电站建设项目进行谈判的邀请。
利哈乔夫称，Rosatom已表明愿意以“任何文明的方式”参与有关项目参数的讨论。他表示，公司一贯将合作伙伴和客户利益置于重要位置，并准备对项目技术方案的有效性以及相关财务、经济影响作出说明和论证。
他同时表示，Rosatom多个项目曾经历外部压力考验，但公司认为，这些项目对有关国家民众仍具有价值。

title: 保加利亚批准科兹洛杜伊核电站采购俄制设备
content:
保加利亚批准科兹洛杜伊核电站采购俄制设备
保加利亚政府新闻部门9月2日通报，政府已向科兹洛杜伊核电站 (Kozloduy NPP) 颁发特别许可，允许其从俄罗斯采购维持电站持续安全运行所需的设备和材料。
保加利亚政府表示，保障核安全和机组无事故发电，需要定期从核电站设备的设计方、工程方和制造方获取零部件。由于科兹洛杜伊核电站大部分系统和设备来自俄罗斯，围绕5号、6号机组可靠安全运行所需设备供应的多项合同，已经或即将与俄罗斯供应商签订。
政府还授权保加利亚国家电力公司与俄罗斯原子能建设出口公司 (Atomstroyexport) 签订新合同，为贝莱内核电站 (Belene NPP) 1号、2号机组已交付设备的重新封存工作提供技术指导，以确保相关设备处于安全状态。合同内容显示，俄罗斯专家需参与该项工作。
目前，贝莱内核电站长周期设备重新封存技术指导合同将于2026年12月31日到期。保加利亚方面计划依据公共采购法续签该合同。贝莱内项目于2009年停工后，已交付的俄罗斯VVER-1000型反应堆设备仍留在保加利亚。2012年3月，保加利亚方面放弃继续建设该核电站。
科兹洛杜伊核电站是保加利亚唯一在运核电站，发电量占该国总发电量的三分之一以上。为满足加入欧盟的相关要求，保加利亚分别于2002年和2006年关闭了该电站前四台机组。目前，科兹洛杜伊核电站5号、6号机组保持运行，总装机容量为2000兆瓦。

title: 保加利亚能源部长呼吁协调应对多瑙河低水位影响
content:
保加利亚能源部长呼吁协调应对多瑙河低水位影响
保加利亚能源部长伊娃·彼得罗娃 (Eva Petrova) 9月2日在索非亚出席国民议会能源委员会会议时表示，多瑙河水位持续偏低已对沿岸核电站运行产生影响，各国虽已分别采取应对措施，但仍有必要加强区域层面的协调。
彼得罗娃说，多瑙河目前处于极低水位状态，导致沿河核电站发电量下降，其中包括保加利亚科兹洛杜伊核电站 (Kozloduy Nuclear Power Plant)。她表示，相关预测显示，类似严峻情况今后可能会更加频繁出现。
她介绍，科兹洛杜伊核电站近几个月已积累了低水位条件下的运行经验。能源部近期同电站团队进行了沟通，电站方面已对可能出现的情况作出预判，并形成了在多瑙河极低水位条件下维持运行的实践经验。
彼得罗娃还表示，多瑙河当前水位与一个月前基本相同，科兹洛杜伊核电站团队对此已有应对准备。能源部正对相关情况进行全天候监测，并持续维护有关设施。她说，保方认为后续形势有望趋于稳定，不会出现更为严峻的情况。

title: 印度被敦促调整绿色金融规则以支持核电扩张
content:
印度被敦促调整绿色金融规则以支持核电扩张
印度官员和行业人士近日表示，印度若要实现到2047年将核电装机容量提升至100吉瓦的目标，需要重新审视现有绿色金融规则，并加快培养核能领域专业人才。
印度国家转型委员会 (NITI Aayog) 成员阿巴伊·卡兰迪卡尔 (Abhay Karandikar) 在新德里举行的印度电力展上表示，印度主权绿色债券框架、绿色存款以及相关融资规则目前尚未覆盖核能投资，应进行审查和调整。他说，包括世界银行在内的一些全球金融机构已经开始重新评估相关安排，以支持核能项目投资。
印度目前核电装机容量约为8.8吉瓦。按照规划，该国希望到2047年将这一规模提高至100吉瓦。为实现这一目标，印度核能行业预计需要近2100亿美元投资。印度去年已向私营企业开放长期严格管控的核能行业，以吸引外国技术和资本进入。
除融资规则外，人才储备不足也被认为是印度核电扩张面临的重要制约。行业人士指出，印度清洁能源行业已出现人才短缺，核能领域在专业教育和培训方面的问题更为突出。
法国电力公司 (EDF) 核能项目印度私人有限公司 (EDF Nuclear Projects India Private Limited) 总经理S·卡利拉詹 (Kalirajan S) 表示，印度从中小学到顶尖大学，除少数一流院校外，核能课程设置仍然不足。他说，法国电力公司正与印度供应商开展认证项目，并计划进一步扩大相关工作，以推动当地核能供应链发展。
卡兰迪卡尔表示，印度国家转型委员会已成立一个专门委员会，研究印度如何在技术人员培养、工程能力建设和研发等不同层面扩大核能专业能力。

title: 叙利亚未申报核设施获国际原子能机构确认
content:
叙利亚未申报核设施获国际原子能机构确认
一份联合国机构机密报告显示，国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 核查人员今年8月访问叙利亚多个地点后，确认叙利亚前当局未按《不扩散核武器条约》保障监督协定要求申报相关核材料、核设施和核活动。
报告称，相关信息包括代尔祖尔一座曾处于建设中的核反应堆、一处燃料制造设施，以及前政府时期用于燃料储存的另一处地点。长期以来，外界一直怀疑叙利亚曾秘密推进核计划，其中代尔祖尔省一处设施被认为是由朝鲜协助建设的核反应堆。该设施在2007年遭以色列空袭摧毁后才被公开关注，随后被叙利亚方面夷平。
国际原子能机构此前已于2024年在代尔祖尔地点采集样本，并在去年报告称样本中发现铀颗粒。叙利亚新当局同意该机构进入疑似前核设施开展核查，并表示有意发展民用核能计划;在叙境内发现的任何核材料，将在国际保障监督下由叙利亚保管。
国际原子能机构在报告中说，核查人员于8月29日访问代尔祖尔遗址，以监督挖掘工作进展。根据现场观察，该机构确认，目前发现的冷却基础设施与核反应堆冷却系统特征相符。
报告还指出，有三个地点与代尔祖尔核设施存在“功能关联”。其中一处涉及“转化和/或燃料制造活动”，一处用于“临时存放建筑材料”，另一处用于临时存放进出该设施的建筑材料，并与“计划中的后处理活动”有关。
访问期间，国际原子能机构总干事拉斐尔·格罗西 (Rafael Grossi) 及高级核查员团队还前往叙利亚一处此前未申报地点。叙利亚方面曾在7月17日致信通知该机构该地点存在，并邀请其与叙方合作，对该地点及可能发现的核材料进行检查和核实。
国际原子能机构称，新发现地点存有以燃料棒和包壳形式存在的天然铀金属。经核实，该地点约有73吨天然铀金属。目前，相关核材料均处于国际原子能机构的严密控制和监控之下。

title: 国际原子能机构完成芬兰核与放射性应急准备审查
content:
国际原子能机构完成芬兰核与放射性应急准备审查
国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 专家组近日结束对芬兰核与放射性应急准备和响应框架的审查。此次应急准备审查 (EPREV) 应芬兰政府请求开展，由芬兰辐射与核安全管理局 (STUK) 承办，任务时间为8月24日至9月2日。
审查组重点评估了芬兰应对核与放射性紧急情况的安排和能力，并与国际原子能机构安全标准进行比对。芬兰目前在洛维萨核电站和奥尔基洛托核电站两个厂址运行5台核电机组。其中，洛维萨核电站位于赫尔辛基东北约90公里处，奥尔基洛托核电站位于赫尔辛基西北约270公里处。奥尔基洛托厂址还建有翁卡洛乏燃料地质处置库，这是全球首个用于乏燃料最终处置的地质处置设施。
除核电领域外，放射源还广泛应用于芬兰医疗、工业和科研等领域。审查期间，EPREV团队会见了负责核与放射性应急准备和响应的主要政府部门、国家和地区警察救援部门以及地方公共机构，并参观了奥尔基洛托核电站，审查了洛维萨核电站场外应急响应安排。团队还走访了萨塔赛拉拉医院化学、生物、放射性和核培训中心、食品安全实验室、赫尔辛基市救援部门和民防避难所。
此次国际审查组由法国核安全与辐射防护局 (ASNR) 应急准备与响应副局长奥利维耶·伊斯纳尔 (Olivier Isnard) 率领，成员来自阿根廷、奥地利、加拿大、法国、荷兰、斯洛文尼亚和南非。伊斯纳尔表示，芬兰在核与放射性应急方面投入了大量资源，相关机构展现出较强专业能力;进一步加强国家层面以及不同应急阶段、不同部门之间的系统协调，将有助于更有效发挥现有能力。
审查组认为，芬兰核与放射性应急框架具有多项优势，包括通过国家机制统筹公共机构、行业组织和非政府组织，保障紧急情况下关键社会功能连续运行;萨塔赛拉拉医院也已建立培训计划，用于处置在紧急情况下可能受到放射性污染的人员。
审查组同时提出若干改进建议。相关建议包括：在准备阶段建立更完善的国家协调机制;依据国际原子能机构安全标准制定国家辐射应急计划，明确各级别、各阶段响应中的角色、责任和协调安排;制定管理核事故或放射性事故去污活动所产生放射性废物的法律规定;进一步完善公众保护、应急和救援人员防护、公共信息沟通以及国际援助纳入国家响应体系的安排;提升实验室对环境、食品和水样品的分析能力。
芬兰核安全局局长卡里姆·佩尔托宁 (Karim Peltonen) 表示，EPREV任务提出的观察意见将为芬兰完善核与放射性应急准备安排提供重要参考，尤其有助于加强参与准备和响应各方之间的协调。

title: 日本伊方核电站1号机组退役第二阶段获县委员会认可
content:
日本伊方核电站1号机组退役第二阶段获县委员会认可
日本爱媛县“伊方核电站环境安全管理委员会”9月2日在松山市召开会议，围绕四国电力公司 (Shikoku Electric Power) 计划推进伊方核电站1号机组退役第二阶段工作进行讨论。该机组位于爱媛县伊方町，目前正处于退役过程中。
伊方核电站1号机组的退役工作被划分为四个主要阶段。四国电力此前已就进入下一阶段向爱媛县和伊方町提出事前协商，并获得地方同意，同时向日本原子能规制委员会 (NRA) 提交相关申请。今年7月，原子能规制委员会批准了该申请。
在2日的会议上，爱媛县方面说明，依据国家审批结果，县专家小组已编制完成关于第二阶段安全保障措施的报告。报告认为，国家层面的审查程序和结论总体适当。
报告同时要求四国电力采取必要措施，避免第二阶段退役过程中产生的低放射性废物在厂址内长期滞留;在作业实施过程中，应加强放射性物质扩散防控，并确保辐射管理信息的透明性。
会议最终在未提出异议的情况下通过了该报告。爱媛县表示，委员会审议结果将提交知事。知事将在听取县议会和伊方町意见后，决定是否同意四国电力推进伊方核电站1号机组退役第二阶段工作。

title: 日本川内核电站完成新燃料运抵
content:
日本川内核电站完成新燃料运抵
九州电力株式会社 (Kyushu Electric Power Co.) 9月2日发布消息称，日本川内核电站1号、2号机组所需新燃料已完成运抵。此次运输工作于2026年8月30日开始，至9月2日结束。
根据九州电力公布的信息，本次运抵的新燃料由原子燃料工业株式会社 (Nuclear Fuel Industries, Ltd.) 加工制造。其中，川内核电站1号机组新燃料为24组，使用12具运输容器;2号机组新燃料为28组，使用14具运输容器。
此次新燃料运输采用陆路与海路相结合的方式进行。九州电力表示，相关燃料已按计划运抵川内核电站。

title: 瑞典1.2吉瓦BWRX-300核电项目确定战略合作方
content:
BWRX-300
小型模块化反应堆
Studsvik
斯图兹维克公司 (Studsvik AB) 9月3日宣布，已在竞争性评估后选择GE Vernova日立核能公司 (GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy) 和三星物产 (Samsung C&T) 作为其在瑞典首个核电项目的战略合作伙伴。项目计划在斯图兹维克位于尼雪平的现有许可厂址，或位于瓦尔德马斯维克的Målma厂址推进。
根据安排，各方将与GE Vernova金融服务业务以及DS投资伙伴公司 (DS Investment Partners) 合作，推进瑞典首个由4台BWRX-300机组组成的核电项目，总装机容量约1.2吉瓦。首台机组预计在21世纪30年代中期投入运行。
该项目属于斯图兹维克旗下ReFirm新核能开发平台。ReFirm是一个面向多厂址小型模块化反应堆及先进核电项目的平台，斯图兹维克今年早些时候通过收购Kärnfull Next (KNXT) 获得该项目。KNXT自2022年起一直与GE Vernova日立核能公司合作，推动BWRX-300在瑞典部署，并于2024年12月与三星物产签署战略合作协议。
在尼雪平，斯图兹维克目前运营着一处已获许可的核设施。在瓦尔德马斯维克，该公司已于2026年3月提交申请，这是瑞典相关新规生效后，核设施建设项目首次依据新要求申请政府批准。首个项目的最终选址将在后续开发过程中确定。
各方表示，项目将采用分阶段、多机组推进方式，以提高设计、采购、施工和后续运营环节的标准化水平，并将早期机组建设经验用于后续机组，从而改善成本、工期和施工效率。这一模式也将为瑞典本土企业参与工程设计、设备采购、建设和长期运营创造条件，并支持面向后续项目的供应链建设。
本次协议为独家合作协议，设有固定期限，并可由各方续签。协议标志着项目进入联合开发阶段，但不构成最终投资决定，也不等同于建设许可。独家合作期内，各方将围绕商业模式、技术方案、监管许可和融资安排开展工作。
根据分工，斯图兹维克将负责许可审批、环境影响评估、场地权益、社区沟通以及与瑞典政府的对接。GE Vernova日立核能公司将负责反应堆工程、许可支持和成本估算，并担任工程技术权威机构;该公司还将与三星物产共同组成项目执行团队，为建设和交付提供统一责任安排。独家谈判期间，DS投资伙伴公司将牵头投资工作，GE Vernova金融服务业务将以顾问和财务结构顾问身份参与。
各方还计划成立一家项目公司，负责核电站开发、融资、建设、所有权和运营等工作，具体安排将在最终协议中确定。
瑞典正依据2026年生效的新法律扩大核电发展空间。新规允许在现有三座核电站以外的地点建设反应堆，但每座反应堆仍需获得政府批准，并可在国家贷款、双向差价合约等融资框架下获得支持。

title: 罗马尼亚切尔纳沃德核电站9月10日前难以重启
content:
罗马尼亚切尔纳沃德核电站9月10日前难以重启
罗马尼亚切尔纳沃德核电站 (Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant) 预计难以在9月10日前恢复运行。罗马尼亚能源部 (Romanian Ministry of Energy) 国务秘书克里斯蒂安·布索伊 (Cristian Bușoi) 表示，虽然多瑙河流量正在回升，但核电站周边水位尚未达到安全、稳定重启所需条件。
布索伊在近日受访时说，为避免外界形成不切实际的预期，目前可以确认的是，9月10日前切尔纳沃德核电站尚不具备重启条件。他解释称，核电站运行依赖稳定水源，以保障反应堆冷却系统正常工作。河流水量短期增加并不足以支持机组恢复生产，若重启后水位再次下降，核电站仍可能在数日内被迫停运。
约三周前，受多瑙河水位显著下降影响，切尔纳沃德核电站暂停发电。为保障进水口水量，当地随后采取应急措施，包括清除一块阻碍水流的岩石，并有意沉没4艘驳船，以引导更多水流进入核电站取水区域。
此次停运暴露出在长期低水位条件下，罗马尼亚部分电力基础设施对河流水文状况的依赖。高温天气和用电需求上升，也进一步放大了电力供应压力。布索伊表示，政府目标是确保切尔纳沃德核电站两台反应堆在今年秋季和初冬保持运行，以应对预计增长的电力需求。
此外，切尔纳沃德核电站1号机组计划于明年启动大规模现代化改造，届时该机组将停运两年以上。因此，在寒冷季节到来以及1号机组长期停运前，保障核电站稳定运行对罗马尼亚电力供应具有重要意义。
目前，当局将运行安全置于优先位置。多瑙河水位能否持续稳定，仍是切尔纳沃德核电站恢复运行的关键条件。

title: 美国PACMAN人工智能框架实现聚变等离子体毫秒级控制
content:
PACMAN人工智能框架
聚变等离子体控制
DIII-D国家聚变设施
美国能源部普林斯顿等离子体物理实验室 (PPPL) 与普林斯顿大学 (Princeton University) 研究人员开发的PACMAN人工智能框架，已在真实聚变实验系统中完成五项实验验证。该框架可在约20毫秒内完成数据处理、状态预测和控制指令输出，用于应对聚变等离子体中快速发展的不稳定性。
这是艺术家对PACMAN融合系统人工智能框架的诠释。(插图来源：Kyle Palmer / PPPL通信部)
PACMAN全称为“基于机器学习的预测与控制”。相关设计和初步实验结果已发表于《核聚变》期刊。研究团队表示，托卡马克装置中的等离子体温度、密度和稳定性需要持续调节，加热系统、磁体和气体注入等参数都可能影响放电状态。部分等离子体扰动可在毫秒级时间内增长，传统人工操作难以及时响应。
该框架的核心是将多个机器学习模型和控制器接入同一控制回路。系统首先采集托卡马克的实时测量数据，包括温度、密度和磁信号;随后检查数据误差并完成整理;机器学习模型据此预测等离子体当前状态或即将出现的变化;控制器再计算加热束调节等操作指令;最后由输出环节协调不同控制器之间的指令冲突，执行硬件安全限制，并将控制指令发送至装置。
研究团队在美国DIII-D国家聚变设施 (DIII-D National Fusion Facility) 的托卡马克装置上完成了五项实验。实验中，PACMAN实现了由强化学习训练的人工智能模型对加热系统的控制，预测了等离子体边缘能量突发，探测并调控了由高速粒子驱动的等离子体波，还对等离子体密度和旋转状态进行了调节，使其接近预设目标。
在一项实验中，机器学习模型提前约200毫秒预测到撕裂模不稳定性，使系统能够在不稳定性形成前调整等离子体状态。研究人员称，传统控制器通常只能在撕裂模出现后进行抑制，可能导致等离子体性能明显下降。PACMAN还同时调控了DIII-D装置的六个回旋管，通过实时调整回旋管镜面方向和功率，完成预设控制目标。
研究人员强调，PACMAN并不意味着由人工智能完全取代人类操作。该框架内置硬件和运行安全限制，人工智能模型提出的控制建议仍需在既定边界内执行;每次实验后，物理学家还会审查数据，并据此调整下一轮实验的控制参数。
由于PACMAN采用模块化架构，新的机器学习模型和控制器可在不影响其他模块的情况下接入系统。研究团队认为，这一方式有望从DIII-D扩展到不同尺寸、不同构型和不同诊断配置的托卡马克装置，为后续聚变等离子体控制研究提供可复用的软件基础。

title: 美国Realta Fusion与MGE拟合作开发200兆瓦聚变电站
content:
美国Realta Fusion与MGE拟合作开发200兆瓦聚变电站
从事磁镜聚变能源技术开发的瑞尔塔聚变公司 (Realta Fusion) 9月2日宣布，已与麦迪逊天然气电力公司 (Madison Gas and Electric, MGE) 及其母公司MGE能源公司 (MGE Energy, Inc.) 建立战略合作伙伴关系，双方将共同评估在美国威斯康星州联合开发一座200兆瓦电功率级聚变能源发电厂的可能性。
根据合作安排，第一阶段内容包括MGE能源公司对瑞尔塔聚变公司进行直接股权投资。MGE还同意向瑞尔塔聚变公司提供设备、工程和技术支持，并在项目选址、许可、并网和融资等方面提供协助，为拟建200兆瓦聚变发电项目推进前期工作。
瑞尔塔聚变公司首席执行官基兰·弗隆 (Kieran Furlong) 表示，与MGE共同探索建设聚变电站，显示聚变能源正向实际应用迈进。他说，聚变能源有望成为满足零碳电力需求的重要来源，MGE的参与将为相关技术走向工程化提供支持。
MGE董事长、总裁兼首席执行官杰夫·基布勒 (Jeff Keebler) 表示，实现净零碳排放需要创新、合作以及对新兴技术的持续探索。瑞尔塔聚变公司正在麦迪逊开发聚变技术，此次合作体现了MGE评估新兴无碳能源技术的意愿，相关技术未来有望为客户和社区提供可靠、全天候的无碳电力。
该合作也延续了双方此前的联系。瑞尔塔聚变公司近期宣布，计划租赁约25万平方英尺办公和工业空间，用于建设其研发中心Realta Forge。该中心位于MGE服务区域内，所在地为OM Station，即原奥斯卡·梅尔公司 (Oscar Mayer) 工厂及总部旧址。
MGE将减少碳排放列为核心目标之一。2019年，MGE成为美国较早承诺到2050年实现净零碳电力的公用事业公司之一。该公司表示，持续投资无碳发电是其能源战略的一部分，目标是保障未来能源供应安全、可靠、经济并具备可持续性。
瑞尔塔聚变公司总部位于威斯康星州麦迪逊市，正在开发基于磁镜聚变概念的紧凑型、可扩展、模块化CoSMo聚变能源系统。该公司获得科斯拉风险投资公司 (Khosla Ventures) 和未来风险投资公司 (Future Ventures) 支持，是美国能源部“里程碑式聚变开发计划”入选企业之一，并被世界经济论坛评为2026年技术先锋企业。瑞尔塔聚变公司还在威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校物理科学实验室运行威斯康星高温超导轴对称磁镜聚变装置。
MGE为威斯康星州戴恩县约17万用户发电和配电，并向威斯康星州中南部及西部七个县约18万用户采购和供应天然气。其母公司MGE能源公司在麦迪逊地区已有150多年运营历史。

8月30日，中国石油吉林油田45万千瓦风光发电项目正式宣告全容量并网投产。
吉林油田45万千瓦风光发电项目充分盘活油田闲置土地、低效井场、排涝区等空间，统筹采用"光伏+风电"复合布局，推行“分期开工、分步实施”模式，10万千瓦光伏和35万千瓦风电两部分“并肩战斗”，全力保障建设效率与效益。
“风电项目于2025年12月16日正式开工建设，10万千瓦光伏部分今年2月实现投产，截至目前，项目累计发电8762.5万千瓦时。”吉林油田新能源建设项目部副经理曲乃涛说，项目开工建设以来，新能源生产一线广大干部员工直面极寒施工、大风吊装、征地协调等诸多难题，锚定投产节点，质量与安全同步推进，进度与合规协同管控，从而圆满完成了各项攻坚任务，为区域绿色低碳发展注入强劲新动力。

title: 国际新能源网-太阳能光伏行业专业门户网站
content:
日期：2026-09-03
国际太阳能光伏网
2026年9月1日，孟加拉国政府通过能源、电力和矿产资源部发布通知，推出一项针对居民太阳能发电盈余并入电网的上网电价补贴计划。
该计划主要依赖电池储能技术，使太阳能发电能够在白天以外的时间也能使用。
像Ascend Analytics这样的专业公司正在大规模部署这项技术，该公司在北美管理着超过5.2吉瓦的电池储能容量。由于国内天然气长期短缺以及进口液化天然气供应中断，电力供需缺口进一步扩大。
根据当地媒体转述的政府说法，近期电力产量下降主要归因于国内因素——天然气终端中断和煤炭处理受限——而非地区冲突对国家能源供应的直接机械性影响。面对这种情况，当局选择加快部署家用储能太阳能系统，因为该系统比大型地面太阳能项目更容易实施。
该方案基于现有的净计量框架，该框架由前任政府制定并由现任政府继续沿用。并入电网的电力回购价格通过在当局设定的生产成本上限基础上加上利润和溢价计算得出。根据通知中所述的条款，安装成本低于该上限的电力系统的消费者可以将差价作为自己的利润。
尽管孟加拉国在2026年2月经历了政治过渡，但这种监管的连续性表明该国能源政策的稳定性。在世界上人口最稠密的国家之一，可用于大规模安装的土地仍然稀缺，因此，当局认为，与大型地面安装式太阳能项目相比，带储能功能的住宅太阳能是一种部署速度更快的解决方案。
这项电价激励措施是国家战略的一部分，旨在到2030年提高可再生能源在电力结构中的占比，并重申了2040年的中期目标。然而，为实现这一目标所需的新增装机容量规模，因所采用的来源和需求增长假设的不同，估计结果存在差异。自2026年2月17日接替穆罕默德·尤努斯领导的过渡政府担任总理以来，塔里克·拉赫曼已将电力供应列为政府的优先事项之一。能源、电力和矿产资源部长伊克巴尔·哈桑·马哈茂德和自2026年2月起接替纳斯鲁尔·哈米德担任同一职务的国务部长阿南迪亚·伊斯兰·阿米特正在监督该计划的实施。
由于当局试图证明其有能力保障国家电力供应，部分民众对反复停电仍感到不满，社会氛围依然紧张。2026年9月1日的通知中并未披露生产成本上限的具体水平以及奖励金额。

墨西哥联邦电力公司（CFE）计划到2030年投资6510亿墨西哥比索（约合329亿美元），安装18.6GW的新增发电装机容量，其中82%为可再生能源。该计划包括确定的5.48GW太阳能项目，并提及电池储能，但并未设定具体的储能容量或投资目标。
墨西哥国家电力公司联邦电力委员会（CFE）发布了其2026-2030年发展计划，概述了在此期间对发电、输电和配电领域6510亿墨西哥比索（329亿美元）的投资。其中，发电项目投资4673亿墨西哥比索（234亿美元），涵盖52个项目，新增装机容量18.6GW。
根据该文件，计划新增发电量中，15.2GW（占82%）将来自墨西哥联邦电力公司（CFE）归类为可再生能源的技术。这其中包括1.69GW的热电联产，该公司将其归入此类是因为其不产生污染排放。剩余的3.39GW将主要来自新建的联合循环发电厂。
大部分新增可再生能源装机容量将采用混合投资模式开发，并引入私营部门参与。墨西哥联邦电力公司（CFE）计划根据这些安排建设约13.8GW的可再生能源项目，主要包括太阳能和风能项目。
该计划确定了 30 个混合投资太阳能项目，总装机容量为 4.90 GW，计划于 2028 年至 2030 年间并网发电。此外，索诺拉州的普埃尔托佩尼亚斯科太阳能发电厂第三期和第四期工程也包含在内，这两期工程总装机容量为 580 兆瓦，预计将于 2028 年开始运营。该计划明确确定的太阳能项目总装机容量为 5.48 GW。
该计划还包括八个总装机容量为 3.13 GW的混合投资风电项目、582 兆瓦的地热发电容量、两个总装机容量为 150 兆瓦的聚光太阳能发电 (CSP) 项目，以及另外 4.15 GW的混合投资项目，但其技术尚未确定。
根据墨西哥联邦电力公司（CFE）纳入该文件的更广泛的电力行业发展计划（PLADESE），太阳能是墨西哥国家电力系统（SEN）预计新增装机容量的主要来源。预计到2030年，太阳能发电将新增12.31GW的装机容量，占该系统规划新增28.00GW装机容量的44%。风能发电占6.58GW，而联合循环发电厂则贡献了5.44GW。
截至2025年12月，墨西哥已接入国家电网（SEN）的太阳能发电容量为8.44GW，约占该系统总装机容量91.07GW的9%。其中，墨西哥联邦电力公司（CFE）直接拥有433MW太阳能发电容量。2025年，该公司新增约307MW太阳能发电容量，主要得益于纳奇-科科姆（Nachi-Cocom）电站的投产以及普埃尔托佩尼亚斯科（Puerto Pe?asco）项目二期工程的竣工。

日期：2026-09-03
国际太阳能光伏网
据最新报告显示，印度从依赖进口90%以上的太阳能组件，转变为世界第二大太阳能组件制造中心，截至2026年6月，其产能将达到233吉瓦。然而，产能扩张速度超过了市场需求，导致工厂的利用率仅为35%至40%，低于通常认为可持续运营所需的50%至65%。
据美国能源经济与金融分析研究所 (IEEFA) 和 JMK Research 发布的一份新报告《评估
光伏制造市场的产能过剩风险》发现，印度目前的组件制造能力几乎是其电池产能的7倍，是其硅锭和硅片产能的116倍。这导致电池、硅片和多晶硅等上游环节相对落后，供应链依赖进口原材料，主要来自中国。
“印度新增组件产能的速度超过了市场消化能力，”JMK Research高级顾问兼该报告的主要作者普拉巴卡尔·夏尔马表示。“目前已有约135吉瓦的新增产能正在规划或建设中，而工厂的开工率仅为35%至40%，这将加剧产能利用率、利润率和回报方面的压力。独立组件制造商面临着资产搁浅的切实风险。”
报告指出，这种不平衡状况到2030年不太可能缓解。印度的太阳能部署预计将强劲增长，但速度不足以消化已承诺的制造产能。
报告指出，到2030年，数据中心、绿色氢气和氨的生产以及出口带来的额外需求可能新增17至22吉瓦的能源需求。绿色氢气是潜在新增需求的最大来源，因为其生产需要专门的可再生能源发电能力。然而，研究人员表示，这些新增需求不足以完全消化已规划的制造业扩张。
因此，出口可能发挥越来越重要的作用。报告显示，印度的组件出口高度集中于美国，2026财年美国出口量约占印度总出口量的97%。
由于美国对大多数印度制造商征收超过200%的综合关税，该市场受到冲击。报告称，这些措施导致印度对美国的出口额较2024财年的峰值下降了44%至47%。欧盟可能提供一个中期替代方案，因为其供应链和采购政策日益鼓励多元化。
“如果印度太阳能光伏制造商能够通过投资研发和多晶硅、硅锭、硅片和电池的生产，有效地与中国制造商竞争，那么印度就有机会开拓新的出口市场，”能源经济与金融分析研究所 (IEEFA) 首席能源专家、该报告的撰稿人之一 Charith Ko
报告预计，产能与需求之间日益扩大的差距将推动整个行业的变革。规模较小、非一体化的制造商可能面临更大的压力，而规模较大、垂直一体化的生产商则可能更能抵御较低的产能利用率。
研究人员还预计，印度制造业将进一步向上游发展，从组件到电池、晶圆，最终到多晶硅，从而减少对进口原材料的依赖。
Tewani表示，激励措施应该更均匀地分配到电池、晶圆和多晶硅上，而不是集中在组件上，同时加强产业研究合作，并为出口商提供有针对性的、有时限的支持。
该报告还呼吁加快输电线路建设和通行权（RoW）清理，以支持国内太阳能项目部署，并制定老旧太阳能项目改造框架。
研究人员得出结论，目前组件生产的过剩可能是印度快速扩张的太阳能产业的一个过渡阶段。他们表示，更强劲的需求、行业整合以及对上游制造环节更审慎的投资，将有助于在未来十年内实现该行业的平衡。

title: 国际新能源网-太阳能光伏行业专业门户网站
content:
日期：2026-09-03
国际太阳能光伏网
近日，MN8 Energy、Eos Energy Enterprises Inc和 Google 宣布建立合作伙伴关系，将在美国 PJM 电网中交付一个 86 兆瓦的
位于西弗吉尼亚州卡纳瓦县的猛犸太阳能项目（Mammoth）将由独立电力生产商 MN8 所有并运营。该项目将配备 70 MW/280MWh锂离子
，以及由美国制造商 Eos 提供的 10MW/100MWh锌基长时储能系统 (LDES)。
谷歌将购买该项目的电力，为其在该地区（包括西弗吉尼亚州的一个规划项目）的数据中心供电。该交易也是谷歌加速LDES技术商业化举措的一部分。
该项目总投资额高达3.5亿美元（3.02亿欧元），将建在已复垦的煤矿上。太阳能部分预计将于2028年投入运营，锂离子电池储能系统将于2029年投入运营，低压配电系统将于2030年投入运营。
这是首个采用Eos美国制造的Z3技术并获得谷歌支持的项目。该项目也是MN8与Eos此前宣布的主供货协议下的首个项目。
与此同时，美国地热开发商 Fervo Energy 周二宣布与谷歌达成协议，将从其位于犹他州的 Cape Station GeoCluster 项目中向这家科技集团供应 396 兆瓦电力。

title: 国际新能源网-太阳能光伏行业专业门户网站
content:
日期：2026-09-03
国际太阳能光伏网
泰国能源部日前宣布，取消此前针对数据中心设置的2000兆瓦直接
交易上限，并将适用范围由数据中心扩大至各类产业，以进一步推动
发展、满足企业日益增长的绿色电力需求。
本次政策的核心抓手是第三方输电接入机制（TPA，Third Party Access）。在泰国长期以国有电力机构为主导的电力格局下，企业过去购电高度依赖国家电网统一转售。新政下，企业可直接向可再生能源发电企业采购清洁电力，不再完全依赖国有机构供电，相当于在企业与
发电商之间打开了“点对点”直购通道。
对跨国科技与制造业巨头而言，这条通道意义不小，其数据中心的绿地投资普遍有明确的绿电采购（RE100/碳中和）要求，能否“直购绿电”直接影响项目落地决策。
这次变化可以拆成两层看：
取消2000兆瓦上限——此前即便数据中心能直购绿电，也受总量额度约束，存在“抢额度”问题；
从数据中心扩展至各类产业——制造业、化工等大型工商业同样可参与，让直购从“点状试点”升级为面向全市场的开放通道。
需求侧放开，往往能撬动供给侧。绿电直购市场打开，有望带动泰国可再生能源新增装机，也让购售电价更多由买卖双方协商形成、倒逼批发电价机制更趋市场化，绿电可得性也成为泰国吸引外资与数据中心的新卖点。
当然，开放不等于马上落地。需求放开若快于新能源装机和输电通道供给，TPA能否真正跑通要打问号；以光伏、风电为主的直购绿电若无储能配套，供电稳定性与辅助服务成本如何分摊，也需后续细则跟上。并网、计量、绿证归属等执行条款仍待进一步明确。
这一动向背后是一条东南亚共同脉络，为承接AI与数据中心需求、同时兑现减碳承诺，多国正陆续放开“企业绿电直购/购电协议”大门。
对中国企业而言，既意味着出海建厂/建数据中心时绿电可得性上升、更易满足国际客户减碳要求，也提示光伏、风电、储能出海的海外业主市场正在扩大。
反过来看，以市场化机制撬动绿电消纳，已是区域共识，也值得国内绿电市场与PPA机制演进对照思考。

title: 10亿元！国创中心湖南一新能源产业基地迎新动态
content:
湘江智能网联产业园P19-A81地块（面积约126.2亩）由长沙矿山研究院有限责任公司竞得，将用于建设战略性稀有金属矿产高效开发国家技术创新中心新能源与智能装备检测基地。
图片来源：湖南湘江新区
“湖南湘江新区”消息显示，9月1日，湘江智能网联产业园P19-A81地块（面积约126.2亩）由长沙矿山研究院有限责任公司竞得，将用于建设战略性稀有金属矿产高效开发国家技术创新中心新能源与智能装备检测基地（简称“国创中心检测基地”），总投资约10亿元，投产后预计新增就业岗位450个。
该基地规划布局数字算力中心等18个专项实验室、4大功能中心及235台套专业检测设备，重点开展矿山智能装备、矿用机器人、新能源运载工具及下一代通信智联系统的检验检测与仪器制造认证业务。
项目选址湘江智能网联产业园，主要基于技术同源与产业协同优势。据悉，该园区聚焦智能网联及低空经济，与基地检测方向高度契合；同时周边电力、物流及公辅配套可满足大型装备检测需求。项目负责人表示，将积极借鉴园区智能网联汽车测试标准，优先对接园区内整车、核心零部件、新能源装备及机器人企业，并联合第三方机构推动标准共建与试验资源共享，带动传感器、控制器、工业软件等上下游企业集聚。

title: 30亿元正极项目之后 超钠新能源6GWh钠电池项目再落四川绵竹
content:
早在2024年1月，超钠新能源就曾在四川绵竹落户钠离子电池正极材料项目，项目规划总投资30亿元。
图片来源：绵竹市人民政府
据绵竹市人民政府消息，8月28日上午，湖州超钠新能源科技有限公司（简称：超钠新能源）年产6GWh钠离子电池生产线项目签约仪式在四川绵竹举行，绵竹高新区管委会与超钠新能源签订《投资协议书》。
电池网注意到，早在2024年1月，超钠新能源就曾在四川绵竹落户钠离子电池正极材料项目，项目规划总投资30亿元，建设年产8万吨钠离子电池正极材料，其中一期项目投资5亿元，实现年产2万吨钠离子电池正极材料。
资料显示，超钠新能源成立于2021年8月，以浙大教授团队为公司核心，实现多平台研发资源整合，拥有超100项钠离子电池核心技术与专利，是行业内少有的拥有钠离子电池核心研发能力的企业之一，已完成中建八局、国家能源集团、国家电网钠离子储能商业项目应用，台铃两轮车及旭派电源启动电源项目应用。
今年5月，超钠新能源还与巴基斯坦RIC集团签署战略合作协议。双方将基于钠离子电池技术、硅基新能源材料、储能系统解决方案、本地化生产与市场推广等领域开展全方位深度合作。其中，超钠新能源将向巴基斯坦市场输出自研普鲁士蓝钠离子电池、核心正极材料及全套储能系统解决方案，并依托RIC集团优质硅矿资源优势，打通新能源上游材料产业链。

title: 总投资约7亿元！河北张家口一储能电站正式投运
content:
河北燕赵沽源储能示范项目由建投储能（沽源）电力有限责任公司投资建设，总投资约7亿元。
据沽源县融媒体中心消息，近日，位于河北省张家口市沽源县西辛营乡的河北燕赵沽源储能示范项目实现全容量并网，300兆瓦/600兆瓦时独立储能电站正式投运。
据悉，该项目由建投储能（沽源）电力有限责任公司投资建设，总投资约7亿元。项目今年4月10日正式开工，面对坝上高寒、施工窗口期短等不利条件，参建各方抢抓工期，于6月30日首次并网，近日实现全容量并网。
项目采用磷酸铁锂电化学储能技术，设置48组6.25兆瓦/12.5兆瓦时标准化储能单元，配套新建220千伏升压站及送出线路，电能经升压后接入白土窑500千伏变电站，并入冀北主电网。整套系统配置电池管理、储能变流、能量管理平台，依靠智能化技术实时监测电池健康状态，模块化设计便于调度运维，系统安全性能处于行业先进水平。
