title: Danish wind firm contests state aid for offshore wind
content:
Danish onshore wind company Dansk Vindenergi has lodged a case with the Court of Justice of the EU, seeking annulment of the European Commission's decision that approves Danish state aid for the Hesselo and North Sea I Mid offshore wind projects.
The tender for the two projects, with a combined capacity of at least 1.8 GW, was
recently won by Vattenfall
. The Swedish utility secured state support in the form of 20-year, two-way Contracts for Difference (CfD). The Danish government
moved to offer state support
to offshore wind developers after its previous offshore wind auction in December 2024 got no bids. The European Commission
approved the support scheme
for the two projects in March.
Dansk Vindenergi is also seeking interim measures to suspend the approval pending the resolution of the case. According to the Court of Justice’s case-law database, Dansk Vindenergi’s application was filed on July 30.
The company argues that state support for offshore wind is distorting competition as it could reduce the price onshore wind turbines could get for their electricity in the future, according to a publication in Børsen.dk.
CEO Niels Mejlholm told the newspaper that it is impossible to make an investment calculation when the price of electricity is politically determined, and also makes it impossible to secure financing because the banks do not know either.
The Danish government has moved to intervene in the case in support of the European Commission, according to a note filed with parliament in late August by Minister for Climate, Energy and Utilities Samira Nawa.
In the document, the government says it is important that Dansk Vindenergi does not succeed in its claims, as this would mean that state aid could not be paid to the two offshore wind farms as provided for in the contracts. In addition, the development of future offshore wind farms could be challenged if it becomes more difficult to grant state aid.
The government also said that in its view, the Commission’s decision is lawful.
Dansk Vindenergi is a company that currently owns and operates 50 wind turbines in Denmark, producing electricity to meet the annual consumption of about 25,000 Danish households, according to its website.

title: EIB raises financing framework for Ren-Gas projects to EUR 680m
content:
The European Investment Bank (EIB) has increased its financing framework for Finnish green hydrogen and e-methane project developer Ren-Gas to EUR 680 million (USD 791.3m) from EUR 230 million previously.
The framework is designed to provide project-level debt financing for Ren-Gas' portfolio of e-methane projects in Finland. The financing approval comes as the company prepares to move its first project into construction in the fourth quarter of 2026, a plant in Tampere, southern Finland.
Ren-Gas develops RFNBO-compliant e-methane projects that convert renewable hydrogen and captured biogenic CO2 into renewable gas for heavy transport, maritime and other hard-to-abate sectors. Its project portfolio consists of six projects at home.
The company said it has secured long-term off-take agreements for green hydrogen and heat from its projects, providing a basis for project financing. Its customer base includes, among others, European
renewable LNG platform avanca Energy
.

title: Enersense to operate Alight's 101-MWp solar park in Finland
content:
Finnish green energy services provider Enersense International Oyj (HEL:ESENSE) has secured a contract to operate and maintain a
recently-commissioned
, 101-MWp solar park of Alight in the country.
The solar installation, located in the municipality of Eurajoki on Finland’s west coast, produces around 100 GWh annually. The generation is sufficient to meet the needs of about 20,000 households.
Enersense said on Friday that it signed agreements for the solar park and its associated substation. The company will be responsible for the comprehensive operation and maintenance of the solar power plant as well as operational management, fault response, inspection and maintenance services for the substation.
Enersense designs, builds, maintains and modernises critical infrastructure across the Nordics and the Baltics. In 2025, the firm generated revenue of EUR 307 million (USD 356.76m).

title: Engie acquires 438-MW battery storage project in Poland
content:
The local unit of French utility Engie SA (EPA:ENGI) announced today the acquisition of a 438-MW/876-MWh energy storage project in central Poland.
Engie Zielona Energia has acquired the special purpose vehicle (SPV) responsible for the large-scale battery storage project, developed so far by Mithra Energy and a member of the Futureal Group. The project is scheduled to reach a shovel-ready status in the fourth quarter, while commissioning is planned for the first quarter of 2029.
The storage facility in Trebaczew, the Lodz province, will be strategically connected directly to the Trebaczew power station, which will facilitate power evacuation, reducing the burden on the local transmission infrastructure and increasing the overall power reliability throughout the region, Engie said in a press release.
The deal is another important step for Engie in building a portfolio of assets supporting grid stability, security of supply, and the energy transition in Poland, Engie said referring to the recent acquisition of the
250-MW/1,000-MWh BESS
project in Tursko Wielkie.
"Expanding our portfolio of large-scale energy storage facilities is a priority for us, as these installations constitute an essential foundation for a modern, renewable-based economy," pointed out Piotr Rogiz, country manager at Engie Polska.
In July and August alone, the group expanded its European energy storage portfolio through a series of strategic acquisitions, construction starts and project commissionings in a number of European countries, representing a total capacity of 1.1 GW/3.3 GWh.

title: Eurowind closes deal for EnBW's Swedish renewables platform
content:
German utility EnBW Energie Baden-Wuerttemberg AG (ETR:EBK) has closed the sale of its Swedish renewable energy platform to Denmark's Eurowind Energy A/S, divesting about 120 MW of operating onshore wind farms and a development portfolio.
The Danish renewables company said on Thursday it had finalised
the deal
, which was subject to approval under Sweden's foreign direct investment screening regime. Apart from power assets and projects in development, the platform also includes an operations and maintenance (O&M) business.
Financial details remain undisclosed.
“This acquisition gives us a solid basis for long-term growth in Sweden. With skilled colleagues, operating assets and new development opportunities, we are well positioned to grow our business and contribute to Sweden’s future energy supply,” said Anders Widman, country manager Sweden at Eurowind Energy.
Eurowind Energy said the acquired O&M business will operate in cooperation with Connected Wind Services Danmark A/S, its Danish wind turbine servicing business. Connected Wind Services Danmark, which was also
acquired from EnBW
, has the potential to expand to Sweden as well, the company added.
EnBW said earlier that the sale would mark its withdrawal from the development and operation of wind and solar projects in the Nordic markets, allowing it to focus on its core geographies.

title: Flex to acquire power conversion tech maker EPC Power for USD 4.4bn
content:
Flex (NASDAQ:FLEX) has agreed to acquire US power conversion technology company EPC Power Corp for USD 4.4 billion (EUR 3.78bn), gaining technology and manufacturing capabilities that serve data centres, utility-scale energy storage and microgrids.
EPC Power develops and manufactures high-performance, software-defined power conversion solutions. The acquisition will add EPC Power's power conversion platform to Flex's portfolio of power and thermal management technologies for critical infrastructure.
Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Cleanhill Partners are the company's current controlling shareholders. Cleanhill Partners first invested in EPC Power in 2021, citing power conversion as an enabling technology for renewable generation, grid modernisation and digital infrastructure.
The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals and is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. Upon completion, EPC Power will become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment.

title: Floating wind turbine for UK gas field arrives on site
content:
The single 3-MW floating turbine that will
power the Culzean gas platform
in the UK Central North Sea has been towed from Wergeland Base in Gulen, Norway, to its site at the gas field, Norwegian Offshore Wind said on Wednesday.
This is one of 13 projects that secured seabed rights under Crown Estate Scotland's Innovation and Targeted Oil and Gas (INTOG)
leasing round in 2023
and the first of them to be installed, the industry organisation said.
The project is now operated by NEO NEXT+ Energy after the merger earlier this year of NEO Energy, Repsol UK and TotalEnergies' UK upstream business.
The turbine was assembled at Wergeland Base in western Norway, part of Wergeland Group. Archer Wind, the floating wind unit of Norwegian oilfield services group Archer, acted as EPC contractor. The floating turbine foundation is based on a design from Ocergy, in which Archer Wind owns a minority stake. It supports a 3-MW Vestas turbine that is expected to meet around 20% of the Culzean platform's power demand.

title: Ireland to study geothermal heating potential beneath Dublin
content:
Ireland will conduct a survey to collect geothermal information from deep beneath Dublin city in order to assess the potential of renewable geothermal heat.
The Dublin Seismic Survey project was announced on Thursday by the Department of Climate, Energy and the Environment at the European Geothermal District Heating and Cooling Days 2026 conference.
The survey will use non-invasive geophysical technology to image the subsurface up to 3 km below ground. The data will reduce uncertainty for deep geothermal projects across Ireland’s capital and support planned deep geothermal drilling at Grangegorman as part of the separately funded GEMINI demonstration project. The government said the survey results could also be extrapolated to other parts of Ireland and help assess the full potential of geothermal energy to decarbonise heating and cooling.
Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment Darragh O'Brien said Dublin city has some of the highest heat demand in the country and is a prime location for the roll out of district heating networks.
“Geothermal district heating – using geothermal heat pumps or high temperature deep geothermal heat – represents an exciting opportunity to increase our use of renewable heat while enhancing our energy security and taking pressure off the grid," he added.
The government has published a request for tenders to find contractors for the survey, which is expected to take place in early 2027.

content:

title: Lichtblick brings 44 MWp solar park online in Germany
content:
Hamburg-based renewable energy firm LichtBlick SE has commissioned a solar park in the German city of Muehlhausen, able to produce 45 GWh of electricity annually.
The facility, consisting of 71,000 solar modules, is the largest solar park of the company, LichtBlick said. The installation covers an area of around 37 hectares and its output could meet the needs of over 13,000 households.
According to a planning document of the City of Muehlhausen, the capacity of the solar system is about 44 MWp.
The facility was developed by LichtBlick’s subsidiary Solargruen, while German solar engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company Goldbeck Solar acted as the general contractor.
LichtBlick plans to invest around EUR 600 million (USD 697.43m) in its own generation and storage capacities by 2030.

title: Northern Ireland renewables provide 50% of consumption in year to June
content:
Northern Ireland generated 4,431 GWh of electricity from renewable sources in the 12-month period from July 2025 to June 2026, accounting for 50% of gross final electricity consumption and 53% of total electricity generation, according to an official report on Thursday.
On the rolling 12-month basis, renewable generation has outstripped non-renewable generation since January 2026.
Most of the renewable power produced in Northern Ireland comes from wind. In the 12-month period through June, wind made up 74% of renewable generation. Bioenergy provided 18%, solar 6%, landfill gas 1% and hydro and tidal generation 1%.
The Northern Ireland grid is connected to the Great Britain and Ireland grids. In the past year, Northern Ireland had net imports of 578 GWh, compared to net imports of 172 GWh in the year to June 2025.
The report helps track progress towards Northern Ireland’s target of sourcing at least 80% of electricity consumption from renewables by 2030.

title: PG&E, partners to deploy VPP in California's Bay Area
content:
Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), a subsidiary of PG&E Corp (NYSE:PCG) operating in Northern and Central California, on Thursday unveiled an initiative to deploy a new Virtual Power Plant (VPP) aiming to aggregate home batteries, smart devices and battery-enabled heat pumps in Bay Area.
The programme is called SHARE (Smart Home Assets for Reliability and Efficiency) and is described as a first-of-its-kind VPP proof-of-concept. PG&E is partnering on it with Rewiring America, Google, Carrier Global Corporation, Tesla, Sunrun, Renew Home, Demand Side Analytics, encoord and more. The programme will be fully funded by Google.
The initiative will seek to enrol nearly 21,000 existing flexible energy devices. New deployments are planned in partnership with Carrier, which will be providing its battery-enabled heat pump product. Coordinating these distributed resources is expected to add a further 12 MW during periods of peak demand.
"This is about delivering power at the speed our economy demands—while improving affordability and reliability for the people we serve," said PG&E Chief Commercial Officer Chelle Izzi. "SHARE shows how investing in customers can unlock grid capacity, support growth, and bring real benefits back to communities."
PG&E and Rewiring America will start contacting eligible customers this autumn, with the scheme set to run through 2027.

title: Pacifico pledges to invest USD 1bn in S Korean offshore wind
content:
US energy infrastructure developer Pacifico Energy intends to pour over USD 1 billion (EUR 856m) into its Manho and Jindo Baram offshore wind projects in South Korean waters.
The company said on Friday it has submitted a declaration to South Korea’s Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources (MOTIR) with its commitment to investing in the two schemes.
Manho (990 MW) and Jindo Baram (1.8 GW) form part of the 3.2-GW Jindo offshore wind cluster. They will be installed off the coast of Jindo County in South Jeolla Province and will add to the capacity of the 420-MW Myeong Ryang project, which was awarded an
Electricity Business Licence
(EBL) last year and is now in the active development phase.
Last month, Manho and Jindo Baram
were selected
as the sole developers of the Jindo Offshore Wind Integrated Cluster Phase 2, a government-designated offshore wind development area totalling 2.13 GW.
As previously reported, Pacifico Energy is
exploring financing solutions
and funding strategies with Hana Bank and Hana Securities to support the further development of the Jindo offshore cluster.

title: R.Power contracts 76 MW at capacity market auction in Poland
content:
Polish developer R.Power Renewables said its battery energy storage facilities have been awarded annual contracts of a total 75.994 MW in the latest capacity market auction for delivery in 2027.
Poland's supplementary auction ended on September 3 with a closing price in the range of PLN 325.56 (USD 87/EUR 75) per kW a year to PLN 372.04/kW/year, R.Power said, citing preliminary information from grid operator PSE.
R.Power's energy storage facilities, which will fulfil the capacity obligations, have a connection capacity of 159.5 MW, the company noted, adding that the contract capacity will be adjusted by a KWD factor of 95% for standalone installations and 53.86% for mixed BESS+PV units.
The total revenues under the contracts may amount to at least PLN 24.74 million during their term. The company explained that the estimates have been made based on the preliminary auction results, while the final result will be announced 21 days after the auction.
In the country's regular capacity market auction
in December
, the R. Power group contracted 134 MW of capacity obligation for delivery year 2030.

title: South Korea to designate 25 GW of offshore wind zones by 2031
content:
South Korea plans to designate 25 GW of preliminary offshore wind zones by 2031 under a new government-led siting system aimed at accelerating project development and supporting the deployment of 45 GW of offshore wind by 2040.
The government formally launched the new planning framework at the first meeting of its Offshore Wind Power Committee this week. Under the system, authorities will identify suitable sites in advance, assess factors including wind conditions, environment, fishing activities, maritime traffic and military operations, and work with local governments to secure community acceptance before selecting developers.
The government plans to designate its first preliminary zone by the end of 2026. About 20 GW of this capacity could subsequently be offered through competitive tenders, potentially allowing offshore wind projects developed under the new system to start entering operation from 2033.
The government's roadmap lays out a cumulative deployment trajectory of 3.1 GW by 2030, 25 GW by 2035 and 45 GW by 2040.

title: Spain's renewables reach 53.6% of power generation in Aug
content:
Renewables accounted for 53.6% of Spain's electricity generation in August, while their share rose to 55.1% when estimated output from self-consumption installations was included, grid operator Red Electrica de Espana (REE) said on Thursday.
Renewable generation excluding self-consumption totalled 13,640 GWh. up 11% from a year earlier. Self-consumption systems produced around 1,600 GWh, according to REE’s estimates.
In July, the renewables share was estimated
at 54.1%, and 55.7%
when adding output from self-consumption installations.
Solar photovoltaic continued its streak as Spain’s largest source of generation for the fifth consecutive month, accounting for 29.2% of the national mix. Its output rose 27.5% year-on-year to 7,445 GWh.
Solar PV also set a new record for maximum daily generation on August 5, producing 281.2 GWh.
Combined-cycle gas-fired plants were the second-largest source at 20.7% of generation, followed by nuclear at 18.6%, wind at 13.3% and hydropower at 6.9%.
Generation from sources without CO2-equivalent emissions accounted for 72.2% of the total in August, with the volume of such generation increasing 8.2% year-on-year.
Battery storage and pumped-storage hydropower added 954 GWh to the grid during the month, helping integrate renewable generation, REE said.
National electricity demand rose 2.4% year-on-year in August after adjusting for working days and temperatures. Gross demand reached 23,137 GWh, up 3.7% from August 2025.
In the first eight months of 2026, national electricity demand totalled 175,858 GWh, up 2.8% year-on-year, or 1.7% after adjusting for working days and temperatures.
In the Balearic Islands, adjusted electricity demand rose 15.4% in August, while gross demand increased 16.4% to 850,670 MWh. Combined-cycle plants accounted for 63% of generation, followed by diesel engines at 11.3% and solar PV at 10.6%. Solar PV output increased 18%, while renewable generation rose 20.6% to a 13% share of the island mix. The submarine link between mainland Spain and Mallorca covered 23.5% of Balearic electricity demand.
In the Canary Islands, adjusted electricity demand increased 1.9% year-on-year in August, while gross demand rose 3.1% to 843,145 MWh. Combined-cycle plants supplied 35.9% of generation, followed by wind at 22.9%. Wind output reached 192.8 GWh, up 29% from a year earlier.
Renewable generation in the Canary Islands increased 21.6% year-on-year and accounted for 28.7% of total generation in August, REE said.

title: TenneT advances construction of 2-GW Dutch offshore wind platform
content:
Grid operator TenneT has erected the first major structural section of a 2-GW offshore wind platform in the Netherlands, achieving a key milestone in the project.
The platform will support the transportation of electricity from the planned 2 GW offshore wind farm
IJmuiden Ver Beta
in the Dutch North Sea.
The structural section, weighing about 1,700 tonnes, was raised into position at the Heerema Fabrication Group shipyard in Vlissingen. The section represents half of one of the two towers from which the jacket is being built. The roll-ups of the other major structural sections will follow in the coming period.
The complete foundation structure will be approximately 100 metres (328.1 feet) long, 55 metres wide and 46 metres high, and will ultimately weigh around 10,000 tonnes. A topside, currently being built in Singapore, will be installed on the jacket. It will convert the wind farm's alternating current (AC) into direct current to enable its transmission to shore.

title: Uniper gets enough off-take interest to advance H2 terminal project
content:
German energy company Uniper SE (ETR:UN0) has attracted sufficient capacity reservations from potential off-takers to advance the development of its planned hydrogen import terminal in Wilhelmshaven, Germany.
The company said it has completed the first phase of
an open season process launched in May
, during which it signed expressions of interest (EoI) with market participants. The capacity reservations allow Uniper to proceed with further development, permitting and commercialisation activities.
The next phase will include the issuance of heads of terms and the development of a terminal use agreement, the German firm noted in a statement.
The modular terminal is planned to import ammonia as a hydrogen carrier and could eventually reach an annual throughput capacity of up to 2.6 million tonnes of ammonia, equivalent to around 350,000 tonnes of hydrogen.
Uniper said that one or several additional open seasons could be launched if market demand supports an expansion of the terminal.

title: Vestas wins 108 MW of wind turbines orders for projects in Germany
content:
Danish wind turbine maker Vestas Wind Systems A/S (CPH:VWS) has received orders totalling 108 MW for two wind projects in Germany, including one for a repowering scheme from Danish renewable energy developer European Energy.
European Energy Deutschland has ordered eight Vestas V162-6.2 MW turbines, totalling 50 MW, for the Wulfshagen wind farm repowering project in Germany.
Vestas will begin deliveries in the first quarter of 2027, with commissioning scheduled to start in the fourth quarter. European Energy also signed a 20-year AOM 4000 service agreement for two of the turbines and a 20-year AOM 5000 agreement for the remaining six.
Separately, Vestas received an order for eight V172-7.2 MW turbines, totalling 58 MW, for the Ueberhaesiges Viertel wind project in Germany.
The order from Windpark Ueberhaesiges Viertel Projekt GmbH includes a 20-year AOM 5000 service agreement. Delivery for this development is scheduled to begin in the second quarter of 2027, with commissioning expected to start in the fourth quarter of 2028.

Kaleris Acquires Newport to Automate M&R Supply Chains
Prioritise Us
on Google
Kaleris has announced its acquisition of Newport Systems, a leading provider of maintenance and repair (M&R) and depot management software. Credit Getty Images
Kirk Knauff, CEO of Kaleris, says the Newport Systems acquisition will accelerate its vision to deliver automation in maintenance and repair supply chains
Kaleris has announced its acquisition of Newport Systems, a leading provider of maintenance and repair (M&R) and depot management software.
It says the acquisition will create the industry’s only end-to-end M&R platform, connecting the full asset lifecycle across marine terminals, inland depots, rail terminals, equipment owners and repair providers onto a single platform.
Kirk Knauff, CEO of Kaleris, says: “The people and the technology network Newport adds accelerates our vision to
deliver automation
and optimisation at every critical node our customers depend on.”
Kirk Knauff, President and CEO at Kaleris. Credit: Kirk Knauff via LinkedIn
Why Kaleris acquired Newport Systems
Kaleris says the combined platform will be the only solution that spans the full intermodal ecosystem and the full range of assets, including containers, chassis, reefers, gensets and railcars, under a common M&R operating model.
Newport will add key expertise in M&R operations, pre-trip inspection workflows, reefer monitoring, genset management and temperature monitoring.
Kirk says: “Kaleris runs the most complex nodes in global trade, the terminal, the yard, the depot and maintenance is where value quietly leaks out of every one of them. Newport lets us close that gap.”
According to Kaleris, its reach across the most demanding segments of the supply chain has now been strengthened through Newport’s involvement.
One key factor behind Kaleris’ decision to acquire Newport is the company’s network of proprietary carrier and equipment owner integrations.
Newport has more than 20 years of industry relationships, including 25 live EDI integrations.
Key Facts Behind the Kaleris and Newport Systems Deal
25 - Live EDI integrations Newport holds
20 - Years Newport spent building industry relationships
5 - Asset types now covered under one model
4 - Node types connected on one platform
1 - End-to-end M&R platform created
Automating maintenance and repair
According to Kaleris, maintenance and repair is one of the least automated workflows in global logistics.
“We are automating the connection between the people who own the equipment and the people who repair it, replacing manual processes with work the system can carry," says Kirk.

CEO: Kirk Knauff
Kaleris is a leading provider of supply chain execution software specialising in transportation and yard management solutions. The business develops cloud-based operational technology for ocean terminals, rail networks, industrial shipping yards and trucking fleets. The organisation plays a critical role in global freight logistics, unifying multi-modal transport workflows, optimising asset tracking, reducing supply chain friction and enhancing visibility across complex international trade and distribution networks.
Newport Systems
Headquarters: Wall Township, US
CEO: Bob Morton
Newport Systems is an intermodal logistics technology provider delivering maintenance, repair and depot management software platforms. Serving ocean carriers, equipment lessors and container depots, the enterprise streamlines asset maintenance operations through its digital management tracking systems. The business plays an essential role in global shipping infrastructure by automating equipment inspection processes, managing repair estimates, improving fleet utilisation and standardising data exchanges across international supply chain networks.

title: China further reduces tax incentives for EVs - electrive.com
content:
Politics
China is gradually phasing out tax incentives for electric cars and batteries. Since September, the previously announced consumption tax on lithium-ion batteries has been in effect, and further benefits will be removed in 2027.
Lithium-ion batteries have been subject to a two percent consumption tax in China since September.
Image: BYD
Since 1 September, lithium-ion batteries have been subject to a consumption tax of two per cent. This will rise to four per cent in September 2027. The change was
already announced in July
and ends a tax exemption that has been in place since 2015.
In contrast, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries, as well as fuel cells, will remain exempt from consumption tax until the end of 2028. China is thus partially shifting tax incentives away from the now-established lithium-ion technology towards alternative technologies.
The immediate additional costs due to the new battery tax are likely to remain limited for the time being.
CarNewsChina
calculates that for an electric car with a 60-kWh battery, the two per cent tax would result in additional battery costs of around 438 yuan, or $62 USD. With the increase to four per cent, this would rise to around 876 yuan, or $125. However, the calculation is based on prices for Chinese LFP storage cells and is therefore merely an illustrative example.
The battery tax is just part of a broader realignment of China’s incentive policy: since the beginning of 2026, electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids (grouped under the NEV designation in China) have been subject to a
purchase tax
reduction of 50 per cent instead of a full exemption. The effective tax rate is thus five per cent, with the relief capped at 15,000 yuan per vehicle.
Furthermore, additional tax benefits for vehicle and vessel taxes are set to be abolished on 1 January 2027. These include battery-electric commercial vehicles, plug-in hybrids, range extenders, and fuel cell commercial vehicles. For purely electric passenger cars, however, this tax will remain unchanged.
China is thus gradually withdrawing from tax incentives that have supported the development of its NEV market for years. However, this does not mean the end of state support. Among other things, the state continues to invest in charging and battery-swapping infrastructure. In addition, the remaining tax benefits generally also apply to electric vehicles produced in China by foreign manufacturers.

title: Vulcan advances Ludwig lithium project - electrive.com
content:
Vulcan Energy has presented a pre-feasibility study for its second lithium project in the Upper Rhine Valley. The Ludwigshafen region is expected to produce 21,100 tons of lithium carbonate annually. However, several development steps are still required before an investment decision can be made.
Vulcan is also building a lithium processing plant in Frankfurt-Höchst.
Image: Vulcan Energy
Vulcan Energy is advancing plans for a second lithium and geothermal project in the Upper Rhine Valley. The project, named Ludwig, will be located in the Ludwigshafen region and builds on the experience gained from the more advanced Lionheart project near Landau. The German-Australian company has now published a pre-feasibility study (PFS) for Ludwig.
Lionheart
, Vulcan intends to extract lithium-rich geothermal brine from underground while simultaneously harnessing its geothermal energy. For Ludwig, the brine will be transported to a central processing plant. There, Vulcan plans to first use its proprietary Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology to produce lithium chloride, which will then be further processed on-site into battery-grade lithium carbonate. In contrast, for Lionheart, lithium extraction and processing are split between Landau and Frankfurt-Höchst.
For Ludwig, the pre-feasibility study assumes an annual production of 21,100 tonnes of lithium carbonate. Additionally, up to 3,125 GWh of renewable heat per year is expected to be generated, intended for both the company’s own production processes and regional customers. Combined with the planned 24,000 tonnes of lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LHM) from Lionheart, Vulcan estimates it will produce enough lithium for the batteries of around one million electric vehicles per year. However, these figures are still purely indicative and based on the study’s projections.
Vulcan estimates investment of €1.26 billion
Vulcan currently estimates the investment required for Ludwig at €1.26 billion, approximately 15 per cent lower than for Lionheart. The company attributes the reduced investment to lessons learned from the first project and the integration of lithium extraction and processing at a single location. Operating costs are projected at €4,101 per tonne of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE). Vulcan places Ludwig in the lowest quartile of the global cost curve. However, these figures are also based on assumptions from its own pre-feasibility study and have yet to be confirmed by commercial operations.
Vulcan is significantly further along with Lionheart. For this first project, the company has secured financing of €2.2 billion and obtained construction permits for the facilities in Landau and Frankfurt-Höchst. Commercial production is scheduled to begin in 2028. Offtake agreements are in place with companies including LG Energy Solution, Umicore, Stellantis, and Glencore. In April, Vulcan also brought Siemens on board as a strategic investor and technology partner. According to the companies, the agreement will also extend to later development phases.
Ludwig, on the other hand, is still in a much earlier phase. Vulcan’s next steps include 3D seismic surveys, exploration drilling, and further technical development of the project. A final investment decision (FID) is not expected until after the successful start of production at Lionheart. The company has not yet specified a potential start date for production at Ludwig.
The project is also relevant in the context of Europe’s dependence on battery raw materials. According to a
Deloitte study
Vulcan itself is pursuing a long-term
expansion strategy in the Upper Rhine Valley
. Following the start of production at Lionheart, the company plans to develop additional projects at intervals of two to three years. Ludwig would represent the second phase of this plan. However, whether the project will actually be implemented in the form now outlined—and whether the assumed extraction volumes, investment, and operating costs will be achieved—will only become clear with further geological investigations and more detailed project planning..

title: 86 MW solar project gets 380 MWh battery boost for clean power
content: A new solar-and-storage project in West Virginia will combine 86 megawatts of solar power with 380 megawatt-hours of battery storage, giving Google’s data centers access to electricity that can be dispatched beyond daylight hours.MN8 Energy, Eos Energy Enterprises and Google are collaborating on the project at the Mammoth Solar site in Kanawha County. The system will pair conventional lithium-ion batteries with a 10 MW/100 MWh zinc-based long-duration battery from Eos.The solar plant is expected to begin commercial operation in 2028. The lithium-ion storage is scheduled to follow in 2029, while the longer-duration zinc battery is expected in 2030.The project is designed to turn intermittent solar generation into a more dependable power source. Instead of relying on solar output only when the sun is shining, the batteries can store electricity and release it later when demand rises.Solar power gets longer reachThe Eos system is particularly important because it can store electricity for 10 hours, compared with shorter-duration storage typically used to shift solar power over fewer hours. Its zinc-based chemistry is intended for long-duration applications and uses aqueous zinc technology rather than the lithium-ion chemistry used in the project’s shorter-duration batteries.The combination allows the three technologies to operate as one dispatchable resource. Solar supplies the electricity, lithium-ion batteries can respond over shorter periods, and the zinc system extends stored power further into the day.“Because Google was willing to pair next-generation storage with utility-scale solar, we could engineer proven and emerging technologies into one dispatchable resource – and deliver clean, around-the-clock power where the grid needs it most.”The project is also significant for Eos because it marks Google’s first deployment of the company’s American-made Z3 technology. It is also the first project under the previously announced supply agreement between MN8 and Eos.Batteries reshape coal countryThe project will be built on a reclaimed coal mine, giving the development an additional role in a region with a long history of fossil-fuel production.MN8 estimates that the project could represent up to $350 million in capital investment. Construction is expected to create about 200 jobs, while the project could generate roughly $4 million in property tax revenue for the county and local schools during its first 20 years of operation.The electricity will feed into the PJM grid, one of the largest electricity markets in the US. That makes the project relevant beyond Google’s own data center demand, as adding dispatchable clean capacity can help the grid handle growing electricity consumption while more renewable generation comes online.At the heart of the project is a simple idea: combine different storage technologies rather than expecting one battery type to handle every part of the power cycle.“At Google, we’re committed to backing solutions that both serve our data center capacity needs and accelerate progress toward cleaner, more affordable energy systems.”For Eos, the project also provides a commercial test of whether zinc-based long-duration storage can help renewable power serve demand across a much longer portion of the day.The Mammoth Solar project is therefore not simply another solar installation. It is a demonstration of how solar generation and multiple battery technologies can be combined into a single power resource designed to deliver electricity when it is needed.

title: Anti-aging EV battery additive can cut heat output by around 40%
content: An Oklahoma-based company is scaling production of its anti-aging battery additive. Called TENIX, the patented cathode additive is developed by Ten-Nine Technologies.Every time batteries charge and discharge, unwanted chemical by-products build up inside them.TENIX stops that aging process at the source. It’s blended directly into a battery’s cathode material during manufacturing – taking up just 0.5–2% of its weight, or roughly 0.5–2kg for every 100kg of cathode, which is about what’s in a typical EV battery pack.Battery additive supply enough to treat between 50,000, 200,000 typical EV battery packsIt drops into cathode production lines that manufacturers already run, so adopting it requires no new equipment and no battery redesign. At its current production capacity of 100 tons, Ten-Nine can supply enough TENIX to treat between 50,000 and 200,000 typical EV battery packs.“Just like people, batteries age. Products of chemical decomposition build up during use, limiting a battery’s performance and lifetime, and until now that’s just been treated as an unavoidable cost of doing business,” said Paige Johnson, Founder and CEO of Ten-Nine Technologies. “I’m a chemist so I wanted to fix that at the source rather than build a whole new battery to work around it. TENIX has a unique surface chemistry that disrupts that aging process, giving batteries more power and significantly longer life. I started this company in the back of a warehouse in Tulsa with $100,000 and four grams of material in a flask. I never imagined we’d end up here, but I always believed that if the chemistry was right, it would matter to a lot of people’s lives. That’s still what gets me up in the morning.”Battery additive delivered over 75% more charge-discharge cycles In third-party testing, TENIX delivered over 75% more charge-discharge cycles, extending a typical EV battery’s life from a 150,000-mile warranty baseline to more than 265,000 miles. That longer life translates into roughly 40% lower cost per kilowatt-hour delivered over a battery’s lifetime, while 10% lower internal resistance means faster charging and less energy wasted as heat, according to a press release.TENIX can also cut a battery’s heat output by around 40% over its lifetime – a benefit that is becoming increasingly critical as AI-driven data centers push backup batteries harder than ever. This momentum comes as the battery industry is increasingly shifting toward manganese-rich cathodes – a cheaper, more abundant, and more geographically secure alternative to the cobalt- and nickel-heavy chemistries that dominate EV batteries today, as per the release.Ten-Nine Technologies also revealed that the manganese-rich cathodes also offer a far more secure supply chain than the nickel- and cobalt-heavy chemistries they could replace. Manganese is mined widely across Africa, South America, and Southeast Asia, rather than concentrated in a handful of countries, making it far less exposed to the geopolitical pressure points that increasingly worry battery manufacturers and policymakers alike.Manganese-rich cathodes have also long been held back by poor cycle life, exactly the problem TENIX is built to solve. Ten-Nine believes the shift could reshape the global cathode supply chain the way LFP did twenty years ago.

title: China’s quantum router breakthrough hits 98% transmission efficiency
content: A quantum router tested on China’s Origin Wukong superconducting quantum computer has achieved information transmission efficiency of up to 98 percent, offering researchers a route toward building more scalable quantum memory systems.Several Chinese research teams developed and tested the coherent routing system for bucket-brigade quantum random access memory, or QRAM, Science and Technology Daily reported on Wednesday. Their experiments used three independent quantum routers and a two-layer network to examine how the approach performs on existing hardware.The work addresses a key challenge in expanding QRAM: routing quantum information through a system as its architecture becomes more complex.Researchers said the results could support scalable memory development while improving the integration of quantum chips and circuit design.Routing quantum informationThe teams carried out their experiments on Origin Wukong, China’s third-generation, independently developed superconducting quantum computer. Rather than testing only an isolated component, they built individual routers and a network linking routing functions across two layers. The coherent routing system acts as a “fast lane” for data transmission, according to the report. Its development is aimed at bucket-brigade QRAM, with the researchers exploring how such routing can be implemented using superconducting computing hardware.Building three independent routers allowed the teams to test the individual routing units. The two-layer arrangement then provided a way to examine transmission through a more complex network.That distinction matters when assessing the findings. Strong performance from a single router establishes one part of the picture, while the network tests show how the system performs when additional routing stages are involved.Transmission and fidelity resultsThe single quantum router achieved information transmission efficiency of up to 98%. Across the two-layer routing network, overall transmission efficiency reached 93%.The teams also conducted random-access tests, reporting average fidelity of 94.8% for the single router and 82.4% for the two-layer network. These are separate measurements from transmission efficiency. The 98% figure describes the reported transmission performance of an individual router; it does not represent the fidelity of the full network or the performance of the computer as a whole.Both sets of results were lower for the two-layer network than for the individual router. The experiments demonstrated routing at two levels of complexity on the same superconducting computing platform.A path toward scalable memoryResearchers said the breakthrough offers a new approach to building scalable QRAM on existing superconducting hardware. The results provide a basis for pursuing that approach beyond individual routing components.According to the report, the work also reflects a shift in China’s quantum computing research toward testing more complex quantum functions on real machines, alongside efforts to improve individual performance metrics.The researchers identified potential benefits including lower computing costs, greater efficiency and closer integration between quantum chips and circuit design. Those possibilities extend beyond the transmission and fidelity measurements reported in the tests. For now, the demonstrated achievement is a coherent quantum routing system tested through individual routers and a two-layer network on Origin Wukong.

title: Chinese firm releases 11,430 robot trajectories furthering research
content: Chinese robotics player AGIBOT has open-sourced its WORLD 2026 dataset, which focuses on reinforcement learning for embodied AI.The dataset is designed to help robots learn from real-world interactions rather than relying solely on successful expert demonstrations. It captures the broader learning process, including how robots improve through failures and human intervention.Recently, AGIBOT topped the second World Humanoid Robot Games with 46 medals, including 18 golds, making its international competition debut.Real-world robot datasetAGIBOT’s WORLD 2026 Theme 3 dataset initiative provides researchers with real-world robot experience data aimed at advancing reinforcement learning and embodied AI.The open-source dataset contains 11,430 real-world trajectories collected across 14 industrial and household tasks. Unlike datasets focused primarily on successful demonstrations, the new release captures a wider range of robot experiences, including successful executions, failed attempts, autonomous deployments, and interventions by human operators.The dataset is organized around three types of trajectories. The first consists of expert demonstrations, which document reference task executions carried out by human operators in real-world environments. These demonstrations provide robots with examples of how tasks can be performed and serve as a foundation for learning.The second category covers autonomous policy rollouts. These records capture robots attempting tasks independently after deploying learned policies. Both successful and unsuccessful attempts are included, allowing researchers to examine not only what a robot can accomplish but also where and why its performance breaks down. The dataset includes 1,024 successful policy rollouts and 1,369 failed rollouts.The third category focuses on human-in-the-loop corrections. These trajectories document a robot’s behavior before an intervention, the moment a human operator takes control, and the corrective actions used to recover or complete the task. This provides researchers with data on how robots respond when autonomous behavior goes wrong and how human guidance can help overcome failures.AI learns failureAGIBOT has also included detailed annotations covering task progress, completion status, errors, environmental disturbances, and human interventions. Such information is intended to give researchers a more structured view of robot behavior and provide useful signals for reinforcement learning and other embodied AI applications.The release reflects a broader shift in robot learning from relying primarily on curated demonstrations toward learning from actual deployment experience. In real-world environments, robots can encounter unexpected obstacles, make mistakes, deviate from intended actions, or require assistance. Capturing these situations can help researchers study capability limits, failure modes, and recovery strategies that successful demonstrations alone may not reveal.Theme 3 forms part of the broader AGIBOT WORLD 2026 initiative, which is being developed as an open-source resource for embodied AI research. The company plans to expand the initiative with additional datasets, benchmarks, and research resources. According to the firm, by making real-world successes, failures, and corrective interactions available to researchers, it aims to provide a broader foundation for developing robots capable of learning continuously from their own experiences and operating more reliably in everyday environments.“We invite researchers worldwide to leverage AGIBOT WORLD 2026 to drive robotic intelligence from the lab into the real world, empowering every industry and tangibly boosting production and service efficiency,” reads the AGIBOT WORLD website.

title: Critical lithium component production for US nuclear stockpile shifts to modular design
content: Engineers are designing a modular production unit to replace decades-old infrastructure used for lithium manufacturing in Tennessee. The National Nuclear Security Administration, an agency within the US Department of Energy, selected BWX Technologies to draft the engineering plans for the Y-12 National Security Complex. The US nuclear weapons stockpile depends on precision-machined lithium parts. However, the systems that handle them have run well past their designed service life. To keep the stockpile functional, technical teams must extract, purify, machine, and recycle this material without interruption. “This project represents an important investment in modernizing the nation’s nuclear security infrastructure and ensuring NNSA has the capabilities needed to support its mission well into the future,” said Heatherly Dukes, president of BWXT’s Technical Services Group. Handling lithium is challenging Handling lithium introduces severe engineering hurdles. The element reacts violently with moisture, corrodes rapidly in normal air, and poses an immediate fire hazard if exposed to humidity. Also, cutting and shaping it is hard because pure lithium is a soft metal. The planned Machining and Inspection Module will isolate these processes inside tightly controlled inert atmospheres. Inside the unit, computer-controlled tools must shape parts to microscopic tolerances while preventing any ambient air from entering the work envelope. Once parts are cut, technicians will use non-destructive sensors to inspect their internal density and geometry without touching the sensitive surfaces. Building this work into a self-contained module also keeps mechanical dust separate from the chemical recovery lines elsewhere on site. Under the current four-month arrangement, BWXT has received four million dollars to develop the initial designs. Another competing contractor has also received funds to submit an alternative plan. Once agency evaluators finish reviewing both designs at the end of the second phase, they will select one winner to negotiate the final construction deal. BWXT has assembled a technical team for the bid, including Edgewater Technical Associates, Evans General Contractors, Process Engineering Associates, and Merrick & Company. Running alongside another military assignment The project runs alongside another major military nuclear assignment awarded to the firm earlier this year. In August, the company won an award under the Janus program, an initiative set up by the US Army and the Defense Innovation Unit in October 2025. Janus aims to deploy transportable, resilient nuclear reactors to power critical military sites off the commercial grid. BWXT is supplying its Advanced Nuclear Reactor design for that project. The system uses high-temperature gas to deliver heat and electricity. Crucially, the reactor core runs on TRISO particle fuel, which packs uranium inside four concentric isotropic layers of carbon and silicon carbide. These microscopic ceramic coatings act as individual containment structures that withstand extreme temperatures without melting, eliminating the need for complex, active emergency coolant pumps. For the Janus contract, the company is currently determining a viable operating location at Fort Campbell, clearing safety regulations with the Army, and preparing to manufacture the ceramic fuel particles at its commercial plants.

title: Drilling hits 10,350 feet in 15 days at Oregon geothermal site
content: Drilling miles into the Earth to tap energy hot enough to melt lead usually breaks equipment before it breaks records. Texas-based Mazama Energy has announced a drilling performance milestone at its Athena geothermal well in Newberry, Oregon. It is a key step toward commercializing superhot rock geothermal energy.The energy company said its latest geothermal well, Athena, reached a depth of 10,350 feet in a swift 15 days. Interestingly, it is roughly an 80 percent reduction in drilling time compared to a landmark well drilled at the same site just last year. The development will help move the clean energy sector a step closer to tapping “superhot rock.” These subsurface formations are hotter than 750°F (399°C) and hold enough energy to transform green grid economics. “Our goal was to demonstrate that we could drill faster and be cost-effective as we move toward increasingly hotter and deeper conditions,” said Pat Brand, Project Athena Director and Mazama’s Drilling SME. “We still have work ahead as we drill toward 750+°F temperatures, but the performance we are already seeing gives us confidence.”Faster, deeper, hotterFar from just surviving the harsh conditions, the drill bit achieved remarkable speeds. Athena logged peak penetration rates exceeding 350 feet per hour and sustained over 130 feet per hour through long intervals.A single drill bit churned through 3,578 feet of solid rock without a single downhole motor or directional tool failure. The job isn’t finished. Crews are now pushing Athena deeper, targeting a final depth of 15,500 feet. The aim is to tap into superhot geothermal resources with temperatures exceeding 750°F (399°C).Exceptional equipment reliability drove the effort, yielding zero downhole motor or directional system failures and enabling a single 3,578-foot bit run to operate uninterrupted until reaching its planned casing point.The technical rewards are massive. Superhot fluids carry vastly more energy than standard geothermal steam, producing up to ten times more power per well. The Newberry field alone holds an estimated thermally recoverable capacity exceeding 10 gigawatts of electricity. That could mean reliable, 24/7 carbon-free power.More energy stored in deep rocks Going above 700°F (371.1°C) is transformative because, under intense subsurface pressure, water enters a supercritical state — behaving as a high-density hybrid between a liquid and a gas. In this state, the fluid gains extraordinary heat capacity and flow properties, carrying more thermal energy to the surface with minimal flow resistance. As a result, a single supercritical well can produce 5 to 10 times more electricity than a conventional geothermal well. According to Mazama Energy CEO Sriram Vasantharajan, early development costs for the Newberry project are expected to be between $4,500 and $4,950 per kilowatt. As the technology matures, costs could fall to $3,200 per kilowatt. At that price point, superhot geothermal directly challenges the economics of natural gasThe success of Athena will lay the groundwork for Project Ceres, backed by the U.S. Department of Energy. Scheduled for late 2026, Ceres will drill the world’s first commercial-scale superhot horizontal wells, bringing subterranean power one step closer to the grid.Mazama Energy’s demonstrated superhot rock platform optimizes well construction, drilling, and stimulation to boost power capacity while minimizing water use, land footprint, and well counts.

title: Hermeus and Anduril team up to boot supersonic aircraft autonomy
content: Hermeus has selected Anduril to integrate its mission autonomy technology with the Quarterhorse Mk 2, bringing autonomous and collaborative flight capabilities to the company’s high-Mach aircraft program.Under the agreement, Anduril will integrate its Lattice for Mission Autonomy software with Quarterhorse Mk 2. The system is intended to allow multiple aircraft to collaborate on missions while giving human operators a common interface to interact with the aircraft throughout the mission.High-Mach flight meets autonomous aircraftAccording to Hermeus, the partnership will combine two rapidly developing areas of military aviation. High-speed flight and mission autonomy. Lattice for Mission Autonomy is designed to provide an end-to-end software environment through which operators can interact with autonomous systems. Hermeus says it covers activities including operational analysis, threat modeling, training, mission planning, execution, and post-mission debriefing. Operators will use Anduril’s Menace-T C4 system as the physical interface for interacting with the aircraft. Hermeus says the interface is intended to help operators work with autonomous aircraft throughout the mission rather than treating autonomy as a capability that operates separately from human control.The companies are already integrating the systems, with the first mission-autonomy flight on Quarterhorse Mk 2 planned for 2027. The agreement is also notable for Anduril. Hermeus says it is the first commercial agreement in which Anduril will integrate its mission-autonomy solution with a third-party Group 5 aircraft. It will give the company an opportunity to demonstrate its autonomy software on an aircraft operating at high Mach speeds.Quarterhorse is moving rapidly toward flight testingHermeus has been developing Quarterhorse as part of its effort to rapidly design, build, and test high-Mach and hypersonic aircraft. The company says it flew its first aircraft in 2025 and reached supersonic speeds with the Mk 2.1 aircraft 364 days later. The program has also recently demonstrated the ability to deploy a payload, while the next aircraft, Mk 2.2, was built in less than a year.The Quarterhorse Mk 2 aircraft are being developed as test platforms for technologies relevant to future high-speed flight. Adding mission autonomy gives Hermeus another capability to evaluate as the aircraft program progresses.The companies say the eventual objective is not simply to make an individual aircraft autonomous, but to enable coordinated, collaborative missions involving multiple aircraft. That could change how high-speed aircraft are employed. Instead of relying entirely on a pilot to control each aircraft and manage every action, autonomous systems could potentially coordinate aspects of a mission while human operators retain oversight and control.Building an autonomous aircraft ecosystemThe Hermeus partnership also connects Quarterhorse to a wider effort to establish common technologies for autonomous military aircraft. Anduril’s Lattice autonomy technology is already being used in the U.S. Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program, according to Hermeus. The company says the Air Force’s Autonomy Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA) is intended to promote compatibility between autonomy software and aircraft hardware. Hermeus argues that this modular approach can help create a broader ecosystem in which autonomy technologies can be transferred between different aircraft rather than being developed separately for every platform.For Quarterhorse, that means the aircraft’s high-speed capabilities could eventually be combined with an autonomy system already designed around collaborative robotic flight.The first autonomous Quarterhorse mission is still planned for 2027, so the combined system has yet to demonstrate this capability in flight. But the integration marks a significant step for Hermeus as it moves from demonstrating high-speed flight toward testing how autonomous aircraft could operate at those speeds.This effort could offer a glimpse of a future in which speed and autonomy are developed together rather than as separate capabilities, allowing high-Mach aircraft to become participants in larger coordinated missions.

title: High-energy fuel passes first rotating detonation rocket engine test
content: CycloKinetics is testing its alternative rocket fuel with Venus Aerospace in a rotating detonation rocket engine (RDRE). The program will examine whether CycloRP can replace conventional RP-1 and RP-2 propellants.CycloRP aims to work with existing engines without requiring hardware modifications. CycloKinetics designed the fuel for higher energy density and cleaner combustion.The testing has support from the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory and the Department of War’s Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering. Results from the program could offer a closer look at how alternative propellants perform inside advanced rocket hardware.RDRE puts fuel to testThe first testing phase concluded in July 2026. Engineers evaluated how CycloRP behaved during combustion inside Venus Aerospace’s RDRE.The tests confirmed that CycloRP could successfully detonate inside the engine. That result is important because an RDRE uses controlled detonation waves instead of conventional combustion.The approach could improve propulsion efficiency by extracting more useful energy from the combustion process. It also creates demanding conditions for any fuel entering the combustion chamber.CycloRP therefore has to perform reliably under extreme pressure and temperature conditions. Successful detonation provides an early indication that the fuel can operate within the unusual environment created by an RDRE.Sassie Duggleby, co-founder and CEO of Venus Aerospace, said efficient fuel remains an important part of advancing the company’s propulsion technology. She also pointed to the testing as an opportunity for the Air Force and CycloKinetics to evaluate the fuel against established propellants.Venus has previously described its RDRE as flight-proven, giving CycloRP a test platform tied to an emerging propulsion architecture rather than a conventional laboratory setup.Cooling brings another challengeThe second phase will examine CycloRP’s cooling performance. Rocket engines produce enormous amounts of heat, making thermal management a major engineering challenge.Engineers can circulate fuel through engine components before combustion. The fuel absorbs heat during that process, helping control temperatures before reaching the combustion chamber.CycloKinetics and Venus will compare CycloRP with RP-1 and RP-2 during this part of the program. The results should show whether CycloRP can provide comparable cooling performance while serving as the engine’s primary propellant.That test could prove just as important as combustion performance. A drop-in fuel must meet multiple requirements if operators want to use it without redesigning existing propulsion systems.The two companies previously conducted testing together at Venus Aerospace’s Houston facility in June 2025. The current program expands that relationship with additional combustion and thermal evaluations.Mukund Karanjikar, CEO and founder of CycloKinetics, said the company designed CycloRP as a direct replacement for conventional rocket propellants. He also highlighted domestic production as a potential advantage for future U.S. propulsion programs.A fuel that fits existing engine architectures could reduce the engineering work required to introduce a new propellant. It could also give propulsion developers another option as they explore higher-performance engine designs.The companies expect the combined testing to produce a fuller technical assessment in early 2027. CycloKinetics and Venus Aerospace plan to share additional results after the final testing concludes.

title: Is GPT-6 Astra AGI? OpenAI unveils 'world's most intelligent' model
content: An interesting turn of events took place Thursday morning, with major artificial intelligence companies reportedly experiencing service disruptions, according to Downdetector.OpenAI, Claude, Grok, Copilot and Cursor were among the services that saw disruption reports. Their respective status pages also showed issues during the day.Gemini users reported similar problems, although Google did not confirm an outage. Microsoft’s Azure cloud platform also recorded a spike in reported problems.The timing created an interesting wrinkle. Several major AI services appeared to stumble on the same day OpenAI began deploying its newest model, GPT-6 Astra.That coincidence quickly fueled speculation online. Some users wondered whether Astra’s deployment had somehow contributed to the disruptions across the broader AI ecosystem.Conspiracy theories remain conspiracies for a reason. There is currently no evidence connecting Astra to the outages. The simultaneous disruptions could stem from entirely unrelated infrastructure problems.The more interesting question sits elsewhere. OpenAI says Astra can handle tasks that increasingly resemble the capabilities associated with artificial general intelligence, or AGI.Perfect cybersecurity scoreGPT-6 Astra arrives with an unusually strong collection of benchmark results. One figure stands out immediately: a 100% score on ExploitBench, a benchmark focused on cybersecurity capabilities.A perfect score does not automatically prove that a system has achieved AGI. Benchmarks measure defined tasks, not intelligence as a single universal property.The result still matters because cybersecurity demands several forms of technical reasoning. A capable system must understand software, identify weaknesses, and reason about how systems behave under attack.This is GPT-6 Astra.Anything you can do on a computer, Astra can do for you. Fast. pic.twitter.com/gDd0IsewJw— OpenAI (@OpenAI) September 3, 2026Astra also reportedly scored 98% on FrontierMath Tier 4. OpenAI says the model has already contributed to solving difficult, long-standing mathematical problems.The model reportedly reached 99.9% on ARC-AGI-3 as well. That benchmark targets increasingly difficult forms of abstract reasoning. Taken together, those results create a broader question about what comes next.Is Astra edging toward AGI?OpenAI has not simply built Astra around one narrow capability. The company says the model can perform advanced software engineering, computer use, browsing, and scientific work.That combination makes the AGI debate harder to dismiss as a distant thought experiment. A system that performs strongly across unrelated technical domains looks very different from an AI optimized for one task.Still, benchmark saturation has limits. A perfect score can show that a model has mastered the tested environment. It cannot establish that the system possesses human-like general intelligence.That distinction becomes important as benchmarks approach their ceilings. Once a model reaches near-perfect performance, researchers need harder tests to separate genuine generalization from increasingly sophisticated task optimization.Astra could therefore represent something more interesting than another generational model upgrade. Its benchmark results may offer an early glimpse of where current AI systems begin running into the boundaries of conventional testing.OpenAI’s rollout will put those claims under greater scrutiny. As more users test Astra across real-world tasks, its performance outside controlled benchmarks will matter just as much.If this is not AGI, then what exactly is it?

title: L3Harris delivers first 35 Viper EW systems for the F-16 fleet
content: L3Harris Technologies has completed production of the first 35 Viper Shield electronic warfare systems for the global F-16 fleet, as the company ramps up manufacturing of a system designed to detect and counter modern electronic threats.Viper Shield is an all-digital electronic warfare and countermeasure system that L3Harris describes as “digital armor” for the F-16. The system can be installed inside the aircraft or carried as an external pod, allowing it to be integrated across different F-16 configurations.New electronic warfare system prepares for wider F-16 rolloutL3Harris currently has orders for 233 Viper Shield systems from eight allied nations and is preparing to move toward full-rate production. The company says it has also assembled the first production pod using production hardware.The milestone follows a series of flight tests designed to demonstrate how the system performs in realistic conditions. In August, F-16C and F-16D aircraft flew together with Viper Shield hardware for the first time at Edwards Air Force Base. The testing evaluated the system’s ability to detect, identify, and counter electromagnetic threats while operating alongside the aircraft’s existing avionics.Viper Shield first flew on a single-seat Block 70 F-16 in 2025; the initial flight also tested compatibility with the aircraft’s APG-83 Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radar and mission systems.Electronic warfare is increasingly important for fighter aircraft operating against modern air defenses. Radar and other electromagnetic signals can reveal an aircraft’s presence, track it, or support the guidance of weapons toward it. An electronic warfare system can monitor those signals, identify potential threats, and use countermeasures to interfere with an adversary’s ability to detect or engage the aircraft. L3Harris has not disclosed sensitive performance details such as Viper Shield’s detection range, jamming power, or specific threat libraries.Software-defined design is keyOne of Viper Shield’s defining features is its software-defined architecture. L3Harris says the system uses commercial off-the-shelf technology to reduce size and weight while making future upgrades easier.Electronic warfare is a constantly changing contest, and adversaries can introduce new radar modes, frequencies, and techniques, requiring defensive systems to adapt without necessarily replacing their underlying hardware.The system is designed for the F-16 Block 70/72 and is fully interoperable with the APG-83 AESA radar. It can also be integrated with previous F-16 blocks, giving operators a potential upgrade path for aircraft already in service.L3Harris has also demonstrated multiple installation options, including internal integration and an external pod. This flexibility is particularly relevant for older F-16 variants that may not have the same internal space or configuration as newly built Block 70/72 aircraft.Eight nations have selected Viper ShieldThe international expansion of the system has accelerated during 2026. Peru became the eighth country to select Viper Shield in August for its F-16 Block 70 program. L3Harris says the system is now supported by an active production line and supply chain serving the eight customers.The company says those countries have collectively invested about $1 billion in Viper Shield, covering development, laboratory and flight testing, and current production. L3Harris has suggested that the U.S. Air Force and Air National Guard could potentially benefit from that investment by joining a program whose development costs have already been shared internationally.F-16 continues to receive upgrades decades after entering service, and modern electronic warfare can be as important as improvements to radar, weapons, and computing. With the first 35 systems now completed and 233 ordered, Viper Shield is moving further into production. The combination of digital threat detection, countermeasures, flexible installation, and software-based upgrades is intended to help keep F-16s capable of operating in increasingly contested electromagnetic environments.

title: Major engine repair facility expands 40% to support Boeing 737s, A320s
content: StandardAero has added 70,000 square feet to its Winnipeg operations, expanding the facility’s footprint by about 40%. The new space increases the company’s capacity for maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) work. It will support the CF34 and CFM56 turbofan families used across commercial and military aviation.Manitoba contributed $3 million toward the expansion. The provincial government says the investment will strengthen aerospace capacity and support skilled employment in the province.Expanded aircraft engine maintenanceThe expanded facility will provide full MRO support for GE Aerospace’s CF34-3/8 engines. It will also support CFM International’s CFM56 family. Those engines remain deeply embedded across the North American aircraft fleet. The CF34-8 powers Embraer E170 and E175 aircraft. It also flies on the MHIRJ CRJ700 and CRJ900 regional jets.The CF34-3 serves the CRJ200 and Bombardier Challenger 600 and 850 families. Meanwhile, the CFM56 powers Boeing 737 Next Generation and Airbus A320ceo aircraft. Its military applications extend further. The P-8A Poseidon uses a military derivative of the CFM56 for maritime patrol missions.That range of platforms makes engine MRO capacity particularly important. Operators can keep established aircraft flying without relying solely on new production engines.StandardAero Vice President and General Manager Peter Wheatley said demand for CF34 and CFM56 support continues to increase. “We believe that this expansion will ensure that we can meet our customers’ evolving needs for years to come,” Wheatley said.He pointed to the facility’s equipment, workforce and established processes as key elements. Long-term customer commitments also give the expanded operation a substantial workload base.$3 million backs expansionManitoba’s provincial contribution connects the project to a broader effort to grow the region’s aerospace industry.Business, Mining, Trade and Job Creation Minister Jamie Moses said the completed facility will increase industrial capacity while creating good jobs.StandardAero already employs about 1,500 skilled workers across eight Winnipeg facilities. Those operations serve commercial, military and business aviation customers around the world.The company’s relationship with Winnipeg also predates modern commercial aviation. StandardAero has maintained a presence in the city for 115 years.That history figured prominently in comments from Chairman and CEO Russell Ford during the opening. “Opening this facility in the city where our company was founded underscores both our deep roots in Winnipeg and our confidence in the future,” Ford said. He added that the investment will reinforce Winnipeg’s role within StandardAero’s global network.Winnipeg expands MRO capacityThe expansion gives the Winnipeg operation more room to support engines that have accumulated decades of operational experience.That matters for aircraft operators focused on fleet availability. Mature engine programs can generate substantial maintenance demand long after manufacturers stop producing the original aircraft.The additional 70,000 square feet therefore represents more than a larger facility. It gives StandardAero additional physical capacity for inspection, repair, and overhaul work across several major aircraft programs.The investment also strengthens Winnipeg’s position in a specialized part of the aerospace supply chain. Skilled technicians, engineering expertise, and dedicated MRO infrastructure are difficult capabilities to build quickly.With the expansion complete, StandardAero can handle more of that work from a city that has supported its operations for more than a century.

title: Molecular 'raincoat' helps tin solar cells reach 16.2% efficiency rate
content: Clean energy can finally afford to be fully clean. Scientists have created a tin-based perovskite material equipped with a built-in defense against air and moisture, functioning much like a molecular raincoat for solar cells.The advance is the result of a joint effort led by the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the National Laboratory of the Rockies, and partner institutions. Interestingly, this tin perovskites could become a promising eco-friendly alternative to hazardous lead-based cells. However, the previous iterations of tin-based materials typically degrade rapidly when exposed to air and water. This new “raincoat” solves this issue.The collaborative team revealed a molecular redesign that gives tin-based solar cells built-in protection against these elements. It tackles the single largest obstacle preventing non-toxic perovskite photovoltaics from hitting the commercial market: durability.“We wanted to find a way to protect these materials while preserving the properties that make them attractive for solar cells,” said Song Jin, a UW–Madison professor of Chemistry. Built-in protectionWith solar panels covering millions of acres, the risk of toxic leaks from damaged or discarded panels remains the biggest roadblock keeping lead-based cells off the market.Tin perovskites possess superior light-absorbing and electronic properties, but degrade in a short time when exposed to air and moisture. Rather than adding a bulky physical layer over the solar cells, the team designed protection straight into the material’s microscopic structure. It all came down to atomic fine-tuning.Song Jin and his team experimented with different halogen atoms (fluorine, chlorine, and bromine) to alter the material’s organic components. This study engineered a mixed-dimensional (2D/3D) heterostructure.Interestingly, when the chlorinated version was introduced, something remarkable happened: the perovskite crystals packed together far more tightly than before.That tight atomic packing acts as a molecular shield. Water and oxygen can’t squeeze inside, creating a protective barrier that keeps them out of the cells.This structural shift improved both performance and durability. Compared to conventional materials, the new chlorinated tin perovskite maintained its integrity for months in open air. It even survived days fully submerged in water without dissolving.Further, theoretical models confirmed the mechanism: the tight molecular structure physically blocks oxygen and water from seeping into the vulnerable tin core.Operational heat testingTo test its practical viability, the team built working solar cells in partnership with researchers Lei Chen and Kai Zhu at the National Laboratory of the Rockies.The devices achieved a 16.2 percent power-conversion efficiency, which makes them among the most efficient tin-based cells ever created.After 1,600 hours sitting in dry air, the cells retained over 95 percent of their initial output. Under severe operational stress with continuous simulated sunlight at a blistering 55°C (131°F), the cells held onto 80 percent of their power after 1,000 hours.Mostly, solar design meant choosing efficiency or durability. This material shows that companies don’t have to compromise.“What is exciting is that a relatively small change in the material’s design produces such a large improvement in stability,” said Christopher T. Triggs, who recently received his doctorate in materials chemistry at UW–Madison. “It shows how designing the organic components and controlling the way perovskite structures pack together can provide powerful protection of the resulting perovskite materials from the surrounding environment,” the first author added. Recognizing the commercial potential of a lead-free, long-lasting solar cell, the Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation and the National Laboratory of the Rockies have jointly filed a patent for the technology. The study was published in the journal Nature Materials.
